set with `Set`, `symbol_variants`, `fallbacks`) is replaced whole, an empty one included; `Append` adds paint layers over `base` (R6), and
over a paint that resolves `Absent` appends to nothing, the paint staying absent, as a patch that states no presence
never draws again what is absent (S6.3, ledger queue #110): outside a keyframe only a `Set` draws an absent paint again,
a keyframe's patch of it, a `Set` included, being `None` (S2.7); so a preset whose state rules would append over a rest
paint that resolves `Absent` states that rest drawn instead, as the platform states it (GTK's initial
`background-color`, transparent, `gtk@4.24.1 gtk/gtkcssstylepropertyimpl.c:902-907`; adwaita's list rows, GN-1.158),
or sets each state's paint whole; over a reference it composes lazily, as a `Fields` patch
does, and neither is a merge conflict there, the merge keeping it on the reference with its position (S2.2, ADD-A122); `Append` in a layer's bases is an error, as `base` is, outside a keyframe's patch (S2.7). The merge conflict is one: a map entry created over a value with a field unset that may not be `Absent` (above), as a `Fields` patch meeting an `Absent` value directly leaves it absent (S2.2, ADD-A126), an `Append` meeting one appends to nothing (above), and no block is `Auto` (S6.3); it is refused when the layer is added (S12), so resolution never meets it (S8). A keyframe's patch is not applied by the merge: resolution applies it over its
part's resolved style, and over a field that resolves `Absent` it is `None` in that query (S2.7; ADD-A125).

**S6.2** Inheritance code goes: `inherit_from`, `theme_inherit`, the `[uniform]`, `[per_platform]` and
`[wrong_safety_nets]` registries and `resolve/inheritance.rs` are removed (R20). Their rules are converted once
into the presets' bases as expressions (S19.2).

**S6.3** `Absent` is allowed from two sources: a block's sub-field this document marks "may be absent" (S2),
wherever that block appears (two marks hold in one place only: `IconStyle`'s fields in an icon-size context, S4.5,
and `TextStyle`'s drawn-text leaves in a keyed text style and a slot, S2.8);
and the catalogue's tables, for colour roles, tokens and, per (widget, part, field
path), at three levels: a
field of a part (`button.body.shadow`), a whole part (`slider.ticks`: some platform draws no ticks), and a whole
widget (a preset declares it `available = false`, S10). A whole part is made absent by a base or a rule
(`PartPresence::Absent`, TOML `absent = true`), so it may be absent under a condition only (a title bar in full
screen); the query then answers `NotDrawn`. An unavailable widget and an absent part need no fields. A compound widget value listed `may_be_absent` (a `Placement`, a record of `Value`s) allows each of its `Value`
members to be absent, and, where it is a `Value` itself (`Value<Placement>`), to be absent as a whole (a desktop that
avoids no keyboard). A widget's root
part is never absent as a whole and is never a repeated element (the catalogue gives such widgets a container root);
its fields may be. `may_be_absent` is about what a platform draws, never about an element's content: a part the
element's content lacks (a dialog given no icon, an icon-only tab's label) is simply not queried by the connector,
and the catalogue does not list it. So no fact states such a part absent where a content variant leaves it no content
(a button's `label` under `icon_only`), and its field facts name that content variant in neither `variants` nor
`not_variants`: they state its look where it is drawn and hold there as in the same combination without the
variant, so nothing there is pending or measured (no platform draws it); the gate compares them there as anywhere,
values no connector queries (ADD-A135). `adwaita`'s facts state its icon-only button's label so (no
`button.label` fact, none of its label facts naming `icon_only`), and the iOS facts follow (ADD-A135's follow-ups). Rejected: the part absent under the content variant (it is the content's, and the
catalogue lists no such absence); a catalogue map of the parts each content variant empties, with the gate skipping
their fields there (machinery for values no connector reads); facts pending there (a measurement of nothing drawn).
A part's presence is decided by the last of its patches that states one
(`PartPatch.presence`): `Absent`, `DrawnAs`, or `Present` (TOML `absent = false` in its table: drawn with its own
style); a patch that states none sets fields only and never brings an absent or redrawn part back,
so no later rule or layer patching a field (an application's colour `@ {hover}`) restores a part a condition made
absent (the title bar in full screen, GN-P3-5†; WinUI's combo-box selection pill outside the selected item,
W1-135), and a rule or a layer that draws a part a broader patch made absent states `absent = false` (an
application drawing a part its preset hides, whose selectors it cannot restate; GtkInfoBar's edge line under
`@info_bar`, GN-2.31); the fields any patch states, before, beside (S11) or after an `Absent` or `DrawnAs`, are kept beneath it
(ADD-A131). A block field follows
the same rule (S2.2): a `Fields` patch over a block that resolves `Absent` leaves it absent, and outside a keyframe,
whose patch of it is `None`, a `Set`'s included (S2.7), only a `Set` draws it again (the
menu's check glyph outside its checked states; Breeze's tab focus line in the base, K1.129); so does a paint, an
`Append` over a paint that resolves `Absent` appending to nothing (S6.1) (ADD-A123, ADD-A126;
ledger queue #110). A part that resolves `Absent` (the query's `NotDrawn`) is not laid out: the connector gives it no
box and lays its siblings out without it, as a part hidden by `shown` keeps its box (S2.7). The parts nested in it
are still queried and laid out in its parent's place (the catalogue's Nesting), so a part removed with its content
states the content absent under the same selector (a title bar in full screen with its title and caption buttons,
GN-P3-5†; a full-screen bar a trigger reveals is drawn while revealed and not absent, the catalogue's
`full_screen_title_bar_reveal`, W-P3-2†, ADD-A146). Rejected (#110): `shown` on
every part a condition can hide (a field every such part would state, and a layout that an absent part leaves and a
hidden one keeps, so a title bar in full screen still needs `Absent`); an S12 refusal of a later rule over a part's
conditional absence (it refuses an application's ordinary `@ {hover}` rule instead of keeping the part absent); a
`Style` patch bringing the part back as before (ADD-A123's rule, under which every later layer's field rule draws the
part again). Likewise `Auto` is allowed only on the length fields the catalogue marks `auto` (sizes, widths, heights,
gaps), per part, and on the core's own marks: `TextStyle.line_height`, `PartStyle.min_width` and `min_height` ("no minimum
beyond the content") and `max_width` and `max_height` ("no maximum") on every part (S2.11); their resolved types are S6.1's.

**May be absent, in the core's blocks** (the first source; wherever the block appears unless a mark names its place,
because some platform has no
counterpart, R6, R20): every `Material` parameter but `identity` and `fallback`; `PartStyle.interaction` as a whole, and
`RippleStyle.effect` and `max_radius` (S2.12); a `FocusIndicator`'s
`shadow` and `transition` (its `dash` is stated, `solid` included, S2.4); `IconStyle.state_effect`, `weight`, `scale`,
`animation`, and `fill` where `rendering_mode` is `Original` only (S2.9);
`Glyph.stroke`, `draw_extent`, and `fill` on a stroked-only path (a spinner's arc, whose paint is its `stroke`'s;
S12 refuses `fill` absent where the stroke can be absent too); `Glyph.size` and `fill` on a `SystemControl` source
(S15: the rendering draws the parts it replaces, and where it is not drawn those parts draw their own style, so
the glyph's size and fill are never drawn; ADD-A125, ADD-A126);
`RippleStyle.color`, `alpha` and `padding` where its `effect` is absent (no press ripple to draw, ADD-A125); `TextStyle.decoration`, `mnemonic_decoration` (not
`letter_spacing` and `word_spacing`: a platform whose text has no such spacing draws the font's own advances and
spaces, with nothing added, so it states `0px`, S17's zero by omission, its absence citation naming the property the
platform's text attributes lack, as every bundled preset's facts state both; ADD-A141, the MT-C1 and MC-C1
tie-breaks; rejected: `Absent`, a second spelling of the same look, which the verifiers wrote for word spacing);
in a keyed text style and a slot only, `TextStyle.fill`, `elision`, `wrap` and `max_lines`, each where the
platform's style does not set it (S2.8, ADD-A130);
`Decoration.by_word`; an `Edge`'s `width` and `paint` (an edge not drawn);
`Font.width`; every `TextRendering` field; `Stroke.outset` on an `Inside` or `Center` stroke only (a length on
an `Outside` one, `0px` for no gap, S2.4; ADD-A146); `Edge.dash` on an edge not drawn only (its `width` or
`paint` absent; S12 refuses it absent on a drawn edge, S2.4); `PartStyle.shape` and `touch_target` (the latter
wherever the platform sets no minimum interactive size, never `0px`, S2.11; not `margin`: a part with no margin
states `0px` on each side, S17's zero by omission where its platform's layout has no such property, for the reason
letter and word spacing do, above; ADD-A146; rejected: `Absent`, a second spelling of the same layout, which the
`material-3` and `kde-breeze` facts wrote),
and a part's drawing fields `fill`, `stroke`, `shadow`, `text`, `icon`, `glyph`, `focus`, `cursor` (a part that paints
nothing at rest, a flat button's fill, states `"absent"`; leaving a listed field out is still missing, S2.2);
`Caret.secondary`, `shown_in_read_only`, `solid_while_typing`, and `width` where the platform's caret width follows
each line, the caret parts stating it (S4.2, ADD-A130); every `Value` field of `Behavior`, `TouchBehavior`,
`ScrollPhysics` and `PointerTokens` (a plain enum or record field, `Behavior.scroll`, is stated, and so is every
parameter of a `ScrollDecay`; the catalogue's rule, *Entry format*; `KdeTokens` and `KdeEffects` are stated whole,
`tint_factor`'s `None` saying the scheme does not tint, S4.8); in an icon-size context, every `IconStyle`
`Value` field but `size` (S4.5); `IconTokens.theme_fallback`; a spring's
`Transition.duration` and `PresentationStep.duration` (checked: `Absent` only where the timing, followed through
references, is a `Spring`, and a `Transition.duration` under `WinUiAnimatedIcon`, whose visual times it, S2.7; a
`Loop.period` is never absent, as its keyframes' `at` are fractions of it);
`Concentric.minimum`; `Full.maximum`; `Keyframe.timing`; `Glyph.draw_start`; a zero-duration `Transition.timing`
and `PresentationStep.timing`, and a `Transition.timing` under `WinUiAnimatedIcon` (checked: `Absent` exactly where
its `duration` is a stated zero or its engine `WinUiAnimatedIcon`, S2.7; ADD-A125, ADD-A126). A list (`Vec`) is never `Absent`: it is
stated, empty where the platform has none (S2.11). The catalogue's tables are the second source; they cite these
marks rather than repeat them. The derive generates the tables from the catalogue; `Absent` anywhere
else is an error when the layer is added (S12).

## S7. Rules and selectors (R2.3)

```rust
pub struct Rule { pub selector: Selector, pub body: RuleBody }
pub enum RuleBody { Colors(Box<ColorRolesPatch>), Tokens(Box<TokensPatch>), Part(PartRef, PartPatch),
                    Values(ValuesPatch) }        // the target and its patch in one: a mismatch cannot be written
pub enum WidgetRef { Typed(WidgetKind), Component(Key) }
pub struct Selector {
    pub conditions: SetMatch<Condition>,
    pub context: Vec<ContextMatch>,           // every one must match
    pub not_context: Vec<ContextMatch>,       // none may match
    pub position: Option<PositionMatch>,
    pub variants: SetMatch<VariantRef>,
    pub size: SizeMatch,
    pub direction: Option<Direction>,
    pub states: SetMatch<StateFlag>,
    pub latest: Vec<(Key, StateFlag)>,        // per recency set (S10), the flag that must be its latest (S7.2)
}
pub enum VariantRef { Typed(Variant), Keyed(Key) }   // Variant: the catalogue's typed variants, one enum
pub struct SetMatch<T> { pub all_of: Vec<T>, pub none_of: Vec<T> }
pub struct ContextMatch { pub scope: ContextScope, pub target: Option<WidgetOrPart>,   // None: any widget (R25.9)
                          pub sizes: SetMatch<ControlSize>,    // the ancestor's control size (MAC-MN15)
                          pub surface: Option<SurfaceSet>,     // the ancestor binds this surface set (Q1.37,
                                                               // ADD-A68); None in any of these: not matched on
                          pub variants: SetMatch<VariantRef>, pub states: SetMatch<StateFlag> }
pub enum ContextScope { AnyAncestor, NearestAmong(Vec<WidgetRef>) }
pub struct PositionMatch { pub among: SiblingScope,                 // which siblings count (R25.9)
                           pub first: Option<bool>, pub last: Option<bool>, pub only: Option<bool>,
                           pub parity: Option<Parity>,
                           pub previous: Option<SiblingMatch>, pub next: Option<SiblingMatch> }
                                                   // previous, next: the adjacent sibling among those `among` names
pub enum SiblingScope { SameKind, Any, Kinds(Vec<WidgetRef>) }     // default SameKind
pub enum Parity { Odd, Even }                                       // counted from 1, among `among`
pub struct SiblingMatch { pub target: Option<WidgetOrPart>,
                          pub variants: SetMatch<VariantRef>, pub states: SetMatch<StateFlag> }
pub struct SizeMatch { pub sizes: SetMatch<ControlSize>, pub densities: SetMatch<Density>,
                       pub size_classes: SizeClassMatch }
pub struct SizeClassMatch { pub horizontal: SetMatch<SizeClass>, pub vertical: SetMatch<SizeClass> }
pub enum Direction { Ltr, Rtl }
```

A rule targeting `Colors` or `Tokens` may only have `conditions` (S12 rejects others).

### S7.1 Conditions

```rust
pub enum Condition {
    // system, by the reader (R2.3)
    Scheme(Scheme), ContrastIncreased, ContrastHigh, ReducedTransparency, ReducedMotion, AnimationsOff,
    BoldText, ButtonShapes, DifferentiateWithoutColor, TabletMode, MobileFormFactor, BatterySaver,
    ContainerSize { container: WidgetRef, size: Key },     // macOS's sidebar icon size
    OverlayScrollbars, OnOffLabels, FullKeyboardAccess, PreferCrossFade,
    AccessibilityTextSize,                                 // the content-size category is one of the five
                                                           // accessibility categories (S8's `ContentSizeCategory`)
    Idiom(Idiom), SystemSetting(Key), DeviceModel(Key),    // a platform switch the reader reads, declared (S10);
                                                           // the device model where a measured value differs per
                                                           // model (the display radius, W-6, X-CR-4)
    // window, by the connector
    WindowInactive, NotMain, AppInactive, Maximized, FullScreen, Tiled(TiledEdges),
    Elevated, Input(InputKind),                            // the kind of the last input (Kirigami's transient
                                                           // touch, WinUI's input kind; R2.3)
    NotComposited, Shaded, AttentionFlash, TintDimmed, MnemonicsVisible, Freeform,   // Freeform: Android's desktop
                                                           // windowing (MAT-W5†)
    Posture(Posture),                                      // MAT-P3-13†
    UnitScale,                                             // device pixel ratio 1 (Qt Quick's text rendering, Q3.32)
    // application
    Flavor(Key), Preset(PresetId),
}
pub enum Scheme { Light, Dark }
pub enum InputKind { Mouse, Touch, Pen, GameController }
pub enum Idiom { Phone, Pad }                          // what the rows need (ADD-A09)
pub enum Posture { Flat, Tabletop, Book }              // a foldable's posture (Jetpack WindowManager)
pub struct TiledEdges { pub top: bool, pub right: bool, pub bottom: bool, pub left: bool }
```

`Tiled(e)` holds when the window's tiled edges include every edge `e` names (a window maximised along one axis is
tiled to those two edges, R13, and a window maximised on both axes to all four, with `Maximized` holding too, so a
`tiled:left` rule matches it); every other parametrised condition holds on equality. `ContainerSize` holds for
exactly one size of each container the preset declares (`container_sizes`, S10): the size the reader or stand-in
reports for it (`ReaderState.container_sizes`), else its declared default, the first, also in the no-reader state
(S16), so a rule under the default size applies wherever nothing is read.

A keyed condition (`SystemSetting`, `DeviceModel`, a `ContainerSize`'s size) holds by its key under whichever preset
is current (ADD-A146): the reader reports the keys of what it read in its `ReaderState`, part of what any preset
takes (S9.5), a rule selects on a key its own preset declares (S10), and a reported key the current preset does not
declare selects nothing (for a container, its declared default then holding, above). So a `SystemSetting` key names
one setting on every platform whose preset declares it, and two platforms' settings that differ take a key each (the
catalogue's *conditions*: Win32's `SPI_GETUIEFFECTS`, W3-53†, and KDE's `GraphicEffectsLevel`, K-P3-24†, are two).
Rejected: a reader's keyed conditions holding under its own preset alone, as its keyed roles and tokens apply (S9.5):
a switch between the two macOS generations would lose the sidebar size the user set, and a key means one setting
either way.

The list is closed by the catalogue and the traceability: a condition a row needs that is not here is added here.
The additions and their rows: ADD-A01 … ADD-A12, ADD-A76, ADD-A83 (S22). `OverlayScrollbars` replaces `scrollbar.overlay_mode`.
The readers report the system conditions directly (R2.3; today's `AccessibilityPreferences` goes, S16);
`text_scaling_factor` stays a reader value (S9.4). `MobileFormFactor` is Plasma Mobile's shell, which is not a device
idiom; `Idiom` is UIKit's and Material's phone and pad.

**`FullKeyboardAccess`** (ADD-A06, ADD-A135; ledger queue #166 (2)) is the setting under which the platform's
controls take keyboard focus, and so show it. On macOS it is the Keyboard navigation setting (System Settings >
Keyboard), which `NSApplication.isFullKeyboardAccessEnabled` reports, "whether
keyboard navigation is enabled in System Settings > Keyboard", not "the separate accessibility setting named 'Full
Keyboard Access'" (`NSApplication.h:377-380` at xcode@26.6, `:373-376` at xcode@16.4), whose highlight the system
draws (MAC-X31†, out, R1.1); the macOS reader reads that property, on the main thread only (S9.3's *The macOS
reader's readings*; ADD-A138), and key-value observing does not report its changes (the same note), so a change shows at the reader's next read, no watcher event announcing it. On iOS it is Full Keyboard Access, the one
setting of the name (X-FO-3†, no API found). The name stays the API's. Rejected: renaming the condition after the
macOS setting's label (iOS's setting and both platforms' API keep the name); one condition per macOS setting (the
accessibility setting's highlight is the system's, MAC-X31†, which no preset states).

### S7.2 State flags (R3)

```rust
pub enum StateFlag { Hover, Pressed, Focused, FocusWithin, FocusVisible, Disabled, Checked, Selected,
                     Indeterminate, Open, Default, Dragged, DropTarget, ReadOnly, Invalid, Visited,
                     Autofilled, Scrolled, OverDarkContent, OpenedByTouch, Overflowing, Redacted,
                     Shared(SharedFlag), Widget(Key) }
pub enum SharedFlag { Empty, InFill, Today, OtherMonth, Current, Multiline, Filled, Half, Preview, Placeholder,
                      Pulling, Refreshing, PlacedAbove, PlacedBelow, RouteActive, Editing, Swiped, ContextMenuOpen,
                      Sorted, Descending, Overwrite, Composing, Minimized,
                      TextSelected,    // a text widget holding a selection (the caret hides, GN-3.73†)
                      DropCopy, DropMove }   // a drop target's operation (W3-49†, P3-10†)
                      // flags two or more platforms draw on a typed widget (ADD-A15); the catalogue's
                      // *Shared flags* table names the widgets that declare each
```

`Selected` is "the current choice among siblings" (a list row, a tab, a segment, a combo list's chosen value); a
menu item's keyboard or pointer highlight is `Focused` or `Hover`, never `Selected`; `Checked` is "toggled on" (a check
box, a toggle button, a menu item's check). A connector sets them by that meaning on every platform. The focus flags
(`Focused`, `FocusWithin`, `FocusVisible`) are the toolkit's in an inactive window (ADD-A126): GTK and Qt clear them as
the window deactivates (`gtk@4.24.1 gtk/gtkwindow.c:6172-6175`, `:5231-5233`, `:5271`; `qtbase@6.12.0
src/widgets/kernel/qapplication.cpp:1891-1892`, `hasFocus()` being `focusWidget() == this`, `src/widgets/kernel/qwidget.cpp:6506`; Qt Quick, under
`flavor:kirigami`, as its window's content item gives up focus, `qtdeclarative@6.12.0
src/quick/items/qquickwindow.cpp:225-230`), so on `adwaita` and `kde-breeze` a window deactivating is a flag change for its focused element, whose focus
transitions run out (S2.7, S2.10); whether AppKit, UIKit, WinUI and Compose keep them in an inactive window is
measured with each lane's focus rows, and where a platform keeps them its facts state the inactive window's focus
under `cond window_inactive`. An element inside a focusable widget holds them as the toolkit sets them on it: Qt sets
a tab's `State_HasFocus` only on its bar's current tab (`qtbase@6.12.0 src/widgets/widgets/qtabbar.cpp:145-146`), so a
tab holds the focus flags only while it is current (K1.129). Which element holds a widget-wide or item-wide flag is
the catalogue's rule (*Entry format*, **Flags**; ADD-A146): a flag is set on the element whose state it is and on no
other element of the widget, `hover` on the element under the pointer and on every element of the widget it nests
in, as the toolkits hold it, `pressed`, `focused` and `focus_visible` on the one element that takes the press or
holds the focus, `focus_within` on that element and on every element it nests in, and `disabled` alone also held by every element of a disabled widget and of a disabled *(element)* part; a
nested element reads its host's flags by `context`. `Shared` flags have
one name for a portable application: the list is exactly the catalogue's flags that two or
more platforms draw, and the catalogue says which widgets declare each.
`Widget(Key)` is a one-platform flag the preset declares (S10). Exclusive groups: S10.

**Recency** (R3, CONTRA-6, ADD-A124). A selector's `latest` entry `(set, flag)` matches when `flag` is present after
the exclusive groups' drop (S10), that is kept, and was set after every other kept flag of the widget's recency set
`set` (S10). The order is the connector's: `Element.state_order` lists the element's flags in the order it last set
each of them, the latest last (S8), which it records, beside the previous query results it keeps per element (S2.7),
when each flag became set (an immediate-mode toolkit recomputes the flags every frame). A kept flag of the set that `state_order` leaves out
counts as set before every flag it lists, and such flags among themselves by the set's stated order, its first as the
latest, so a connector that reports no order gets the stated order as a fixed precedence. A recency term reads the
queried element's own flags only: `ContextMatch.states` and `SiblingMatch.states` match an ancestor's or a sibling's
flags as a set, as the `Scope` and `Sibling` carry no order (no platform row needs one there). Compose is the reason:
its state layer shows the latest of hover, focus and drag, and a button's elevation the latest of hover, focus and
press, each from its own list of the interactions in the order they began (`androidx@e4d933c9
compose/material3/material3-ripple/src/commonMain/kotlin/androidx/compose/material3/ripple/Ripple.kt:250-280`,
`compose/material3/material3/src/commonMain/kotlin/androidx/compose/material3/Button.kt:1703-1747`), so the press
counts against hover and focus for the elevation but not for the state layer, which it is drawn beside.

### S7.3 Sizes, density, size classes (R15, R16)

```rust
pub enum ControlSize { ExtraSmall, Mini, Small, Regular, Large, ExtraLarge }
pub enum Density { Default, Compact, Keyed(Key) }      // Material's density steps keyed
pub enum SizeClass { Compact, Medium, Expanded, Large, ExtraLarge, Regular }   // closed by the catalogue
pub struct Breakpoint { pub measured: Measured, pub width: Option<(Comparison, Value<Px>)>,
                        pub height: Option<(Comparison, Value<Px>)>, pub combine: Combine,
                        pub variant: VariantRef }      // R16; the platform's own conditions, not inverted
pub enum Comparison { AtLeast, AtMost, Above, Below }  // ≥, ≤, >, < (AdwDialog: width ≤ or height ≤)
pub enum Combine { All, Any }                          // both stated sizes must hold, or either
```

A widget's `breakpoints: Vec<Breakpoint>` is a widget value (R16), stated among its values (S11's `Breakpoint` row)
and read through `values()`, so a rule restates the list under a condition or a variant and a threshold may read
element data (the catalogue's `dialog`: AdwPreferencesDialog's under `paged`, its first threshold an expression over
`element.item_count`; Kirigami's under `mobile_form_factor`). It is no declaration (ADD-A146; rejected:
`[declare.widget.<w>] breakpoints`, as S10's example had it and the slice's code read it: a declaration differs by
flavour alone, S10, and reads no element data, so it could state neither). The connector queries `values()` with the
element's other variants, evaluates each `Breakpoint` of the list that query returns against the allocation or the
window it measures, adds the variant of each that holds to `Element.variants` while it holds, and queries the
element's parts and values again with them. The list and the thresholds it evaluates are the first query's, so no
breakpoint's variant feeds back into its own test (as `Measured` names no box the variant sizes, below), and S12
refuses a `Values` rule patching `breakpoints` that selects on a variant a breakpoint of that widget sets, a list no
connector would evaluate. Rules of two variants that hold together apply in stated rule order, as any rules do.

```rust
pub enum Measured { Allocation, Window, Part(PartRef) }   // the size the parent offers the element, the window's,
                                                       // or the allocation of a part of the widget that holds the
                                                       // content (AdwPreferencesDialog's breakpoint bin, GN-2.10):
                                                       // never a box the breakpoint's own variant sizes, so a
                                                       // variant that changes padding does not feed back into it
pub struct SizeClasses { pub horizontal: Option<SizeClass>, pub vertical: Option<SizeClass> }   // R25.10; None:
                                                                     // the platform states no class on that axis
```

Each preset's facts state which of its sizes fills which `ControlSize` slot (Material Expressive's button sizes,
AppKit's control sizes, per macOS version); a preset declares only the slots it fills (S10).

**Kirigami's wide screen** (ADD-A134). Kirigami has one window class, two-valued, on the width alone: an
`ApplicationWindow` is `wideScreen` while its width is at least its page row's `defaultColumnWidth`, a public
property whose default is `gridUnit × 20`, plus the widths of its global drawer and of a context drawer other than Kirigami's own `ContextDrawer`
(`kirigami@6.31.0 src/controls/ApplicationWindow.qml:112`, `src/controls/PageRow.qml:122`; the bare
`AbstractApplicationWindow`'s `gridUnit × 60`, `src/controls/AbstractApplicationWindow.qml:114`, is the one it
overrides). So `kde-breeze` under `cond flavor:kirigami` states two horizontal classes, `Compact` (not wide) from
zero and `Regular` (wide) from the default column width, and no vertical one: the two-valued classes of the closed set,
UIKit's compact and regular (LY-1), where Material's names would claim steps Kirigami does not have. The drawers' widths are the
application's structure, which no token can read (S2.2), so the connector passes `size_classes` (S8) the window's
width less those drawers' widths, the `Regular` bound then the column width alone, exactly Kirigami's test at the
default; an application that sets its own `defaultColumnWidth` states its bound in an application layer
(`token.size_classes`), as it states any look of its own (S8). Rejected:
`Compact` and `Expanded` (Material's names, implying its `Medium` between); `AbstractApplicationWindow`'s `gridUnit
× 60` as the bound (`ApplicationWindow`, the window with the page row and the drawers, overrides it); a bound expression over the drawers (a token reads no
element data).

## S8. Layers, order and resolution (R2.4, R2.5)

```rust
pub struct Layer { pub bases: Bases, pub for_preset: Vec<(PresetId, Bases)>,  // an application layer;
                   pub rules: Vec<Rule> }             // Layer::from_toml (S1); a preset's own bases apply after the
                                                      // layer's common bases while that preset is current, and are
                                                      // validated only then (S11's `[for_preset.<id>]`)
pub struct Bases { pub colors: Box<SchemeMap<ColorRolesPatch>>, pub inputs: InputBases, pub tokens: Box<TokensPatch>,
                   pub widgets: WidgetsPatch,              // derive-generated: per widget an Option<Box<<W>Patch>>, its parts and values
                   pub components: Vec<(Key, ComponentBase)> }
// The patches are boxed where they fan out (per widget, per part, the tokens', the colour roles', a rule's and a
// widget's values'), so a `Layer`'s and a `Rule`'s value stays small and a typed widget adds one pointer to a layer;
// a layer is held by value on a thread's stack while it is read and validated (ADD-A132).
pub struct ReaderState {                                   // the system conditions a reader reports (R2.3, S7.1)
    pub scheme: Scheme, pub contrast: Option<Contrast>, pub reduced_transparency: bool, pub reduced_motion: bool,
    pub animations_off: bool, pub bold_text: bool, pub button_shapes: bool, pub differentiate_without_color: bool,
    pub tablet_mode: bool, pub mobile_form_factor: bool, pub battery_saver: bool, pub overlay_scrollbars: bool,
    pub on_off_labels: bool, pub full_keyboard_access: bool, pub prefer_cross_fade: bool,
    pub idiom: Option<Idiom>, pub device_model: Option<Key>,
    pub container_sizes: Vec<(WidgetRef, Key)>, pub system_settings: Vec<Key>,
    pub text_scaling_factor: f32,                          // S9.4
    pub font_dpi: Option<f32>,                             // the system's font DPI where the platform has a setting
                                                           // the toolkit's scale factor does not carry (S9.4: no
                                                           // reader of 0.8.0 reports one; a stand-in may); None:
                                                           // the preset's `token.text.font_dpi` (S9.4)
    pub content_size_category: Option<ContentSizeCategory>,   // iOS's, for `DynamicType` and `uifm_scaled`
                                                           // (S9.4); None: the default category, the one the
                                                           // `DynamicType` kind's table names (the facts, S17)
}
pub enum ContentSizeCategory {                             // UIKit's `UIContentSizeCategory`, smallest first
    ExtraSmall, Small, Medium, Large, ExtraLarge, ExtraExtraLarge, ExtraExtraExtraLarge,
    AccessibilityMedium, AccessibilityLarge, AccessibilityExtraLarge, AccessibilityExtraExtraLarge,
    AccessibilityExtraExtraExtraLarge,                     // `AccessibilityTextSize` holds for these five
}
pub struct WindowConditions {                              // a window's conditions, by the connector
    pub inactive: bool, pub not_main: bool, pub app_inactive: bool, pub maximized: bool, pub full_screen: bool,
    pub tiled: TiledEdges, pub elevated: bool, pub input: InputKind, pub not_composited: bool, pub shaded: bool,
    pub attention_flash: bool, pub tint_dimmed: bool, pub mnemonics_visible: bool, pub freeform: bool,
    pub posture: Option<Posture>, pub unit_scale: bool,
}
pub struct RootInputs { pub density: Option<Density>, pub size_classes: SizeClasses, pub direction: Direction,
                        pub language: Option<LanguageTag>, pub window: Size, pub screen: Size,  // the work area
                        pub display_corner_radius: Option<[Px; 4]> }   // where the platform reports it (Android,
                                                                       // MAT-W5†); see S4.6
```

Typed structs make a condition from the wrong source unrepresentable: a connector cannot state the scheme, nor a
reader a window's state. The application's conditions (flavour, the scheme and the contrast it picks, R2.3, R25.2)
come from `Theme`'s setters, and win over the reader's. The layout direction is the connector's (`RootInputs.direction`,
R2.3): its toolkit's layout direction for the window, else the application's own; no reader reports one, `ReaderState`
holding none (ADD-A146: GTK's and Qt's, `gtk_get_locale_direction` and `QGuiApplication::layoutDirection`, GN-FM03†,
K-FM03†, are toolkit calls, which a reader that links neither toolkit cannot make; rejected:
`ReaderState.direction: Option<Direction>` from the locale's script, a second source for a value the toolkit or the
application already holds).

**Layers and order.** The stack is: the preset; on `kde-breeze` and `material-3`, the accent-derivation layer `Theme` derives, stating
its roles at the slots where a layer above the preset gives the accent in force (S9.2; ADD-A132, ADD-A134); the reader, or the stand-in an application without a reader sets
(`set_reader_stand_in`, R2.6; refused while a reader exists, `Err(ReaderPresent)`); then the application's layers in
the order it adds them (R2.4), the palette `apply_palette` adds among them where it was first added; and last the
accent layer, which `Theme` derives from the `Accent` the application set on every change of the stack (preset,
palette, reader re-read), so which accent shows never depends on call order. The accent is a setting, not a layer
the application stacks. Every layer's bases apply in that order, then every
layer's rules in that order. While a palette applies, the reader's or stand-in's colour bases, colour rules, inputs
(every input it states, each an `InputValue`, a colour: the `kde_scheme.*` scheme inputs and the inactive input
roles among them; its accent inputs, the preset's `accent_inputs`, S9.1, under a mapping, which states its own, R19,
but not under a KDE port, which states none, so the reader's or stand-in's `input.accent` stays in force there,
R2.6; ADD-A142, ADD-A145), the three lists (`groups`, `inactive_groups` and `unset_keys`, S9's `InputBases`
fields) and `token.kde` are left out; the palette does not apply while `ContrastIncreased` or `ContrastHigh` holds unless it
states colours for that condition (colour rules under it, or per-contrast input bases for it, S9), and the reader's or
stand-in's colours then apply as without it (R19). While the current preset is not the reader's own (S9.5) and declares
`accent_inputs` beyond `accent` (S9.1), `Theme` leaves the reader's common `input.accent`, with its per-contrast
bases, out, as it leaves the reader's `for_preset` part out: that preset keeps its own accent and derived inputs,
and no accent mixes with derived inputs of another (S9.5). On the reader's own preset its accent applies with its
derived inputs. On `kde-breeze`, at a slot (S9) where a layer above the reader or stand-in gives the `input.accent` in
force (the accent layer; a mapping palette, under which the reader's or stand-in's accent is left out; never a KDE
port, which states no accent), the reader's or stand-in's stated
accent-dependent roles and inactive input roles (S9.1's list, the `[WM]` keyed roles among them), in its bases and
rules, are left out, and a
KDE port's at every slot where the accent-derivation layer states its roles (where a layer above the preset gives the
accent in force: under a port, the reader's or stand-in's, which stays in force beneath it, or the accent layer's;
ADD-A142): each holds the derivation of its own accent, or of none, so the
accent-derivation layer's roles over the accent in force show there instead (S9.2; ADD-A132). On `material-3` the
same holds for the reader's or stand-in's stated accent-dependent roles (S9.1's: the `md.sys.color` keyed roles),
which hold the scheme of their own seed (ADD-A134).

**Validation** (S12) holds for the whole stack after every change of it (S16), conservatively (every
rule and binding an expression can meet, under every combination of conditions that can hold together, S12,
R2.8; beneath a palette it may keep the reader's or stand-in's `token.kde`, which it reads under every scheme at
once, since no check then differs: every field of `token.kde` is stated, S4.8, and was validated with that layer, a
port's `Tokens` rule states every field over it at the port's scheme, and S12's one check reading a `token.kde`
value across layers reads the preset's `tint_factor` alone, which the code must match, as today it reads the whole
stack's, the reader's included; ADD-A145, task T6b's reading): a change after which it would not hold is refused
whole, leaving the theme as it was (R2.5). Each layer above the preset has its own checks, and the input cycle check
over the stack up to it, run at every change; the checks over combinations run over each layer whose stack, as they
read it, the change altered, and not over a stack S19.1's build test validates at every commit (one the crate
builds from bundled data alone: a bundled preset whose `[pending]` table is empty, with a bundled palette over it and
the layers `Theme` derives from them; S12's *What a change re-checks*), so a layer the crate bundles or derives from
bundled data is not checked over combinations again at run time, and a layer the system or the application adds (an
application's palette given to `apply_palette` among them) is checked when it is added; the preset's own checks run
when it is loaded, except on the trusted route: trust goes by the `PresetId`, its text the one the crate embeds, on
`from_preset`, `set_preset` and `from_system`'s preset alone, and every other route that takes a text validates it
(R2.8; ADD-A147; the D6 load design, 3.3). So resolution and the query cannot fail. A reader's re-read that fails keeps
the previous reader layer; `Theme::reader_status()` reports the error.

**Windows and resolution.** Each window's connector owns a `WindowState` (`Default`: never resolved), and
`Theme::resolve(&self, window: &mut WindowState, conditions: &WindowConditions) -> Resolution` resolves for it
(infallible), with `Resolution { theme: Arc<ResolvedTheme>, change: Change, suspends: bool }` (`suspends`: the change
starts the theme-change token's `Suspend`, `pick`'s scheme change included, S4.3; ADD-A126; staged with the motion
unit, S4.3, S6.1; ADD-A147), `Change = First | Unchanged | ThemeChange |
ConditionChange` relative to that window's last resolution, which `WindowState` records (a theme change wins when
both happened; a flavour switch is a condition change; S4.3): it compares the layers' values, the inputs and the
reader values with those it recorded, and the conditions (the window's, the reader's `ReaderState` conditions and the
application's) separately, and only a change of the first kind, or of `Scheme` or a contrast condition, is a theme
change. `WindowState` also keeps the resolution it returned: for `Unchanged`, `resolve` returns that one again
without building one (ADD-A147). After any change but `Unchanged` a connector rebuilds the
scopes it kept, whose bound colours are the old resolution's (an inactive window changes roles too):

1. merge bases in order; for colours, the base of the conditions' scheme; for each input, its value at the scheme
   and contrast in force, that of the last layer whose value of the input applies there and that has one (S9: its
   contrast base for a contrast condition that holds, else its per-scheme value; an input S8 leaves out, a reader's,
   a stand-in's or a port's, and a palette suspended or skipped, not counting);
2. apply the `Colors` and `Tokens` rules whose conditions hold, in order (choosing expressions, not evaluating);
3. for each part and widget, keep its base and its rules whose conditions hold, in order.

A window resolves again on any change of its conditions, an input, a reader value, a layer, the flavour or the
preset.

**Query.** `ResolvedTheme::root_scope(&RootInputs) -> Scope` gives the window's root scope. Each query's returned
`Scope` is its input scope plus this part's ancestor entry and bindings; a connector passes, for any part or element,
the scope returned by the query of the innermost part that encloses it in the catalogue's nesting (a widget's root part:
its host's part that holds it). An ancestor entry records the element it belongs to: context selectors (`ContextMatch`,
`context` in S11) skip the entries of the queried element's own parts (its root's, an enclosing plain part's), so
`context button` means an enclosing button, never the button the part belongs to, while bindings found there still
apply (S2.11, S3.3). Every query takes its parent's scope and returns its own, so a connector queries
top-down, as it draws. A `Scope` holds owned, evaluated values only (the ancestor chain, each ancestor's widget, part,
variants, states, control size and the surface set it binds, which context selectors match; the bound colours; density,
size classes, direction, language; the window's and screen's size; which element and part is the nearest container and
its stated corners, the display at the root, whose computed radii the connector passes to `native_theme::corners`,
S2.4), so a scope kept across a re-resolution is safe to use but stale; the connector rebuilds it (above). Tokens and
roles are read in a scope too, for what no part carries (behaviour timings, the caret, text rendering, the pointer, the
window's background).

```rust
pub enum Styled<T> { Style(T), NotDrawn, DrawnAs { target: WidgetOrPart, variants: Vec<VariantRef> },
                     NotAvailable(Unavailable) }   // R2.7's answer; not an error
pub enum Unavailable { Widget, Size, Variant, Part, Later }   // `Later`: the platform has the variant or the
                                                         // size, and a later unit states it (S10; ADD-A147)
impl ResolvedTheme {
    pub fn root_scope(&self, root: &RootInputs) -> Scope;
    pub fn style(&self, element: &Element) -> Styled<(ResolvedPartStyle, Scope)>;  // the scope for its children
    pub fn values<W: Widget>(&self, element: &Element) -> Styled<W::Values>;       // another widget's element:
                                                                                   // NotAvailable(Widget)
    pub fn component_values(&self, element: &Element) -> Styled<ComponentValues>;
    pub fn tokens(&self, scope: &Scope) -> ResolvedTokens;
    pub fn role(&self, scope: &Scope, role: RoleRef) -> Option<Color>;             // None: not drawn
    pub fn size_classes(&self, window: Size) -> SizeClasses;                        // from the thresholds (R16)
    pub fn palette_status(&self) -> Option<PaletteStatus>;                          // S14; None: no palette
    pub fn data_needs(&self, part: PartRef) -> DataNeeds;   // the element data and metrics its values read, and
                                                            // whether its glyph or icon is drawn to its box (below)
    pub fn kept_states(&self, element: &Element) -> StateFlags;   // its flags after the exclusive groups' drop, which
                                                            // a transition's `from` and a Breeze test are matched
                                                            // against (S2.7); a resolved part style carries the
                                                            // Breeze tests of every rule that can apply to the
                                                            // element, in rank order, each with the groups its
                                                            // transitions list (`breeze_tests`, S6.1, S2.7)
}
pub struct Element<'a> {                                   // Element::new(part, scope, metrics) and setters
    pub part: PartRef,                                     // names the widget too (S1)
    pub scope: &'a Scope,                                  // the scope returned by the query of the innermost
                                                           // part that encloses it in the catalogue's nesting
    pub variants: &'a [VariantRef], pub size: Option<ControlSize>,      // None: the default size in force (S10: the matching
                                                                        // context entry's, else the variant entry's,
                                                                        // else the widget's; none in force or pending: S8)
    pub density: Option<Density>, pub direction: Option<Direction>,     // the element's own, if it states one,
    pub size_classes: Option<SizeClasses>,                              // passed to its subtree (R16)
    pub language: Option<LanguageTag>,                                  // for icon lookup (S2.9)
    pub states: StateFlags,
    pub state_order: &'a [StateFlag],                      // the order the connector last set its flags in, the
                                                           // latest last; empty by default (S7.2's recency, R25.3)
    pub siblings: &'a [Sibling<'a>], pub index: usize,                  // its siblings, itself at `index`; those a
                                                                        // connector may leave out: *Siblings*, below
    pub data: ElementData<'a>,
    pub metrics: &'a dyn FontMetrics,                      // the toolkit's measurement
}
pub struct Scope { /* owned: see above */ }
pub trait FontMetrics { fn char_width(&self, font: &ResolvedFont) -> Px;      // the average character width
                        fn max_char_width(&self, font: &ResolvedFont) -> Px;  // the widest glyph (KCharSelect)
                        fn x_height(&self, font: &ResolvedFont) -> Px;
                        fn height(&self, font: &ResolvedFont) -> Px;          // ascent plus descent
                        fn descent(&self, font: &ResolvedFont) -> Px;         // the font's descent, positive
                                                                              // below the baseline (ADD-A147)
                        fn line_spacing(&self, font: &ResolvedFont) -> Px;    // plus leading
                        fn underline_offset(&self, font: &ResolvedFont) -> Px;      // the font's own decoration
                        fn underline_thickness(&self, font: &ResolvedFont) -> Px;   // lines, in `Decoration`'s
                        fn strikeout_offset(&self, font: &ResolvedFont) -> Px;      // convention (S2.8);
                        fn strikeout_thickness(&self, font: &ResolvedFont) -> Px; } // all infallible
pub struct Sibling<'a> { pub part: PartRef, pub variants: &'a [VariantRef], pub states: StateFlags }
pub struct ElementData<'a> {                               // R25.3; Default: zero size, progress 0, scroll 0,
    pub width: Px, pub height: Px, pub progress: Fraction, // item 0 of 1, empty text, transparent
    pub scroll_offset: Px, pub scroll_progress: Fraction,
    pub item_index: u32, pub item_count: u32, pub text: &'a str,
    pub color: Color,                                      // a colour the connector supplies that derived values
                                                           // follow: the application's choice (a badge), or the
                                                           // text's colour under a caret (K-P3-11†)
    pub move_distance: Px,                                 // how far a Move presentation moves it (K1.133†)
    pub caret_height: Px,                                  // a caret part's: its toolkit's caret rectangle's
                                                           // height, as drawn (S4.2; ADD-A130)
}
```

The operands `element.window_width`, `window_height`, `screen_width` and `screen_height` (Q2.50, Q1.60, K-P3-7†)
come from the root's inputs through the scope; the font metrics from `Element.metrics`; the others from
`Element.data`.

The query tells the variants apart by name and element: the content variants are the catalogue's listed pairs, each a
widget or one of its *(element)* parts and a typed variant name (`button`: `icon_only`; `list.row`: `with_subtitle`;
*Entry format*, ADD-A61), or a keyed one whose meaning only one platform has (`button`'s `@with_arrow`, GTK's), which the
connector sets by that platform's rule under every preset (ADD-A123), a name being a content variant only on the widget or part its pair names; the breakpoint
variants are those a `Breakpoint` names in the widget's `breakpoints` value in any base of the stack or any rule of it
that can apply under the current preset, read off the stack as it is validated, not evaluated, as the value may
differ by rule (S7.3; ADD-A146); and every other variant in `Element.variants` (the
same name on another widget or part included: `vertical` on `slider`) is one the application asked for. The
declarations in force are the preset's, a flavour's section replacing the keys it states (S10). The query: ignores a
content or breakpoint variant the widget does not declare (as an undeclared density), and a keyed flag the widget does not declare selects nothing; answers `NotAvailable` for a size the element does not take (S10: its variant's and its context's), for no size where the sizes the element takes (S10) are not empty and its default is pending (S10's *A pending default*; on a synthetic theme alone, S17), an element that takes no size resolving with none (S10; ADD-A131), for an undeclared variant the
application asked for (and `NotAvailable(Later)` for an element holding a variant, a content variant included, that
its widget's declarations in force list under `later` (S10), or asking a size it takes that is not its default in
force while the sizes unit is not enabled (S6.1), or a declared density while the sizes unit is not enabled (S10), an answer that comes before every other but an unavailable
widget's; ADD-A147), an unavailable widget, an element holding none of
its widget's `requires_variants` (S10), or a part the widget does not have, and `NotDrawn` for a part whose style resolved `Absent` (the children of
a `NotDrawn` or `NotAvailable` element take the parent's scope), and `NotAvailable(Variant)` for an element holding two
variants of one exclusive variant group (S10); drops excluded flags by the exclusive groups (S10),
the element's by the groups its widget declares for its element (the widget's own element, or the *(element)* part
it is queried with; a group naming no parts is every element's, S10; ADD-A146), and each ancestor's and sibling's
states (which `ContextMatch.states` and `SiblingMatch.states` match) by the groups its own widget declares for its
element, and ignores a density the widget does not declare (R15);
orders the element's kept flags of each recency set that applies to it (S10) by `Element.state_order` and the set's stated order (S7.2), a flag
of `state_order` that is not present, or that the drop removed, counting for nothing, and a flag listed twice by its last
position; takes density, size classes, direction, language and
bindings from the scope, the element's own overriding them; applies the part's kept rules in order, skipping those
that do not match (position counted among the siblings the rule's `among` names; `SameKind` siblings are those of
the queried element's widget and part; an `index` outside `siblings` is treated as having none); evaluates
expressions (S2.2) with `base`, the element data, `part.`, `widget.`, `values.`, the font metrics and the bindings
in scope; and returns the part's style with the scope its children receive. `element.width` and `element.height`
are the laid-out box of the element the part is queried with: the widget's root part's box for the widget's element,
an *(element)* part's box for that element and the parts that belong to it (S2.11), never a nested plain part's. A
corner operand (`part.corners.<corner>`, `part.focus.corners.<corner>`, or the same through `widget.<part>.`)
resolves `Full` to half the smaller of `element.width` and `element.height` (the part declares that data), at most
its `maximum`; a focus corner (`part.focus.corners.<corner>`, `widget.<part>.focus.corners.<corner>`) on that box
grown by the focus indicator's `offset` on each side, the ring's inner box (S2.10). So it is allowed only on the corners of the element's own part (the root part, or the *(element)* part:
a split button's label reads its half's corners, `widget.primary.corners`); on a nested part's corners (a thumb, a
handle), and on `Concentric` and `FollowPart` anywhere, it is refused (S12), as only the connector computes those at
layout (S2.4); so is one on an `Ellipse` corner, whose two radii are no one length. `Element.variants` includes the variants the connector sets from the element's content
(`icon_only`, `with_icon`; GTK sets `.image-button` itself, ADD-A61).

**Siblings** (ADD-A146). A position term reads of `Element.siblings` only, per `among` scope, which is a set of
parts (S7): whether a counted sibling precedes the element and whether one follows it (`first`, `last`, `only`), the
parity of the number that precede it (`parity`), and the nearest counted sibling on each side (`previous`, `next`:
its part, variants and states). So a connector need not pass every sibling of a long or virtualised container: before
the element it may leave out an even number of each part's siblings, after it any number, and on neither side a
part's nearest sibling. What it passes then answers every position term as the whole list would, under every
`among`; a sibling it passes that is not its part's nearest on its side is counted only, its variants and states
unread. A list whose siblings are rows and separators so needs at most four siblings before a row and two after it,
whatever its length. Rejected: counts of the siblings left out at each end (`siblings_before`, `siblings_after`: two
more fields of an input filled in full, S21.2, and exact for one `among` scope only, the siblings left out being of
several parts); a constant-size position in place of the slice (R2.5's words, its position and its two neighbours:
they are per scope, the scopes are the rules', which the connector does not hold, and it is a breaking change to a
built type for the same answers).

The query cannot fail (R2.8): element data are plain values. Each part declares the data its values read (S10,
`data = [...]`, the font metrics included; a widget value that reads element data, a presentation step's duration
over `move_distance`, is declared under `values`), in the preset's `[declare]`, which every layer's expressions are
checked against (an application layer reads what the part declares, S10, S12); `data_needs` tells the connector what
to supply for a part, as it supplies the element's states. Expressions over `element.width` and `element.height` are not allowed in the fields that
lay the element out (a part's padding, margin, size limits and `touch_target`, widget gaps) or that size its content
(a text style's font size, line height, letter and word spacing, an icon's or glyph's size), unless the element's
size on that axis does not depend on its content (a fixed box: an avatar's initials sized to the avatar, GN-2.14;
the element's own part, root or *(element)*, is the box tested, S12), so one query per frame suffices (S12).

A glyph or icon **drawn to its box** is the one other exemption: a part's `glyph.size` or `icon.size` may read
`element.width` and `element.height` in a box that is not fixed (AdwSpinner draws its arc at the size it is allocated,
the smaller side capped, `adw-spinner-paintable.c:343`, while it measures at its minimum, `adw-spinner.c:70-81`).
That glyph or icon then takes no part in measuring the element: the connector measures the element without it, at
the element's own part's `min_width` and `min_height` on the axis read (which S12 requires stated as lengths, not
`auto`) and its other content, lays it out, and queries once with the laid-out box, which it draws the glyph to.
`data_needs` marks such a part as drawn to its box, so the connector knows to leave it out of the measurement.

A part a preset states `drawn_as` another widget (S6.1) is built as an element of that widget in the host's context,
queried in the scope the drawn part was queried in, with the variants `DrawnAs` names and the states of the host's
element (the element the drawn part belongs to: its hover, focus, pressed, …), as the platform's style draws the
substitute from its host's state (Breeze's scroll-area frame as a styled panel, K2.21); a flag the substitute's widget
does not declare selects nothing there, as on any element.

## S9. Inputs and readers (R2.6, R18)

```rust
pub struct InputBases { pub entries: Vec<(InputName, InputValue)>,
                        pub kde_groups: SchemeMap<Vec<SurfaceSet>>,            // `input.kde_scheme.groups`
                        pub kde_inactive_groups: SchemeMap<Vec<SurfaceSet>>,   // `input.kde_scheme.inactive_groups`
                        pub kde_unset_keys: SchemeMap<Vec<InputName>> }        // `input.kde_scheme.unset_keys`
                                              // (S9.1): `kde-breeze`'s only, empty elsewhere; stated together by
                                              // whoever states the scheme inputs; a later layer's list for a
                                              // scheme replaces the earlier one whole
pub struct InputValue { pub per_scheme: SchemeMap<Value<Color>>,
                        pub per_contrast: Vec<(Contrast, SchemeMap<Value<Color>>)> }
pub enum Contrast { Increased, High }         // one at a time: `ReaderState.contrast` holds one or none, and
                                              // `set_contrast` picks one or none over it (`ContrastChoice`, S16),
                                              // so the two conditions exclude each other (S12)
// An input is replaced slot by slot, never whole (ADD-A132). A slot is a scheme with no contrast or one `Contrast`, six
// in all; a layer's value of an input at a slot is its contrast base for that contrast at that scheme, else its
// per_scheme value at that scheme (so its per_scheme value applies under every contrast it states no base for), and
// the input's value at the slot in force is that of the last layer whose value of the input applies there (S8: an
// input it leaves out, a reader's, a stand-in's or a port's, a palette suspended or skipped, not counting): a layer with none leaves the earlier
// layers' (S9.3's one-scheme reader, S14's port beside a mapping). A layer's `for_preset` part for the current preset
// is taken after its common bases, slot by slot, as a layer above them (S8). Either SchemeMap may hold one scheme; a
// preset's accent inputs are stated as one group by every layer above it (S9.2), judged over both parts together.
```

**S9.1 Declared inputs per preset:** `accent` (all); `accent_ramp` entries (`windows-11`); on `macos-*` the AppKit colours that follow the
accent or the highlight setting, each read from its `NSColor` class property and each an accent input (ADD-A123):
`highlight` (`selectedTextBackgroundColor`, the selected document text's background, which the highlight setting
gives, as the macOS verifier found: queue #70), `selected_content_background` (`selectedContentBackgroundColor`), `keyboard_focus_indicator`
(`keyboardFocusIndicatorColor`) and `selected_control` (`selectedControlColor`) (`NSColor.h:221`, `:233`, `:240`,
`:243` in the Xcode 26.6 SDK); the probe's accent pass changed all four, setting `AppleAccentColor` alone (run
41006842699, `os-probe-macos-26/accent-red`, in both appearances), while `highlightColor` (`NSColor.h:284`, the colour
`highlightWithLevel:` blends toward) the accent pass leaves unchanged (`os-probe-macos-26/probe.toml:667`, `:741`
against `accent-red/probe.toml`); it is a literal per scheme, no input, provisional until a pass sets an explicit
highlight colour other than the accent's. The effective highlight, `selectedTextBackgroundColor`, did change in that
pass (`probe.toml:635` against `accent-red/probe.toml:635`) (ADD-A125); on `ios-*` the `accent` alone, UIKit's tint: the
roles that are the tint reference `input.accent`, and what else UIKit draws in the tint is stated as measured
derivations over it, from a host pass under the default tint and one under a second tint, pending that second pass
(the unmeasured register's U706; R2.6, ADD-A146; rejected: the tint-dependent roles as declared inputs, values per
style and state every application setting a tint would have to supply); on `material-3` the accent is the seed of
Material's dynamic scheme where a layer above the preset gives it, which the accent-derivation layer's `m3_role`
reads (S9.2), while the preset states Compose's baseline scheme, the one `MaterialTheme` draws with no seed:
`lightColorScheme()` and `darkColorScheme()`, fixed tokens (`androidx@e4d933c9
compose/material3/material3/src/commonMain/kotlin/androidx/compose/material3/ColorScheme.kt:876-877`, `:978-979`;
`tokens/ColorLightTokens.kt`, `tokens/ColorDarkTokens.kt`) that no pinned source derives from a seed, its roles
those sourced literals (`shadow`, which Compose's tokens do not hold, material-web's `md.sys.color` literal,
`material-web@2.5.0 tokens/versions/latest/sass/_md-sys-color.scss:156-159`) and its own `input.accent` the baseline's `primary` at each scheme (`ColorLightTokens.kt:97-98`,
`ColorDarkTokens.kt:97-98`), the colour the baseline accents with, which no role of the preset reads (ADD-A134; U550).
`material-3`'s accent-dependent roles are every keyed role of `md.sys.color` it declares, each a role
material-color-utilities' dynamic scheme defines (`m3_role`'s, S2.2), which its typed sets and global roles
reference; on
`kde-breeze` the inactive input roles `inactive.<set>.<key>` (the colour a set's key takes in an inactive window
before KColorScheme's inactive effects, for every declared set and key) and the scheme inputs, the values of the
scheme file before Plasma applies the accent (the preset's from Breeze's scheme files; the reader's from the file
kdeglobals names, `[General] ColorScheme`; a port's from its own file, S14) (R25.1): `kde_scheme.<set>.<key>` and
`kde_scheme.<set>.inactive.<key>` for every declared set and `KdeSchemeKey`; three lists per scheme, which `kde_accent`
branches on as `applyScheme()` and KColorScheme do (S2.2) and which are no expression operands:
`kde_scheme.groups`, the declared sets the file has a `[Colors:<Set>]` group for; `kde_scheme.inactive_groups`, the
declared sets whose group has an `[Inactive]` group (empty where none has); and `kde_scheme.unset_keys`, the scheme
inputs (`kde_scheme.<set>.<key>`, `.<set>.inactive.<key>`) of the groups the file has that it leaves unset (a set
`groups` does not name has every key unset and is not listed); for a set `inactive_groups` does not name, each
`kde_scheme.<set>.inactive.<key>` is stated `= input.kde_scheme.<set>.<key>`, what KColorScheme reads for a set without
an `[Inactive]` group (`kcolorscheme.cpp:345-351`). A value the file lacks, a whole group's or one key's, is stated as
KColorScheme reads it unset over the file, cited, never left missing: `Header`'s from the file's `[Colors:Window]`,
with KColorScheme's `Header` defaults beneath (`kcolorscheme.cpp:330-333`); another set's from KColorScheme's defaults
for that set (the `default*Colors` tables, `:122-216`); a key an `[Inactive]` group lacks from those same defaults, not
from the set's active value (`:345-357`); the reader states each so, with every other colour key it reads (S9.3's *The
KDE reader's readings*; ADD-A140). So every declared input has a value, the lists, not a missing value, carry
what the file lacks, and `kde_accent` follows `applyScheme()` where it reads an unset key itself (S2.2: in a tinting
scheme it tints such a key as `applyScheme()` does, from the invalid colour it reads). And `kde_scheme.wm.<key>` for the four `KdeWmKey`s (S4.8), what
`applyScheme()` writes into `[WM]` with no accent (`colorsapplicator.cpp:287-309`): the file's `[WM]` key where it
states one, else the default `applyScheme()` takes from KColorScheme over the same file, stated by whoever states
the scheme inputs as an expression over them: `active_background` and `active_foreground` the file's `Header` Normal
background and foreground (`= input.kde_scheme.header.background_normal`, `.foreground_normal`), `inactive_background`
and `inactive_foreground` the Inactive `Header` colours KColorScheme gives over the file, `kde_effects(…, inactive, …)`
as the inactive colour rules apply it (S2.2) over `input.kde_scheme.header.inactive.background_normal` and
`.foreground_normal`, which hold the file's `[Inactive]` values where `inactive_groups` names `Header` and its active
ones where it does not. That is the value `applyScheme()` starts `[WM]` from, unrounded; it writes it, as every colour,
in bytes (`kconfig@6.31.0 src/gui/kconfiggroupgui.cpp:137-145`; the clean-room description `briefs/kde-accent-descriptions.md`, §2.4, §10 step 3), so a `[WM]` keyed role with no
accent is that input's 8-bit rounding: the input itself where it is a file value, its rounding where it is the
`kde_effects` default under inactive effects (`kde_accent_wm.tsv:219` at `kde-accent` 1b42258e, with `#00000000`, a green of
0.1447013 read back as 0.145098; ADD-A142). Breeze's files state all four `[WM]` keys (`breeze@6.8.2
colors/BreezeLight.colors:202-207`, `BreezeDark.colors:205-210`, as `docs/facts/kde/inputs.toml` cites them), so the
preset's `= input.kde_scheme.wm.<key>` is exact. The `kde-breeze` preset's own bases state each role as `applyScheme()` writes it on
Plasma's default path, "Accent color from color scheme" (no `AccentColor`): Breeze's scheme values with no accent
derivation applied, the inactive roles as that path writes them. `kde_accent` applies only when an accent is set:
the reader states the results kdeglobals holds when the user chose one, and the accent-derivation layer (S9.2)
states each accent-dependent role and inactive input role as `= kde_accent(<set>, <key>, <group>)`, and each `[WM]`
keyed role as `= kde_accent_wm(<key>)`, over the accent and the scheme inputs in force (the reader's, a KDE port's,
else Breeze's).

**The KDE reader without its scheme file.** The reader reads kdeglobals as KConfig does, with Plasma's
`kdedefaults/kdeglobals` beneath the user's file (`startplasma.cpp:421-426`, as today's reader does), and its scheme
inputs and scheme-file tokens from the file `[General] ColorScheme` names. Where neither file names a scheme (an empty
value naming none, a recorded reading, S9.3's colours' source), the scheme is Plasma's own default, Breeze Light
(`startplasma.cpp:452`), whose inputs are the preset's. Where the file it names cannot be found or read, the reader takes them from kdeglobals itself, read as the scheme file would be
(its `[Colors:*]` groups and their `[Inactive]` groups, the lists from what kdeglobals has, its `[WM]` group; a key it
lacks as S9.1 and S4.8 state for an unset key, so `tint_factor` is `None` and the title-bar option false), keeps
everything else it read, and reports it: its status is `ReaderStatus::Fallback`, the failure naming the scheme and
the file. Only a kdeglobals the reader cannot read fails the read (`ReaderFailure::Platform`; a first read's failure is
`from_system`'s error, a re-read's keeps the previous reader layer, S8, S16). Weighed: failing the whole read, so that
`set_accent` never derives over anything but the user's scheme file, discards the user's fonts, colours and
conditions, all of which the reader has, to protect one derivation; while kdeglobals holds exactly the colours Plasma
shows, and is Plasma's own output of the scheme it was applied from. What the fallback costs is that a later `set_accent` derives over
those results rather than over the file (a tinting scheme's tint or an accent-coloured title bar already applied
there), which the status tells the application.

**Accent-dependent roles** (`kde-breeze`): the roles `applyScheme()` writes from the accent
(`colorsapplicator.cpp` at v6.8.2), named by scheme key per set (the catalogue's key table gives each key's
`SurfaceRoles` field), the one list the accent-derivation layer states (S9.2) and S12 checks a mapping palette against:

- in every declared set, `foreground_active`, `foreground_link`, `decoration_focus` and `decoration_hover`
  (`:178-218`);
- `Selection`'s `background_normal`, `background_alternate`, `foreground_normal` and `foreground_inactive`
  (`:230-238`);
- `Button`'s `background_alternate` (`:240-245`);
- `Header`'s `background_normal` and `foreground_normal` where the file has a `Header` group (the accent-coloured
  title bar, `:270-278`; without one `Header` reads `Window`'s results, S2.2);
- the four `[WM]` keyed roles `role.@wm_active_background` … `role.@wm_inactive_foreground` (`:320-338`);
- wherever `token.kde.tint_factor` can be `Some` (conservatively, S12), every other key of every declared set
  (`:219-221`).

The inactive input roles, every declared set's and key's, are stated beside them (S9.2), as `applyScheme()` writes
each `[Inactive]` group from the accent while the scheme tints and `Header`'s under the title-bar option where the
file has a `Header` group (`:247-284`). `kde_accent` gives a role the scheme input unchanged where `applyScheme()` changes nothing (a key the
accent does not touch while the scheme does not tint, `Header`'s colours without the title-bar option), so the list's
conditional entries are harmless under a combination where their condition does not hold.

**Accent inputs.** A preset declares which of its inputs follow the accent, `[declare] accent_inputs` (S10, a subset
of `inputs`): the inputs `set_accent` sets and requires, `set_preset` checks an `Accent` against
(`AccentInputsMissing`), a mapping palette must state (S14), an application layer may not state (S12), and every
layer above the preset states as one group (S9.2). On
`kde-breeze` that is `accent` alone: its other inputs are the scheme's, which Plasma's derivation reads (R25.1). On
every other preset it is every declared input, `macos-*`'s `highlight` included: whether or not the user's highlight
follows the accent, an application or palette replacing the accent states the text-selection colour with it, or the
user's selection colour shows beside the application's accent (R2.6).

**S9.2 Setting the accent:** `Theme::set_accent(Some(accent))` sets the preset's accent inputs (S9.1) in the accent
layer's bases (S8), at the slots the `Accent` states them (S9); it requires them as one group (below): at every scheme
at which the `Accent` states any of them it states every one's per-scheme value, and otherwise `set_accent` returns
`Err(AccentInputsMissing)`, naming each that lacks it once (on `adwaita`, `material-3`, `kde-breeze` and `ios-*` the group is the
`accent` alone, so what is refused there is an `accent` contrast base at a scheme where it states no per-scheme
value). A scheme at which the `Accent` states none keeps the layers' beneath, the accent and its derived inputs
together, so an application may set an accent for one scheme (ADD-A132). On `kde-breeze` the accent layer states the `accent` alone, at every
slot as on any preset; Plasma's derivation is the accent-derivation layer's (below; ADD-A132).

**The accent-derivation layer** (`kde-breeze`; ADD-A132). `kde-breeze`'s accent input is the accent alone (S9.1), so
the application's accent, and a reader's or stand-in's common `input.accent`, from another platform too (S9.5), reach
it, while the preset's accent-dependent roles are Plasma's no-accent path, references to the scheme inputs that
follow no `input.accent`. So on `kde-breeze` `Theme` derives one layer directly above the preset, beneath the reader
or stand-in (S8), which at each slot (S9) where a layer above the preset gives the `input.accent` in force, and at no
other, states each accent-dependent role (S9.1's list) and each inactive input role as `= kde_accent(<set>, <key>,
<group>)` and each `[WM]` keyed role (`role.@wm_active_background` …) as `= kde_accent_wm(<key>)` (whether tinting is
on or off: each function gives the untinted value when it is off), and nothing else (no accent input, no scheme input,
no rule); at a slot where the preset's own `input.accent` is in force it states nothing, so the preset's own
statements show there, as without it (an `Accent` or a stand-in's accent for one scheme leaves the other scheme the
preset's). `Theme` derives the layer for the slot in force on every change of the stack and of the slot (`pick`,
`set_contrast` and a reader's re-read among them, S16), its colour bases and inactive input roles that slot's; S12 holds for it,
as for the S8 leave-out, at every slot where it can state its roles: S19.1's build test validates each form `Theme`
can derive over the bundled preset (each set of schemes at which an accent is given, with and without the tinting
roles), and a theme does not check it again (S8; ADD-A147). Its expressions are evaluated at the slot in force over the accent and the scheme inputs in force there
(S8, S9), as bases, so every rule (the preset's inactive
rules, a contrast's) and `active(…)` (S2.2) read them as any base, and every layer above replaces the roles it states
where they apply: at every scheme and contrast the accent in force changes every role Plasma's derivation changes,
never `role.global.accent` alone, what `applyScheme()` gives for that scheme with that accent
(`plasma-workspace@6.8.2 kcms/colors/colorsapplicator.cpp:125-137`):

- the KDE reader: at the scheme it read, its results, which hold the derivation of its accent, replace the layer's;
  at the other, where it states its accent but no results (S9.3), the derivation of its accent over Breeze's inputs
  there shows, as Plasma would apply that scheme with that accent; with no `AccentColor`, the preset's own accent is
  in force at the other scheme, so the layer states nothing there (S9.3);
- another platform's reader, whose roles are in its own `for_preset` part: the derivation over Breeze's inputs at
  both schemes;
- a stand-in: the roles it states replace the layer's, the rest derived (a partial set is the stand-in's choice);
- an application layer stating an accent-dependent role: its role over the layer's, base or rule, as on every
  preset (in ADD-A112's form the `Accent`'s roles won over such a base);
- an application's `Accent`: where its accent is in force, the reader's or stand-in's results and a KDE port's roles
  are left out (S8), so the derivation of the `Accent` over the scheme inputs in force shows (the reader's, the
  port's, else Breeze's), whose stated roles it so replaces, as `set_accent` requires (R25.1);
- a mapping palette, which states every such role, following `input.accent` by reference where it does (S12, S14):
  its roles over the layer's, the `Accent`'s accent reaching them by reference; under a contrast for which it is
  skipped (S8), at a scheme it does not serve, or while it is suspended, the derivation of the accent in force shows,
  as without it;
- a KDE port (S14), which states no accent and leaves the reader's or stand-in's in force (S8; R2.6): at a slot
  where it applies, the accent in force is the `Accent`'s, else the reader's or stand-in's (the KDE reader's
  `AccentColor`, or its `#00000000` at the scheme it read with none; another platform's reader's), else the
  preset's `#00000000`; under either of the first two the layer's roles over the port's scheme inputs show and the
  port's are left out, as Plasma applies a scheme with the user's stored accent (`colorsapplicator.cpp:127-136`, as
  the 0.8.0 plan's KDE measurement cites it), and under the preset's the layer states nothing and the port's
  no-accent roles show (ADD-A142);
- an accent of `#00000000` from a layer above the preset (the KDE reader's on `kde-breeze` at the scheme it read with
  no `AccentColor`, where its results replace the layer's, S9.3, or one an application or a stand-in states): `kde_accent` and `kde_accent_wm` then give `applyScheme()`'s output with no accent over the scheme
  inputs in force (S2.2): `hasAccent` false (`colorsapplicator.cpp:129-137`), every key copied from the file
  (`:225-227`), an `[Inactive]` group tinted toward that accent only where the file sets `TintFactor` (`:154`,
  `:253-255`) and `Header`'s `[Inactive]` the file's `Window` values otherwise (`:256-262`). That is the file's
  no-accent scheme as Plasma writes it, equal to the preset's statements over Breeze's files, which set no
  `TintFactor`, and not the file's raw values in a tinting scheme; the accent run compares both (S17);
- the gate's normal and perturbed runs, whose stand-ins state no accent on `kde-breeze` (S17), meet no slot where it
  states anything, so the preset's facts, references to the scheme inputs, are compared as stated, while the accent
  run's `set_accent` gives it its roles (S17).

Rejected: the layer stating its roles at every slot while any layer above states an accent (a one-scheme `Accent`
sends the other scheme through `kde_accent`'s no-accent branch where the preset's own statements are exact; ADD-A132's
fourth draft); a layer always present on `kde-breeze` (the preset's own statements would never show, nor be compared);
the accent layer stating the roles itself above every layer (it was ADD-A112's form: it must choose per
scheme and contrast between the roles and the accent alone under a mapping, and under a contrast a mapping is skipped
for it can state the roles only as a rule, which overrides the preset's inactive rules, which `active(…)` does not
read, and under which the disabled roles, the inactive `Selection` tint and the `[WM]` roles leave the `Accent`: three
checks in a row found such a case; the layer also lets an application layer's base on such a role win, as on every
preset); deciding per scheme by what the reader's or stand-in's layer states (it misses a
contrast under which a mapping is skipped, and turns the derivation off for every role where a stand-in states one);
deciding by the layer's own preset (S9.5 defines it for a reader only, and at the KDE reader's unread scheme its accent
would sit beside Breeze's no-accent roles); the KDE reader stating its accent at the scheme it read alone (the user's
