accent is lost when the application `pick`s the other scheme, S9.3); the preset stating `= kde_accent(…)` and `=
kde_accent_wm(…)` itself (equal in value at every slot, Breeze's `#00000000` giving the no-accent path, with the S8
leave-out above; it needs no layer, no existence condition and no change of S8's order or of the stack's place indices,
but the preset's expressions would no longer be its facts' references to the scheme inputs, so either the KDE facts are
restated or `generate_preset.py` takes a `kde-breeze` exception, and R2.6's and S9.1's statement of the preset as the
scheme's values with no accent derivation, the maintainer's decision, would change; the layer keeps both as they
are). The layer's own costs: one derived layer in S8's order, whose roles at a slot depend on which layer gives the accent
in force there, and the S8 leave-out, judged per slot the same way.

**On `material-3`** (ADD-A134; ledger queue #161 (2), U550) the layer is the same, in the same place, derived and
validated the same way, at the same slots: where a layer above the preset gives the `input.accent` in force, it states
each of the preset's accent-dependent roles (S9.1: every `md.sys.color` keyed role it declares) as `= m3_role(@<role>)`,
the dynamic scheme of that seed under `token.material`'s variant, version and contrast level, and nothing else; at
a slot where the preset's own accent is in force it states nothing, so Compose's baseline scheme, the preset's
literals, shows. The preset's typed sets and global roles reference the keyed roles, so they follow. Toward the
layers above it, it is `kde-breeze`'s (the bullets above, read with Material's roles and no scheme inputs): a reader's
(the Android reader's, R18, whose roles hold the dynamic scheme the system derived) or a stand-in's stated roles
replace the layer's, and are left out at a slot where a layer above them gives the accent in force (S8); an
application layer's role wins over the layer's, as each role a mapping palette states does, and an `md.sys.color`
role a mapping does not state shows the derivation of the mapping's accent. `kde_accent`'s no-accent branch
has no counterpart, the baseline being the preset's own literals. Rejected: the preset's roles as `= m3_role(@<role>)` with a
seed as its accent (the baseline is no seed's scheme in any pinned source, so a seed would be a value no fact gives,
and its roles would not be Compose's tokens); the baseline literals with no derivation (an `Accent` would change no
role, where Material's look follows its seed, R2.6); `#00000000` as the preset's accent, as `kde-breeze`'s (Plasma
stores that value, Compose none); `m3_role` by a rule under a condition (no selector says which layer gives the
accent, the reason the layer exists, above).

**The accent inputs as one group** (ADD-A132). Every layer above the preset states the current preset's accent inputs
(S9.1), those of its inputs that apply (S8), as one group: at a scheme at which it states any of them, a per-scheme
value or a contrast base, it states every one's per-scheme value. The one exception is a reader whose platform gives
it its values only under the contrast in force: while that is a contrast, it states at such a scheme every one's base
for that contrast and no per-scheme value (the macOS reader while Increase Contrast is on, S9.3's *The macOS
reader's readings*; ADD-A138). So at every slot (S9) a layer gives all of them a value or none, and the accent inputs in force at a slot all come from one layer, the last that gives any there: no
accent mixes with derived inputs of another, at any scheme or contrast (S8, S9.5). The preset, the bottom layer, needs
no check, as nothing beneath it can mix with it. `Theme` checks the group where an application supplies the values,
and refuses a change that breaks it with `Err(AccentInputsMissing)`, naming each accent input that lacks its
per-scheme value where the group needs it, once whatever the schemes (rejected: `Vec<(InputName, Scheme)>`, a public
type changed for a diagnostic the caller reads off its own `Accent`): `set_accent` (the `Accent`), `apply_palette` (the mapping's inputs, S14),
`set_reader_stand_in` (the stand-in's common inputs with its `[for_preset.<id>]` part for the current preset) and
`set_preset` (each of the three under the new preset, S9.5). A reader states its own preset's group so by
construction (S9.3), and an application layer states no accent input (S12). So a stand-in stating `accent` alone is
refused on `macos-*` and `windows-11`: a stand-in there states the derived inputs beside the accent (in its
common bases or a `for_preset` part), or no accent input at all; it is accepted where the group is the `accent`
alone (`ios-*` among them, S9.1; ADD-A146). Weighed: the group per slot
alone, a layer giving all of them a value or none at each slot (it needs a second condition, all or none of the
contrast bases at a scheme where the layer states no per-scheme value, only to admit a group stated under a contrast
alone, which no palette or gate states and only the macOS reader does, by construction, the exception above;
ADD-A138); the check by input name it replaces (an `Accent` or a mapping stating a derived input at one scheme and the
`accent` at both mixes them at the other); every `Accent` required at both schemes, as a mapping is at
its palette's (it removes the one-scheme `Accent`, an application's own choice, and leaves a stand-in's partial
group); the stand-in's `accent` left
out as the reader's is under a preset declaring derived inputs (a silent drop of an application's value, whose
reason, that a reader from another platform cannot state those inputs, does not hold for an application, which can);
an S12 problem on every layer, the reader's included (the reader's layer is the crate's own, and the error the API
already reports for an application's accent serves the same check).

**S9.3 Readers** state each value under the conditions they read it in: base conditions into the reader layer's bases,
other conditions into reader rules (or inputs' per-contrast bases). A reader rule carries the condition
`preset:<its own preset>` (S9.5) unless its patch touches the portable part only, so it is neither validated nor
applied under another preset (S12), as the reader's preset-specific bases are not (the macOS reader's
increased-contrast values of its keyed roles, `label_tertiary`, would otherwise name keys `adwaita` does not declare). A reader that reads both schemes (today's macOS
reader reads both appearances) states each value under the scheme it read it in. A reader that reads only the
system's current scheme, while inputs and colour bases are per scheme (S9, S3.1), states a value the platform
defines independently of the scheme (the accent setting on GNOME, Windows and KDE, which the facts mark so) under
both schemes, so the user's accent
shows when the application `pick`s the other scheme; a scheme-dependent value it states only under the scheme it read,
and the other scheme keeps the value of the layers beneath, the preset's, until the system switches and the reader
reads again (S9: an input is replaced slot by slot). Likewise for a contrast: a reader states an input's base for each
contrast under which its platform gives the input a value of its own, beside its per-scheme value where it reads
one, which would otherwise stand under that contrast over the preset's base for it (S9): the macOS reader states its five inputs'
`contrast.increased` bases from the Aqua and DarkAqua appearances it reads while Increase Contrast is on (MAC-X22;
*The macOS reader's readings*, below; ADD-A138), as the macOS presets state theirs, and whether the Windows reader states the accent's and the ramp's `contrast.high` bases follows the Windows
facts' high-contrast inputs (S22's follow-up). A reader states its own preset's accent inputs as one group (S9.2),
every one at each scheme at which it states any (the macOS reader the five, read under the same appearances; the
Windows reader the accent with its ramp; the GNOME and KDE readers the accent alone); a reader that cannot read one of
its group's per-scheme values at a scheme states none of the group at that scheme, the layers beneath keeping theirs;
one that cannot read one of its bases for a contrast at a scheme states none of the group's bases for that contrast
there, its per-scheme values then standing under that contrast over the layers beneath (as for a platform that gives
none); either reports it (`ReaderStatus::Fallback`, the failure naming the input), never part of the group beside the
preset's rest (ADD-A132; weighed: keeping the portable accent on a preset whose group is the accent alone, where the
Windows reader's unreadable ramp shade costs the user's accent too, needs another S8 leave-out for a rare failure;
dropping the whole group at the scheme for a failure under one contrast would cost the user's accent under every
contrast for no gain where the preset's contrast base follows its default accent (macOS's increased contrast), and
where it does not (a high-contrast theme's colours, if the Windows facts give them) the per-scheme values standing
under that contrast cost what a reader stating no base there costs, for a rare failure). A slot at which the
platform gives the reader no value in the state it reads (AppKit, which resolves its colours under the contrast in
force alone, below) is no failure but a slot the platform gives none at: the reader states nothing there and
reports no `Fallback` for it, as the KDE reader reports none for an absent `AccentColor` (below); `Fallback` stays
for a read that fails (ADD-A138; weighed: `Fallback` there, which the macOS reader would report on every read, so it
would carry no information; a status of its own, an API member for a state the platform is always in). The KDE reader states its results, the `[WM]` fallback references among them (the catalogue's `[WM]`
roles), under the scheme it read only. Its `input.accent` (ADD-A132), read from kdeglobals with Plasma's
`kdedefaults` beneath, as KConfig reads it:
- where `[General] AccentColor` is set and not equal to Qt's `transparent` (`#00000000`, as `applyScheme()` compares
  it, `plasma-workspace@6.8.2 kcms/colors/colorsapplicator.cpp:130`), that colour, in its common bases at both
  schemes, the accent the user chose, which `applyScheme()` writes verbatim into each set's `DecorationFocus`
  (`:178-217`);
- where it is absent or equal to `transparent`, Plasma's default "Accent color from color scheme"
  (`colorssettings.kcfg:12-15`, no failure, no `Fallback`): in its common bases, the scheme's own accent as KDE
  publishes it to other toolkits, the palette's `Highlight` (`xdg-desktop-portal-kde@6.8.2 src/settings.cpp:280-284`),
  which is the `Selection` set's `BackgroundNormal` (`kcolorscheme@6.31.0 src/kcolorscheme.cpp:676`), under the scheme
  it read only, a scheme-dependent value; and in its `for_preset.kde-breeze` part `#00000000` at that scheme alone,
  taken after the common bases slot by slot (S9), so on `kde-breeze` the reader's results show at the scheme it read
  and the preset's own statements at the other, where the preset's `#00000000` is in force and the accent-derivation
  layer states nothing (S9.2).
So another preset on KDE shows the accent every KDE application shows, the colour KDE's portal publishes as
`accent-color` (which libadwaita classifies into one of its nine accents, `libadwaita@1.10.0
src/adw-settings-impl-portal.c:123-140`, as the GNOME reader does, below). Weighed: no accent where `AccentColor` is absent (every other preset then shows its own accent, unlike
every application on that desktop); the `Highlight` also where `AccentColor` is set (it is the accent blended at 70 %
over the `View` background, `colorsapplicator.cpp:230-238`, `colorsapplicator.h:45-50`, not the colour the user
chose, which `material-3`'s seed and `adwaita`'s own derivations take); `[Colors:View] DecorationFocus` where
`AccentColor` is absent (today's reader's key, equal to the `Selection` background in Breeze's files,
`BreezeLight.colors` and `BreezeDark.colors` in `kcolorscheme@6.31.0 src/color-schemes/`, but not what KDE publishes
in a scheme where they differ); `#00000000` in the common bases (S9.5 carries it to `adwaita` and `material-3`, which
would mix and seed from transparent black). The new reads per
platform are the rows of the traceability whose target is a reader read (S20); each is a `reader::<platform>` change.

**The KDE reader's readings** (ADD-A140; ledger queue #180, from the KDE reader's port on `readers-kw`, ce325f32).
Beside its accent (above) and its scheme inputs (S9.1), it states:

  scheme and xdg-desktop-portal-kde publishes as `org.freedesktop.appearance` `color-scheme`: dark where Qt's grey of
  the palette's window colour (`qGray`, an integer weighted mean of its 8-bit channels) is below a fixed threshold,

  palette, `kcolorscheme@6.31.0 src/kcolorscheme.cpp:671`; their source and an unset key, below). Both sources are

  give); the portal first and the test after it (the test, and so the clean room, is needed anyway, and the two routes

  builds the palette (`khintssettings.cpp:445-446`); where it has none, from the file plasma-integration takes
  instead, the colours of the look-and-feel package `[KDE] LookAndFeelPackage` names (`org.kde.breeze.desktop` by

  Each candidate is found as the scheme file is (below): the first data directory where it is a file, and a package
  or scheme name that is not one plain path component naming no file, so the next candidate is taken, as for one not
  found (a recorded inexactness where Qt's `locate` would join the name's components, `qstandardpaths.cpp:453-462`:
  the reader reads no file outside the directories it names); an empty name is read as none named, so the default
  package is taken, and no scheme file, as S9.1 then names none (the merged reading, a recorded one: S4.8
  reads an empty bool, number or colour as a present value, and whether KConfig's string read gives the default for
  an empty value is the clean room's question, D10). Where none is found, the colours are an empty file's, every key
  KColorScheme's default (below), with no `Fallback`: nothing failed, and those defaults are Breeze Light's
  (`kcolorscheme.cpp:119-120`; one row aside, below), the last candidate's scheme, as where the platform gives no
  value (ADD-A138). Where the one found cannot be read, that is no reason to look further (Qt locates by existence):
  the colours are an empty file's and the status is `ReaderStatus::Fallback`, the failure naming the file, as for the
  unreadable scheme file (S9.1; where both fail, the scheme file's failure, which the reader reads first, S1's first
  failure) (ADD-A145; a140-left's unstated cases).
  Both are recorded readings until the clean room's description of plasma-integration's palette where no file is
  found or the one found cannot be read (`khintssettings.cpp:445-466`, D10) states what Plasma's applications draw
  there; a different answer takes a spec row. Rejected: kdeglobals whatever it holds (without a `[Colors:View]` group
  Plasma's applications draw another file's colours), as the stand-in for an unreadable file too; a `Fallback` where
  none is found (nothing failed, and on a system with no colour files every read would report one, carrying nothing,
  ADD-A138); no `Fallback` for an unreadable file (a read failed, and the application would learn nothing of it,

  locates); failing the read (the fonts, conditions and accent the reader has would be lost for one file's colours).

  `token.motion.speed_factor` under `for_preset.kde-breeze` (K3.30), another value unread.
- the icon sizes (K3.63, K1.158) under `for_preset.kde-breeze`: the icon theme's `index.theme` `[Icon Theme]` keys the
  facts read, `ToolbarDefault` into `token.icons.sizes.toolbar`, `MainToolbarDefault` into `keyed.main_toolbar`,
  `SmallDefault` into `small`, `DesktopDefault` into `large`, `DialogDefault` into `dialog` and `PanelDefault` into
  `panel` (`docs/facts/kde/tokens.toml:8156-9097`); a key the theme omits, or one KConfig does not read as an integer,
  is KIconTheme's own default for its group (`kiconthemes@6.31.0 src/kicontheme.cpp:160-167`, the keys read over them
  at `:469-472`), and a whole number not above zero is not stated. The six defaults are cited on the KDE
  `token.icons.sizes` facts as the KDE lane cites KColorScheme's rows on the scheme inputs' (above; a KDE facts
  follow-up), the reader's constants citing them, which it states once they land. The theme is the one kdeglobals'
  `[Icons] Theme` names, its `index.theme` found under `icons/<theme>/` in the data directories as KIconTheme finds
  it (`:382`, `:395-405`). Where kdeglobals has no such key, KIconTheme's default for it is `breeze` (`:686`), whose
  sizes are the preset's facts, so the reader states no size and the preset's show; where the value is empty, is not
  one plain path component, or names a theme whose `index.theme` is found in none of those directories, it states
  none either, with no `Fallback`, nothing having been read (ADD-A146: the port's rule, stated). Rejected: the preset's value for an omitted key (Breeze's `DesktopDefault` is not KIconTheme's Desktop default,
  `breeze-icons@6.31.0 icons/commonthemeinfo.theme.in:8` against `kicontheme.cpp:161`, so a theme without the key
  would show Breeze's size where KDE draws its default); the defaults dropped as no fact holds them (the port; the
  pinned source states them, so facts can).
- no font DPI (`font_dpi: None`) on any session (S9.4; K3.46; ADD-A146). Off X11, Qt's Wayland screen gives the
  logical DPI `kde-breeze`'s `token.text.font_dpi` states unless `QT_WAYLAND_FORCE_DPI` is set (`qtbase@6.12.0
  src/plugins/platforms/wayland/qwaylandscreen.cpp:150-160`,
  the preset's fact, `docs/facts/kde/tokens.toml:7938-7946`), and the `Xft.dpi` Plasma sets for Xwayland there is the
  Xwayland scale, no font setting (platform-facts' *Font DPI override* and *Scale factor*,
  `docs/facts/imported/kde.toml:701`, `:711`). On an X11 session (`$XDG_SESSION_TYPE` `x11`) Qt's xcb plugin takes
  its logical DPI from `Xft.dpi`, and the preset's where the session sets none (`qtbase@6.12.0
  src/plugins/platforms/xcb/qxcbscreen.cpp:856-876`), and there the toolkits the connectors draw with take their
  scale factor from that same setting, so it has reached every logical pixel, the text's among them, before a reader
  could report it (S9.4's *What the toolkit's scale carries*). Plasma at its pin ships no X11 session either
  (`plasma-workspace@6.8.2 login-sessions/CMakeLists.txt:3-7` installs one session file, into `wayland-sessions`,
  and `startkde/CMakeLists.txt:16` builds `startplasma-wayland` alone), so the case is Plasma 6.7's and older. Not read:
  `kcmfonts`' `forceFontDPI` (Plasma 6.8 removed it with krdb,
  its only reader, `c675077b`, `fe367323`, and on Plasma 6.7 krdb gave it to X11 as `Xft.dpi`; the same row), so
  `kcmfonts` leaves the reader and its watcher; 0.7.0's `xrdb` and `xrandr` steps and its fixed DPI (the preset's
  token states Qt's). Rejected: `Xft.dpi` on an X11 session reported as the font DPI (ADD-A140's reading, parsed by a
  clean-room helper `qxcb_xft_dpi`: with an `Xft.dpi` of 120 the query converts a point size by 120/72 and winit or
  gpui scales the result by 120/96 again, where Qt converts it by 120/72 once; the GNOME reader withholds its factor
  on X11 for that reason, and one rule now serves both readers, S9.4); `forceFontDPI` (on Plasma 6.8 a value left
  over from 6.7, which nothing reads); `QT_WAYLAND_FORCE_DPI` (a variable of each Qt process's own environment, which Plasma
  does not set: none of plasma-workspace, plasma-integration and plasma-desktop names it at its pin, and KWin's own
  platform plugin reads it for KWin's windows, `kwin@6.8.2 src/plugins/qpa/screen.cpp:22-25`; the reader's environment
  is the application's).

**The GNOME reader's readings** (ADD-A135, ADD-A138; ledger queue #171, #173, #179). Its sources are the XDG Settings portal's
`org.freedesktop.appearance` namespace and gsettings, each setting the portal does not give (no session bus, no
answer within the readers' D-Bus deadline, the setting missing) read from gsettings where GNOME keeps it, and a
setting neither gives stated by nothing, so it keeps the no-reader state's value (S16): a flag false, an unread
`overlay-scrolling` among them (not its schema default, which is no reading). It states:
- `input.accent` (GN-3.15), at both schemes in its common bases: the accent libadwaita shows, not the portal's raw
  colour. libadwaita classifies the portal's `accent-color` by no colour distance: it converts it to OKLCH, takes a
  chroma below a fixed cut-off as `slate`, and otherwise picks the accent by fixed hue ranges, eight cuts around the
  circle (`libadwaita@1.10.0 src/adw-accent-color.c:159-199`), each channel narrowed to single precision
  first (`src/adw-settings-impl-portal.c:124-141`); the reader classifies it with `adw_accent_nearest` (S2.2's readers'
  helpers) and states that accent's colour (`src/adw-accent-color.c:52-80`). GNOME's own portal sends the chosen
  accent's colour, which classifies as itself, so the two differ only where another portal backend answers. A
  channel outside `0..=1`, which the portal's specification reads as no accent, states none, so the preset's own
  shows, `adwaita`'s being libadwaita's blue, which libadwaita takes there (`:124-141`); so does a channel that is
  not a number (NaN), which no range holds (ADD-A138). libadwaita's own range check passes a NaN, every comparison
  with it being false (`src/adw-settings-impl-portal.c:132-133`), and its classifier then falls through every cut to
  pink (`src/adw-accent-color.c:171-198`); the reader does not follow it there: a NaN is no colour, that pink is the
  comparisons' fall-through and no reading of one, and `adw_accent_nearest`'s table holds no such row (rejected:
  pink, as libadwaita shows it; a `Fallback`, the portal's read having succeeded).
- the scheme and `contrast_high` from the portal's `color-scheme` and `contrast`, else gsettings'
  `org.gnome.desktop.interface color-scheme` and `org.gnome.desktop.a11y.interface high-contrast` (the scheme light
  where neither gives one, the reader reporting a scheme as every reader does, S8);
  `reduced_motion` from the portal's `reduced-motion`, else `org.gnome.desktop.a11y.interface reduced-motion`
  (GN-3.26); `animations_off` where `org.gnome.desktop.interface enable-animations` is false (GN-3.25), a condition
  of its own beside reduced motion (S7.1); `overlay_scrollbars` from `overlay-scrolling` (GN-1.85); the text-scaling
  factor from `text-scaling-factor`, but on an X11 session a factor of 1 (S9.4's *What the toolkit's scale
  carries*; ADD-A146).
- no font DPI (`font_dpi: None`): GNOME's is a fixed base, `DPI_FALLBACK`, times the text-scaling factor
  (`gnome-settings-daemon@51.1 plugins/xsettings/gsd-xsettings-manager.c:243`, `:582-594`), the factor it already
  reports, so `adwaita`'s
  `token.text.font_dpi` converts its points (S9.4).
- the text-role slots `body` from `org.gnome.desktop.interface font-name` and `monospace` from
  `monospace-font-name`, in its common bases (S9.5; ADD-A138), each string parsed by `pango_font_description` (S2.2's
  readers' helpers); a string naming no family patches no slot. Of the description it keeps the family, the first
  non-empty entry of its comma-separated list (the model's family is one name; the list is GN-FM02†'s, the readers
  unit's), and the size, a point size converted by its own preset's `token.text.font_dpi` (S9.4; it reports no DPI,
  above) and an absolute (`px`) size taken as it is, unpatched where the description sets none or zero; nothing else
  (ADD-A141; the GN-C1 tie-break). GTK 4 takes only the family and the size from `gtk-font-name`, which GNOME sets from
  `font-name`, and never its weight (`gtk@4.24.1 gtk/gtksettings.c:1356-1390`, as the GNOME facts cite it on the card
  button's inherited weight, `docs/facts/gnome/button.toml`), so a label that inherits its weight draws GTK's initial
  `normal` whatever the string names: the body slot's weight, style, width and case stay the preset's, which are GTK's
  CSS, and a patch of them would state a look GTK does not draw. The `monospace` slot takes the same two fields, the
  ones a monospace setting is known to give, until the GNOME facts cite which fields libadwaita takes from
  `monospace-font-name` (its style manager at `libadwaita@1.10.0`), a recorded open item; a field they show it takes is
  added then. Pango's variants, gravity and colour, its `@` variations and its `#` features are not read, as GTK
  applies none of them from the setting, so GN-1.193's question (how a `wght` or `wdth` variation or an `smcp` feature
  meets the description's own weight, width and variant) asks nothing of the reader, the description's weight, width
  and variant being unread too; it stays the readers unit's for a source that applies them. Rejected: ADD-A138's
  weight, style, width and small caps (GTK draws none of them from the setting, the tie-break's card button); the
  whole description stated as the slot's font.
- `token.icons.theme` from `icon-theme` under `for_preset.adwaita`, a freedesktop theme's name being its own
  preset's (S9.5).
Rejected: the portal's raw accent (it is not what any libadwaita application shows where the two differ); a nearest
colour by distance (libadwaita computes none); the schema's defaults for unread keys (a value the system did not
report); the font's family list as one name (Pango's list is a fallback order, GN-FM02†); Pango's other variants
mapped to the nearest `TextCase` (no member means them); `Mixed` stated where the description names no small caps
(it would undo a preset's case transform the font string says nothing of).

**The macOS reader's readings** (ADD-A138; ledger queue #178, from the macOS reader study of 2026-11-08). It resolves
each `NSColor` class property it reads under `NSAppearance appearanceNamed:` of `NSAppearanceNameAqua` (light) and
`NSAppearanceNameDarkAqua` (dark), inside `performAsCurrentDrawingAppearance:` (macOS 11 and later,
`NSAppearance.h:36` at xcode@26.6), converted to sRGB by `colorUsingColorSpace:`, and reads Increase Contrast from
`NSWorkspace.accessibilityDisplayShouldIncreaseContrast`. AppKit resolves both appearances under the contrast in
force: with Increase Contrast on they give the increased-contrast colours, `effectiveAppearance` staying `NSAppearanceNameAqua` (run
41195846264, `os-probe-macos-26/probe.toml` against `increase-contrast-on/probe.toml`: `labelColor` `#000000d8`
and `#000000ff` at `:3085`, the light `controlAccentColor` `#007affff` and `#0040ddff` at `:3139`, `:3234`; macOS
15 alike, run 41006842699, `os-probe-macos-15/probe.toml:612`, `:666` against its `increase-contrast-on/`), the
reads the presets' `contrast_increased` facts cite; and the increased-contrast names give no appearance: "Passing any
of them to appearanceNamed: will return NULL" (`NSAppearance.h:73-74` at xcode@26.6 and xcode@16.4). So the flag
decides where each read goes:
- flag off: `ReaderState.contrast` is `None`; the five accent inputs (S9.1) take the reads as their per-scheme
  values and the roles as the layer's bases, `input.accent` in the common bases and the rest under
  `for_preset.<own>` (S9.5);
- flag on: `ReaderState.contrast` is `Some(Contrast::Increased)`; the five inputs take the reads as their
  `contrast.increased` bases at both schemes, with no per-scheme value (S9.2's exception), placed as with the flag
  off, and the roles as reader rules under `scheme:<s>`, `contrast_increased` and `preset:<own>`.
The slots it does not read are slots the platform gives none at (above), no `Fallback`: with the flag off, the
increased-contrast slots, where an application's `set_contrast(ContrastChoice::Increased)` shows the reader's per-scheme inputs
and the preset's increased-contrast rules on the roles (every layer's bases apply before every layer's rules, S8);
with it on, the slots without a contrast, which only `set_contrast(ContrastChoice::Standard)` reaches (`System`
takes the reader's contrast, S16; ADD-A146), and the high-contrast slots, which only
`set_contrast(ContrastChoice::High)` reaches, at both of which the preset's values show, AppKit giving the reader
no value without the contrast in force and
macOS having no high contrast of its own. Rejected: the increased-contrast appearance names, through their `extern`
statics or as strings (AppKit returns no appearance for them; their documented use,
`bestMatchFromAppearancesWithNames:`, tells only what the flag tells); the preset's increased-contrast values copied
into the slots not read (values not read under their conditions); the reads under the flag stated as per-scheme
values too (values under a condition they were not read in, which would put inputs read under Increase Contrast beside
the preset's normal roles at a high-contrast slot).

Its other reads, as the reader's code has them (ADD-A146; `native-theme/src/macos.rs`'s *Sources*, `system_scheme`
and `read`). The scheme is the global user default `AppleInterfaceStyle`: dark where it reads `Dark`, light
otherwise, the default being absent in light mode (no header of the SDK names the key); its change is the
distributed notification `AppleInterfaceThemeChangedNotification`, which the watcher observes. Weighed against it:
`NSApplication.effectiveAppearance` (`NSApplication.h:345-346` at xcode@26.6), AppKit's on the main thread only, as
the two flags below are, and the application's own `appearance` where it sets one, not the system's setting.
`reduced_motion` and `reduced_transparency` are `NSWorkspace.accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion` and
`accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceTransparency` (`NSAccessibility.h:103`, `:100`), read beside Increase Contrast
(`:94`), the three reported by one notification (`NSWorkspaceAccessibilityDisplayOptionsDidChangeNotification`,
`:121`). The whole read fails (`ReaderFailure::Platform`) on macOS before 11, which lacks
`performAsCurrentDrawingAppearance:` (the reader does not send the selector there), and where AppKit gives neither
the Aqua nor the DarkAqua appearance; a first read's failure is `from_system`'s error and a re-read's keeps the
previous reader layer (S8, S16).

It reads no system effect of a colour (ADD-A146; MAC-X30†). AppKit's rollover, pressed, deep-pressed and disabled
looks are effects applied to a part's own colour (`NSColorSystemEffect`, `colorWithSystemEffect:`, `NSColor.h:68-74`,
`:290` at xcode@26.6), no colour of a role or an input: the parts' `{hover}`, `{pressed}` and `{disabled}` rules
state them, the presets' measured values, as the macOS role facts assume (`docs/facts/macos/roles.toml:9037-9040`).
A reader's layer has no place for them: a state rule needs the part that draws each colour, which the preset's rules
hold, not the reader. Recorded as the route should a user's accent be found to change a state colour the measured
rules do not follow: a keyed role per effect of each colour the facts need, a base the preset states from its
measurements and the reader restates, which the parts' state rules reference, those of an accent input joining
`accent_inputs` (S9.1). Rejected for 0.8.0: that route now (keyed roles and reads for looks the presets' facts
already state per state, with no finding yet that an accent changes one the rules do not follow).

Each target is read from the `NSColor` property its own preset's fact for that target measured (the fact's evidence
names it, `…/probe.toml#macos.colors.<appearance>.<property>`), so on the OS the facts were measured on the
reader's layer equals the preset; where that fact states a reference and no measurement, the reader states nothing
at the target and reads the role referenced. Two of 0.7.0's reads (`2796b26e:native-theme/src/macos.rs`) change so:
- its disabled text, `disabledControlTextColor` (`:131`, `:179`), becomes `tertiaryLabelColor`, which the facts for
  `role.window.disabled.foreground` measure ("Foreground color for disabled static text", `NSColor.h:203`;
  `docs/facts/macos/roles.toml:372-381`);
- its inactive selection, `unemphasizedSelectedContentBackgroundColor` (`:139`, `:174`), states no
  `role.selection.background` under `window_inactive`, which the presets state `= role.@selected_control_secondary`
  from the header's "Alias for +secondarySelectedControlColor" (`NSColor.h:222`; `roles.toml:982-991`): the reader
  reads `secondarySelectedControlColor` into `role.@selected_control_secondary` instead.
At the slice the two macOS presets declared the same 27 keyed roles (`[declare] color_roles`); after the staging
(S6.1) each declares those a value at depth reads and the five the reader states (ADD-A147). Of the 27 the reader's
port states `role.@system_red`, `@system_orange`, `@system_green` and `@system_blue` (0.7.0
read those properties into its status colours, which the status roles on `macos-*` reference as native-theme's
labelled mapping, AppKit declaring none, S3; ADD-A147) and
`role.@selected_control_secondary` (0.7.0's inactive selection, above); `role.@selected_control`, which follows its
input, `input.selected_control` (`selectedControlColor`), which the five accent inputs' group brings (S9.2), waits
with the keyed roles' parking unit (ADD-A147); the other 21 are the readers unit's new reads (M3b; their lines among
MAC-DF01 to MAC-DF05†). Rejected: a literal port of
0.7.0's two reads (a reader's layer differing from its own preset's facts on the OS they were measured on); all 27 at
the slice (the readers unit's work without that unit's trace check, the plan's split); `@selected_control_secondary`
left to the readers unit (the port would drop 0.7.0's inactive selection until then).

`full_keyboard_access` (S7.1) is `NSApplication.sharedApplication.isFullKeyboardAccessEnabled` and
`overlay_scrollbars` `NSScroller.preferredScrollerStyle`, both AppKit's on the main thread only (`NSApplication` and
`NSScroller` are `NSResponder`s, which is `NS_SWIFT_UI_ACTOR`, `NSResponder.h:20` at xcode@26.6, and both bindings
take a `MainThreadMarker`). The reader reads them where `MainThreadMarker::new()` finds the calling thread the main thread,
as 0.7.0 read the scroller style (`2796b26e:native-theme/src/macos.rs:586`), and elsewhere states both unread:
`false`, the no-reader state's value, as the GNOME reader's unread flags are, and no `Fallback`, S16 documenting it.
Rejected: the reads run on the main thread through `dispatch2`'s `run_on_main`, which "will block indefinitely"
where the main thread runs no event loop (dispatch2 0.3.1, `src/main_thread_bound.rs:15-18`), so a read from a
worker the main thread waits on would deadlock; the user default `AppleKeyboardUIMode`, which no SDK header
documents, nor its values, where the header has applications read the property ("accessing this property is fairly
inexpensive", `NSApplication.h:377-380`); `Option<bool>` (every other flag is a `bool`, a condition holds or not
in a resolution, and an application learns the setting by calling on the main thread); `Fallback(Platform(…))`
(its meaning is a source another stood in for, S1, while here the caller's thread decides, which the documentation
names).

The macOS reader patches no text-role slot at the slice (S9.5): macOS has no font setting, its system, monospaced,
menu, tool-tip and title-bar fonts being ones "System Settings has no setting for" (`2796b26e:native-theme/src/macos.rs:21-22`),
so the presets' facts carry its fonts, each style's weight the drawn face's (S2.8's *Weight*). 0.7.0's mapping from
AppKit's weight trait to a CSS weight goes with it: its thresholds have no source and differ from WebKit's, and
ADD-A136 withdrew every conversion from the trait. The user's fonts AppKit keeps (`userFont`, `userFixedPitchFont`,
MAC-I07) are the readers unit's reads, their weights then by S2.8's *Weight*. Rejected: patching `body` and
`monospace` with the system font's family and size (it restates the preset's own facts, and S9.5 would carry Apple's
system font to the other presets as if the user had chosen it); the face's `wght` coordinate read now (it needs
`unsafe` Core Text calls, for a slot the reader does not patch); WebKit's thresholds (withdrawn, ADD-A136).

**The Windows reader's readings** (ADD-A140; ledger queue #180, from the Windows reader's port on `readers-kw`,
32e65ba1). It reads `UISettings` (WinRT), `SPI_GETHIGHCONTRAST` and, under high contrast, `GetSysColor`, and states:
- the scheme dark where `UISettings.GetColorValue(Foreground)` is light by Microsoft's `IsColorLight`, an integer
  weighted sum of the 8-bit channels against a fixed bound, "If the foreground is light, then Dark mode is enabled"
  (*Support Dark and Light themes in Win32 apps*, `ms.date` 2026-06-16, `windows-dev-docs@f54166ed
  hub/apps/desktop/modernize/ui/apply-windows-themes.md:5`, `:75-78`, `:88`), else light; the page's sample code is
  under the repository's MIT licence (`LICENSE-CODE`), so it needs no clean room. The read fails
  (`ReaderFailure::Platform`) only where `UISettings` or that foreground cannot be read, the scheme having no other
  source. Rejected: 0.7.0's BT.601 luminance against a threshold no Microsoft source states
  (`2796b26e:native-theme/src/windows.rs:118-125`).
- `animations_off` and `reduced_motion` where `UISettings.AnimationsEnabled` is false (W3-37): "Gets whether
  animations are enabled for the user interface" (`winrt-api@4c1e9164
  windows.ui.viewmanagement/uisettings_animationsenabled.md:13`), the property WinUI's controls read to leave their
  animations out (`microsoft-ui-xaml@2.5.1 src/controls/dev/dll/SharedHelpers.cpp:29-33`, called as at
  `src/controls/dev/AnimatedIcon/AnimatedIcon.cpp:432`), a safe call whose change the watcher hears
  (`AnimationsEnabledChanged`, Windows 10 2004, `windows.ui.viewmanagement/uisettings.md:25`).
  `SPI_GETCLIENTAREAANIMATION` "Determines whether animations are enabled or disabled", for content that "can cause
  seizures in users with photo-sensitive epilepsy" (`sdk-api@656e9656
  sdk-api-src/content/winuser/nf-winuser-systemparametersinfow.md:126`, `:128`), is the setting platform-facts names
  Windows' reduced motion (`docs/facts/imported/windows.toml:1414-1415`) and the one 0.7.0 read into its
  `reduce_motion`; the two read the same on the three Windows probe images (`:1889-1890`), though no Microsoft page
  says they are one setting. So Windows has one motion setting, as KDE has its factor (above), and it stands for both
  conditions, which keeps 0.7.0's reduced motion (D13); the desktops with no reader of their own differ, gsettings
  holding two settings there, each its own condition (S16). Rejected: `SPI_GETCLIENTAREAANIMATION` (not what WinUI
  reads, where a property WinUI does read gives the setting; that it is an `unsafe` call whose change the windowless
  watcher does not hear holds of the high-contrast reads too, below, which have no such alternative, ADD-A146); both, a condition
  holding where either is off (two reads of what the probe found one setting); `animations_off` alone (the port:
  reduced motion would never hold on Windows, where 0.7.0 reported it).
- `reduced_transparency` where `UISettings.AdvancedEffectsEnabled` is false (W3-38; the registry's
  `EnableTransparency` not read beside it, the API reporting the same *Transparency effects* setting,
  `docs/facts/imported/windows.toml:1911-1912`); the text-scaling factor `UISettings.TextScaleFactor` where it is
  finite and above zero, else unscaled (S9.4); `Contrast::High` where `SPI_GETHIGHCONTRAST` reports
  `HCF_HIGHCONTRASTON` (W3-35). A setting it cannot read keeps the no-reader state's value, with no `Fallback`, as
  the GNOME reader's unread flags do.
- its accent group as S9.2 and S9.3 state it: `input.accent` in its common bases and the six ramp shades under
  `for_preset.<own>`, at both schemes, the whole group left out with a `Fallback` naming the input where one cannot be
  read; no `contrast.high` bases until the Windows facts' high-contrast inputs decide them (above, S22's follow-up).
- the system colours (W3-35; ADD-A135): under high contrast the eight `GetSysColor` colours as `role.@system_*` in a
  reader rule under `contrast_high` and `preset:<own>`, with no scheme condition: `GetSysColor` has one value per
  index, and WinUI fills its `SystemColor*Color` resources from it with no theme argument
  (`microsoft-ui-xaml@2.5.1 src/dxaml/xcp/components/theming/FrameworkTheming.cpp:145-158`, `:219-232`;
  `src/dxaml/xcp/components/theminginterop/SystemThemingInterop.cpp:202`), a value the platform defines independently
  of the scheme, which S9.3 states under both. Outside high contrast they are not read, WinUI drawing no classic
  system colour there, so those slots are ones the platform gives none at (ADD-A138), no `Fallback`. Rejected: the
  rule under the scheme read as well (after a `pick` of the other scheme under high contrast the preset's placeholders
  would show where WinUI shows the same system colours).
- no watched high contrast (ADD-A146): a change of high contrast, and of the system colours under it, is announced
  by no event the watcher receives, so it shows at the reader's next read, as macOS's Keyboard navigation setting
  does (S7.1). `WM_SETTINGCHANGE` and `WM_SYSCOLORCHANGE` are "sent to all top-level windows" (`win32@ca8274de
  desktop-src/winmsg/wm-settingchange.md:11`, `desktop-src/gdi/wm-syscolorchange.md:11`), of which the watcher has
  none, and `AccessibilitySettings.HighContrastChanged` "never fires" outside UWP, relying on a `CoreWindow` to
  handle `WM_THEMECHANGED` (`WindowsAppSDK@2.5.1 specs/themes/ThemeSettings.md:10-12`). A hidden top-level window on
  the watcher's thread would receive them, as .NET's `SystemEvents` creates one (`:157-159`): `docs/todo.md`'s
  *Theme watcher: OS changes it does not report* holds it with the other window-only sources, for the readers unit;
  0.7.0 did not watch it either, so nothing is lost (D13), and no decision is taken here.
- no text-role slot, no font DPI, no system metric and no icon size, which 0.7.0 read
  (`2796b26e:native-theme/src/windows.rs`: `NONCLIENTMETRICSW`'s message, caption, menu and status fonts into the
  default, title-bar, menu, tooltip and status-bar fonts, `:182-191`, `:584-592`; a font DPI fixed at
  `USER_DEFAULT_SCREEN_DPI`, `:145-152`; `SM_CXVSCROLL`, `SM_CYVTHUMB` and `SM_CXBORDER` into the scrollbar's groove
  width and minimum thumb length and the border width, `:245-256`; `SM_CXSMICON` and `SM_CXICON` into the small and
  large icon sizes, `:508-515`, `:603-607`). Under the 0.8.0 plan's D13 (0.8.0 covers what 0.7.0 covers) none of them
  loses a field: every field 0.8.0's model holds for them resolves on `windows-11` from its facts, and only the
  reading goes:
  - the fonts: the `body` slot (the slice) and the window's title, the menu's, the tooltip's and the status bar's
    text (their units, all 0.8.0's) are WinUI's type ramp in the facts (`TextBlock_themeresources.xaml`,
    `docs/facts/windows/tokens.toml:2316-2490`), which WinUI's controls draw with, while WinUI's source reads none of
    the `NONCLIENTMETRICS` fonts (by search of `microsoft-ui-xaml@2.5.1 src/`), so 0.7.0's read put Win32's
    non-client fonts over WinUI's. Whether `windows-11`'s title is drawn by the system's caption, and so in its font,
    is the window unit's question, whose readers step reads that font if so.
  - the font DPI: 0.7.0's fixed DPI is the preset's `token.text.font_dpi`, `USER_DEFAULT_SCREEN_DPI`
    (`docs/facts/windows/tokens.toml:2498-2505`): the same conversion (S9.4).
  - the system metrics: the scrollbar's sizes (the indicators unit) and the border width (each part's stroke) are
    WinUI's in the facts, and WinUI's source reads none of those metrics (the same search), so nothing reads
    them: the Win32 scroll bar's metrics are another preset's (W1-066, R1.3; ADD-A146).
  - the icon sizes: `token.icons.sizes.small` and `.large` (the slice) are pending on `windows-11` (U516), and 0.8.0
    releases with no pending fact (S17). Where U516's facts state them as the Win32 shell's small and large icon
    metrics, the reader reads those, as 0.7.0 did (`GetSystemMetricsForDpi` at the base DPI, inside `windows.rs`'s
    `unsafe` exception, the 0.8.0 plan's D4), each target read from its own preset's fact's source as ADD-A138 has the
    macOS reader read; where they state WinUI's own sizes, it reads nothing: open on U516 (the Windows facts).
    `SM_CXSMICON` for the title-bar icon is W1-010's, the window unit's readers step.
  Rejected: 0.7.0's reads restored at the slice (they would state Win32's values over the facts' WinUI values, the
  reader's layer differing from its own preset's facts on the OS they were measured on, as ADD-A138 rejects for the
  macOS reader).
- no text-rendering setting (`token.text.rendering`, W3-22): WinUI's text draws with its device context's default
  rendering parameters, which its pinned source neither sets nor reads, so `windows-11` states them from its facts (S4's *No Windows
  rendering read*, ADD-A144; whether a changed DirectWrite setting reaches WinUI's text is open, U702).

**S9.4 Points, then text scaling.** A font size, line height, letter spacing or word spacing stated in points becomes logical pixels first, as
`pt × dpi / 72`, where `dpi` is `ReaderState.font_dpi` where the reader or stand-in reports one (a platform's
font-DPI setting that the toolkit's scale factor does not carry: no reader of 0.8.0's reports one, *What the
toolkit's scale carries*, below; ADD-A146) and otherwise the current
preset's `token.text.font_dpi`, stated per preset from its platform's facts, or by the definition below where the
point is the logical pixel (no number is stated here for the others); one stated in pixels is already logical. Where the platform's point is its logical pixel (AppKit's and UIKit's points, their toolkits'
logical unit, in which they lay out and which the screen's scale turns into device pixels: the iOS host's
`screen.bounds_pt` times `screen.scale` is `screen.native_bounds_px`, `docs/evidence/ios-host/2026-10-30-run-41020880059/ios-host-macos-15/run1/index.toml`,
and S17's quote check reads logical points as px), the preset's `font_dpi` is 72, the one value at which
`pt × dpi / 72` is the identity: a derivation from S1's `Px` and the platform's point, not a measured or a published
number. It is therefore the specification's own value, as a conversion of S17's closed list is the model's own: the
Apple presets state `font_dpi = 72` with this paragraph as its comment, no fact states it, and the gate compares the
resolved token with this definition, so no quote is asked of a source that writes no 72 (ADD-A125). Rejected: a
measured citation (the evidence holds the screen's scale, 3 on the iOS host, never 72); a citation kind of its own
for a value the specification defines (`kind = "definition"`): one route the checkers would follow, but it would let
facts, the platforms' values, hold the model's own, where the exception keeps the facts for platform values and names
its keys (this one, and S4.5's empty `animated_visuals`, ADD-A131); `Absent` on the Apple presets (the macOS reader's
conversion would have no operand, and a portable layer written in points would be refused there alone); an S6.3 mark
under which `Absent` means 72 here (no fact, no checker exception, but `Absent` would carry a value, not its one
meaning, not drawn). The Apple
facts state their sizes in px; a point size a layer states, or one the macOS reader reads (`NSFont`'s points, from
MAC-I07's reads on; it patches no font at the slice, S9.3), converts by 72 to the same number. Validation refuses a DPI, the token's or the reader's, that is not finite and above zero (S12).
A reader states the font sizes it reads in logical pixels, converted by its own platform's DPI (its `font_dpi`, else
its own preset's `token.text.font_dpi`), so they keep their size under any preset it applies them to (S9.5). The
conversion comes before the text scaling, and both before every font-derived length (convert, then scale, then
derive).

**What the toolkit's scale carries** (ADD-A146; one rule for every reader). On an X11 session (`$XDG_SESSION_TYPE`
`x11`) the desktop writes its text setting into the session's font DPI: gnome-settings-daemon writes 96 times the
text-scaling factor times the window scale as the X resource `Xft.dpi` and the XSETTINGS `Xft/DPI`
(`gnome-settings-daemon@51.1 plugins/xsettings/gsd-xsettings-manager.c:243`, `:582-594`, `:666-668`, `:742`,
`:797-798`), and Plasma 6.7 and older gave its forced font DPI to X11 as `Xft.dpi` (S9.3's *The KDE reader's
readings*). The toolkits the connectors draw with take their X11 scale
factor from that DPI over 96: winit from XSETTINGS, else the resource (winit 0.30.13
`src/platform_impl/linux/x11/util/randr.rs:41-53`, `:145-146`), gpui from the resource (gpui-pre-linux 0.3.10
`src/linux/x11/client.rs:2674-2681`), each while its own override is unset (`WINIT_X11_SCALE_FACTOR`,
`GPUI_X11_SCALE_FACTOR`, under which the application owns the scale). That factor multiplies every logical pixel, the
text's too, so the setting is applied before the model resolves anything. A reader therefore reports on an X11
session neither a text-scaling factor nor a font DPI that this DPI holds: the GNOME reader a factor of 1, the KDE
reader no font DPI (S9.3), and the conversion and the scaling here add nothing to what the toolkit has done. Off X11
neither toolkit reads the resource or XSETTINGS (only their `x11` modules do), so a reader reports its setting and
the query applies it. The rule reads the session's type, not the client's backend, which no reader can see: an X11
client under Xwayland on a GNOME Wayland session, or in a session started from a text login, gets the DPI through
its toolkit and the factor from the reader, and draws it twice, the inexactness `docs/todo.md`'s *Font DPI* records.
Rejected: a rule per reader (ADD-A140's: the KDE reader reported on X11, as its font DPI, what the GNOME reader
withheld there as its factor, for one mechanism); the readers reporting on X11 and each connector taking the setting
back out of its toolkit's scale (the connectors do not own that scale, their entry points taking no window, the
ruling the same `docs/todo.md` entry records; the lengths those toolkits scale with the text there, which GTK does
not, are the toolkits' either way).

**Text scaling.** The reader supplies `text_scaling_factor` (1 where the platform scales by the font size
itself, and 1 where a reader reads each text style's size, R10); the query scales font sizes by it before
font-derived lengths, by the preset's `token.text.scaling`: `Linear` (a product); `AndroidNonLinear`, Android 14's
`FontScaleConverter`, which scales large sizes less (MAT-X19): the platform's converter (`frameworks-base@android-17.0.0_r1
core/java/android/content/res/FontScaleConverterFactory.java`, its curves applying from its first table's key less
0.01, `:142`), not Compose's own copy (`androidx.compose.ui.unit.fontscaling`, outside the pinned sparse checkout),
which the text-scaling task (a5de6753) reports to differ from it for font scales from 1.03 to 1.05 (ADD-A135);
`DynamicType`, each text style's size for the
reader's or stand-in's `content_size_category` (`ContentSizeCategory`, S8), to Apple's published table (the curve `uifm_scaled` uses for
lengths); or `WinUi`, WinUI's own curve, which scales small sizes more (below; ADD-A141). A part's font is scaled by the curve of its `TextStyle.scaling_role`, `body`'s when `None`; a reader that
reads each style's size reports the default category. A font size is scaled once, where its own style is resolved: a
`Font.size` stated as an expression over other font sizes (`= mul(token.text.roles.body.font.size, <factor>)`) reads
them converted and not yet scaled, and its result is scaled by its own style's curve (S2.2), so a size derived from
another style's is never scaled twice, and under a non-linear kind it follows its own size's curve, as a platform
scales a size stated in its own scalable unit (Android's sp, UIKit's `UIFontMetrics` over a custom size).
`AndroidNonLinear` and `DynamicType` stand in while `material-3` and `ios-*` have no
reader (R25.15). Under `DynamicType` the factor is not read: the category alone scales (`None` is the default
category), so a factor read on another platform does not reach an `ios-*` preset. Validation refuses a reader's or
stand-in's factor that is not finite and above zero (S12).

A line height follows its kind's rule, part of the kind's implementation and cited there: one stated as an
expression on `font_size` follows the scaled font, and `Auto` is the scaled font's own line spacing, under every kind;
one stated in points or pixels is, under `Linear`, multiplied by the factor (R10); under `AndroidNonLinear`, scaled as
Android scales a line height stated in sp (through the converter as a value of its own, or in proportion to its
font's change), the platform's own rule, read in the value phase from `FontScaleConverter` (MAT-X19) and Compose's
`FontScaling` (`androidx.compose.ui.unit`, `material-3`'s reference, R1.6); under `DynamicType`, the leading Apple's
table states for the style's `scaling_role` at that category (TS-2), the table's own line height, and for a style
whose stated line height differs from the table's at the default category (the tight and loose forms, MAC-TS03†), the
platform's own rule, read in the value phase from the fonts UIKit returns per category
(`preferredFont(forTextStyle:compatibleWith:)`, D-5). The value phase confirms each rule from its cited source.

**The rules as implemented** (ADD-A135; the text-scaling task, a5de6753, 419d2db1). Under `AndroidNonLinear`, a line
height stated in points or pixels keeps its proportion to its font's change above a font scale of 1.05, as Compose
does (`androidx@e4d933c9 compose/ui/ui-text/src/androidMain/kotlin/androidx/compose/ui/text/platform/extensions/SpannableExtensions.android.kt:224-250`),
and at or below it goes through the curve as a value of its own; letter and word spacing go through the curve on
their own. Under `DynamicType`, nothing changes at the default category; elsewhere a font size other than the table's
scales by its `scaling_role`'s row's size at the category over its size at the default category, and a line height
equal to the row's default leading becomes the row's leading at the category; a line height other than the table's,
a spacing stated in points or pixels, and a style whose role has no row have no value away from the default category
until the value phase reads UIKit's rule (D-5). The `dynamic_type` table
serves `ios-26` alone, its HIG snapshot (`hig-typography@2026-02-09`) being pinned to that generation. `ios-13` takes
its rows from a second snapshot of the same page (ADD-A136; ledger queue #176): the HIG Typography page's DocC JSON
as the Web Archive captured it (the `id_` form, as the first) after macOS 15's and iOS 18's release and before the
page switched to describing macOS 26 and iOS 26, the last such capture that holds the tables these functions read, the nearest to the iOS 18 updates the runner
measures (18.5 and 18.6, `docs/facts/sources.toml:1060`; D12); its `sources.toml` entry `describes = ["macOS 15", "iOS 18"]` and serves `macos-monterey` and
`ios-13` (S17). The same snapshot serves `sf_tracking`'s rows for those two (U237, U462). Where its tables equal the
first snapshot's row by row, each row cites both and serves both generations; where one differs, the function
selects its table by an enum operand naming the release, S2.2's rule (for `dynamic_type`, an operand the
`DynamicType` kind carries), a class 2 change made then. Until the capture is fetched and pinned (its URL, date and
SHA-256), the table serves no row to `ios-13`, which S2.2 requires before its release; should no capture in that
window hold the tables, `ios-13`'s rows stay pending under U237 and U462. `check_function_vectors.py`
does not yet count a preset's `token.text.scaling` as calling its curve (a scripts follow-up).

Letter and word spacing follow the line height's rule, as a platform scales tracking stated in its own scalable unit
(Compose's typescale tracking is in sp, MAT-TS2): one stated as an expression on `font_size` (`sf_tracking`, a
multiple of the size) follows the scaled font; one stated in points or pixels is, under `Linear`, multiplied by the
factor; under `AndroidNonLinear`, scaled as Android scales a letter spacing stated in sp, read in the value phase from
Compose's `FontScaling` with the line height's rule; under `DynamicType`, as UIKit's fonts per category give it, read
in the value phase with the leading (D-5). A spacing keeps its sign.

**`WinUi`** (ADD-A141; the hosts facts round, U508). WinUI scales a text element's font size by a curve of its own:
`TextFormatting::GetScaledFontSize` gives `m + max(18 − e·ln(m), 0) × (f − 1)`, `m = max(s, 1)`, for a size `s` in px
above zero at the text scale factor `f` (a size below 1 px scaled from 1 px, `:195`, `:203`), and leaves a size at or
below zero as it is (`microsoft-ui-xaml@2.5.1
src/dxaml/xcp/core/text/common/TextFormatting.cpp:181-204`; the code's `exp(1)` and 18, not its comment's `-2.5 ln
s_i + 15`), so a small size grows more than a large one: the WinUI host's TextBlocks at 150 % grew by 1.59 at 10 px
and 1.05 at 68 px, as the curve's 15.87 and 71.27 px would give (run 42308526155's README; its `text-scale/frames.toml`
and `text-text_scale.png`, which the README says were kept, are not in the evidence repository at the pin, `aeeb1969`,
so the match is unchecked until they are committed from the run's artifact, before any fact cites them). `windows-11`
states `token.text.scaling = "win_ui"`, the Windows reader supplying the factor (`UISettings.TextScaleFactor`,
S9.3). Under `WinUi` the font size alone goes through the curve, the one value WinUI scales: a line height stated in
pixels is not scaled (WinUI lays a `LineHeight` out as set, `src/dxaml/xcp/core/text/TextBlock/TextBlock.cpp:1583-1611`;
`windows-11`'s are `auto`, which follows the scaled font under every kind), and a spacing follows the scaled size
where it is stated on `font_size`, as WinUI's `CharacterSpacing` is thousandths of the scaled size
(`src/dxaml/xcp/core/text/RichTextServices/TextFormatter/lineservicescallbacks.cpp:1459`), and is not scaled where it
is stated in pixels. The curve is a platform function checked as S2.2's are (*Checked against their references*):
its vector table generated by the function's lines compiled unchanged against a stub of `TextFormatting`'s two fields
in a CI tool, its arithmetic as they compute it (an MIT source, which needs no clean room), and checked against the
host's text-scale run once its files are committed. Rejected: `Linear` (at 150 % a 10 px size 15 px where WinUI draws 15.87, a 68 px one 102 px
where WinUI draws 71.27); a sampled table (the curve is in the source).

**S9.5 What a reader states for any preset.** A reader builds its layer in two parts: its common bases, which any
preset takes (`input.accent` and its per-contrast bases, except where S8 leaves them out, below; the conditions,
the keyed ones among them, each holding by its key under any preset that declares it (S7.1; ADD-A146), the
text-scaling factor and the font DPI in its `ReaderState`; and the typed text-role slots it reads, as `Fields` patches
over the style each slot references, their sizes in logical pixels (S9.4), composed lazily in R2.4's order (S2.2), so
the user's fonts reach the parts whose leaves reference the slots and the preset's token rules on the referenced styles still
apply over them), and everything else, its own platform's keyed roles, tokens and inputs, under
`for_preset.<its own preset>`. A reader patches exactly the slots its platform has a setting for (the KDE reader
`body` from `[General] font`, `monospace` from `fixed` and `caption` from `smallestReadableFont`, S9.3's *The KDE
reader's readings*; the GNOME reader `body`
and `monospace`; a reader that reads each style's size, every slot; the macOS reader none at the slice, macOS having no
font setting, S9.3's *The macOS reader's readings*, ADD-A138; the Windows reader none, WinUI drawing its own type
ramp, S9.3's *The Windows reader's readings*, ADD-A140); a slot it does not patch keeps the current preset's style, and a slot that shares
another's references that slot (S4.4), so under any preset the patch on `body` reaches every slot that preset shares
with `body`. Its rules split the same way (S9.3): a rule on the portable part (a text-role slot
read under a condition) applies to any preset, every other rule carries `preset:<its own preset>`, so the portable
part is the same for bases and rules. Its own preset is the one the theme was built with (`from_system`, S16: by the
OS version, or the generation the application names). `set_preset` applies the common part to the new preset and the rest only while its own
preset is current; it is refused (`Err(AccentInputsMissing)`) when the `Accent` the application set, the applied
mapping palette's inputs (S14) or the stand-in's (its common inputs with its part for the new preset) do not state
the accent inputs the new preset declares as one group, or the mapping's per-preset section lacks one at one of the palette's schemes (S9.2, S14;
ADD-A132), and
(`Err(PaletteNotForPreset)`) when the applied palette has neither a port nor a mapping for the new preset (S14). The
reader's `input.accent` is portable only to a preset whose `accent_inputs` is `accent` alone (on `kde-breeze` the
accent-derivation layer then derives Plasma's accent-dependent roles from it, S9.2), or to its own preset:
under another preset that declares derived accent inputs (`windows-11`'s ramp, the AppKit-derived roles),
which no reader from another platform states, `Theme` leaves the reader's accent out (S8), so that preset keeps its own
accent and derived inputs, and nothing mixes.

## S10. Declarations (R2.7)

```toml
[declare]
flavors = ["widgets", "kirigami"]            # first is the default
materials = ["mica", "mica_alt", "acrylic"]
color_roles = ["fill_tertiary", …]            # keyed roles
text_styles = [ … ]
elevation = ["<step>", …]                       # the platform's ramp's names
surface_sets = ["window", "view", …]
conditions = ["@ui_effects", …,                # SystemSetting keys; one only applications read, which no rule
              { key = "@show_sounds", for_applications = true }]   # selects on, is marked (S12, `Theme::system`)
params = { layout = { unit = "px", keys = ["grid_unit", …] }, opacity = { unit = "fraction", keys = [ … ] } }
inputs = ["accent", "accent_ramp.light1", …]
accent_inputs = ["accent", …]                  # the inputs that follow the accent, a subset of `inputs` (S9.1)
# every keyed namespace is declared:
blend_modes = [ … ]
timings = [ … ]                                # motion timing tokens' keys
transition_kinds = { <kind> = { <param> = "<unit>" } }    # with their parameters' units
presentation_kinds = { <kind> = { <param> = "<unit>" } }
presentation_events = [ … ]
container_sizes = { sidebar = [ … ] }           # first is the default
symbol_variants = [ … ]
symbol_scales = [ … ]                          # IconStyle.scale (SF Symbols' named scales)
spec_versions = [ … ]                          # MaterialScheme.spec_version (the versions `m3_role` implements)
icon_state_effects = [ … ]
focus_kinds = [ … ]                            # FocusKind::Keyed (WinUI's reveal)
device_models = [ … ]
material_params = { <key> = "<unit>" }
durations = [ … ]                              # motion durations' keys
icon_contexts = [ … ]
symbolic_colors = [ … ]
drag_cursors = [ … ]
accent_ramp = [ … ]
rendering_engines = [ … ]                      # TextRendering.engine
lcd_filters = [ … ]
schemes = ["light", "dark"]                    # a palette's schemes (S14); a palette states them here only

[declare.widget.button]
variants = ["primary", "destructive", "flat", "@pill", "@fab"]   # @: keyed
later = { variants = ["@pill"] }                           # the platform has them; a later unit states them
                                                           # (below, ADD-A147)
sizes = ["small", "regular", "large"]
densities = ["compact"]
flags = ["@<flag>"]
exclusive = [["disabled", "pressed", "hover"]]              # one group, highest precedence first; the gate checks
                                                           # the order against the state models (S17); a group of
                                                           # some of the widget's elements only names them:
                                                           # { parts = ["<part>", …], flags = [ … ] } (below)
exclusive_variants = [["primary", "flat"]]                # variants an element holds at most one of (below)
recency = { elevation = ["pressed", "focus_visible", "hover"] }   # named recency sets, each in its stated order
                                                           # (below, S7.2); the gate checks them (S17); a set of
                                                           # some elements only, as a group: { parts, flags }
sizes_by_context = [{ context = { scope = "any", widget = "navigation_bar" }, sizes = ["regular"],
                     default_size = "regular" }]           # S11's context selector; the first entry matching
                                                           # applies; its default (below, ADD-A131)
sizes_by_variant = [{ variant = "@fab", sizes = ["small", "regular", "large", "extra_large"], default_size = "regular" }]
                                                           # MAT-N1; its default where it differs (below, ADD-A131)
default_size = "small"                                     # the size of an element that states none (ADD-A60)
available = true                                           # false: the platform has no such control
requires_variants = []                                     # e.g. iOS's checkbox only as `selection`


[declare.flavor.kirigami.widget.button]                   # a flavour's declarations where they differ (R2.7):
sizes = ["regular"]                                        # each key replaces the widget's own under that flavour
default_size = "regular"                                   # stated with `sizes` (below)
variants = ["primary", "@<variant>"]                       # the flavour's own variant set (below)

[declare.flavor.kirigami.component.<key>]                  # likewise for a component (which flavour draws it)
available = true

[declare.widget.spinner]
data = { indicator = ["width", "height"] }                 # element data a part's values read (S8; names below)

[declare.component.rule_editor]                # parts and their fields: the catalogue's, generated (S5.1, S6.1);
available = true                               # here what a widget's declaration states, each key as a widget's
sizes = ["regular"]                            # (S5.1's list: availability, sizes and densities, the default
default_size = "regular"                       # size, ADD-A131, variants, flags, groups, sets, element data),
values = { indent_per_level = "length", presentations = "presentations" }   # and `values`, its values' types,
variants = ["@<variant>"]                                           # in place of a widget's `keys`
flags = ["@<flag>"]
data = { <part> = ["<operand>", …] }           # as a widget's (below; ADD-A146)
recency = { <set> = ["<flag>", "<flag>"] }

[declare.widget.segmented_control]
keys = { image_scaling = ["<key>", …] }        # the keys of a typed widget's `Value<Key>` value, keyed map,
                                               # `Vec<Key>` list or list entries' keys (below)
```

A component value's type names one of these `WidgetValue` members (S1): `"number"`, `"integer"`, `"length"`, `"duration"`,
`"bool"`, `"color"`, `"paint"`, `"timing"`, `"transition"`, `"loop"`, `"glyph"`, `"icon_style"`,
`"scroll_physics"`, `"breakpoints"`, `"presentations"`, `"placement"`, `"sides"` (a length per side); `"enum:<Name>"` for one of the model's public
enums (`"enum:Alignment"`, a shared value type of the catalogue's); and `{ key = ["<k>", …] }` for an enumerated
value of the component's own, a `Value<Key>` whose keys the catalogue entry lists. The other members (a font size,
`Vec<char>`, `Vec<Key>`, `Vec<MenuEntry>`) type typed widgets' values only: no component's entry has such a value.

A `data` list (per part, and `values` for the widget's or the component's values) names what the query reads from `Element.data` and
`Element.metrics` (S8), one entry per operand: an `element.` operand by its name (`width`, `progress`, `char_width`,
`font_underline_offset`, …); `line_spacing`, the own font's line spacing that the `line_height` operand reads under
`auto` (S2.2); `body_font_height`; and another part's font metric as `widget.<part>.<metric>` (`char_width`,
`max_char_width`, `font_x_height`, `font_height`, `font_descent` (ADD-A147), `font_underline_offset`,
`font_underline_thickness`, `font_strikeout_offset`, `font_strikeout_thickness`, `font_size`, `line_height`). The root's inputs
(`element.window_width`, `window_height`, `screen_width`, `screen_height`) need none (S8). The declarations are the
preset's, as every `[declare]` is: an application layer's or a palette's expressions may read the element data a
part's declaration names, and no other (S12), so `data_needs` is the same for every stack over that preset.

A `keys` entry names a typed widget's value and lists every key the value may hold: a `Value<Key>` value's, a keyed
map's (`Vec<(Key, …)>`), a plain key list's (`Vec<Key>`, `input.context_menu_items`) and the keys inside a list's
entries at any depth (`Vec<MenuEntry>`: `window.window_menu_items`' actions and submenus). A flavour's section
(`[declare.flavor.<f>.widget.<w>]`, `[declare.flavor.<f>.component.<key>]`) states only the keys that differ under
that flavour, and each key it states replaces the widget's or component's own while the flavour is in force: its own
sizes, availability, flags, and its own variant set (`variants`, the whole set under that flavour, the variants
every flavour draws included), so a variant only one flavour draws is declared in that flavour's set alone and the
other flavour answers `NotAvailable` for it (S8).

**Later names** (ADD-A147). `later = { variants = […] }` in a widget's or a component's declaration lists the
declared variants the platform has and a unit not yet enabled states: the keyed variants of a unit of depth, a typed
variant the model holds (another entry's Depth line lists it) that this entry's Depth line does not list, and a
typed variant at depth that the preset's state model draws in no combination of the enabled units' names. The
declarations stay the state model's whole, a typed variant the model does not hold yet left out (it has no
spelling). A `later` variant selects nothing and is refused in every layer (S12); the query answers
`NotAvailable(Later)` for it (S8). A size that is no element's default in force while the sizes unit is not enabled
("a size of a unit not enabled"), a declared density while the sizes unit is not enabled ("a density of a unit not
enabled": the densities are the sizes unit's, staged as a size is, S6.1), and a flavour of a unit not enabled keep their
declarations; the query answers `Later` for such a density and, per element, for a size it takes that is not its
default in force, and `set_flavor` refuses such a flavour (S8, S16). An exclusive group or a recency set lists
only flags of the enabled units' names; `flags` lists only the keyed flags, and `[declare] conditions` only the system
settings, that a rule of the enabled units' facts names; a keyed namespace declares only the entries a base states, a
map with none stated empty. **The state model in force:** where the generator, its round trip and the gate read a
state model for what an element can hold, an element takes its default size in force alone while the sizes unit is
not enabled, and no density then, the default flavour's model alone is in force while the flavours unit is not
enabled, and no element holds a variant of a unit not enabled; the declarations stay whole. S12's own combinations (the build test's, and an
added layer's) still add every
declared flavour's atom where a state, variant or flavour atom is named (`complete()`,
`native-theme/src/validate/combos/mod.rs:1838-1846`), a flavour of a unit not enabled included; no rule of a bundled
preset names such a flavour, so the values under it are the default flavour's.

Adding a layer rejects any rule, reference or patch naming something undeclared (S12). Which flags form an
exclusive group comes from the platform's state model (the catalogue names the flags, mapping each platform's own
state names to them); the order of precedence inside a group is a fact, cited from the platform's control code: the
preset states it as the order of its `exclusive` arrays, and the gate checks that order against the state-model data
(S17).

**Groups and sets per element** (ADD-A146). An `exclusive` group or a `recency` set stated as a bare array of flags
applies to every element of the widget, its own element and its *(element)* parts; stated as a table, `{ parts =
["increment", "decrement"], flags = ["disabled", "pressed", "hover"] }`, it applies to the elements `parts` names:
the widget's root part, which stands for the widget's own element, or its *(element)* parts, each once. So a widget
whose elements follow different state models states each on its own elements: WinUI's number box holds the text
box's CommonStates on `stepper`'s `body` and the spin buttons' on `increment` and `decrement` (the catalogue's
`stepper`), where one list for the whole widget drops a text box's hover under a press it never has and a spin
button's under a focus it never has. A component's groups and sets take the same two forms (S5.1). Rejected: such
parts as nested `button` widgets (the catalogue's nested-control route would serve `stepper`, but not a set on some
elements only where they are the widget's own parts, `split_button`'s `primary` and `secondary`); a group or set per
part always (`button`, whose one element is the widget, and every widget whose elements share one model would
restate each list per part).

**A flag the platform clears** (ADD-A141; the MT-C1 and GN-C1 tie-breaks). Where the platform never holds a flag while
another holds, clearing or refusing it (GTK never holds hover, active, focus or a drop on an insensitive widget,
`gtk@4.24.1 gtk/gtkwidget.c:6253-6257`, `:8260-8261`, `:8320-8321`, `:10520-10522`, `gtk/gtkdroptarget.c:204-205`, as
the GN-C1 verifier cites them; `material-3`'s state models leave out a disabled button's hover, press and focus
alike), the two form an exclusive group, the flag that stays first (`["disabled", "hover"]`), not a `not_drawn`
combination: so a connector whose toolkit reports both (one that tracks the pointer over a disabled element) is
answered as the platform draws it,
where `not_drawn` only keeps the gate from the pair and leaves the query applying both flags' rules. Where the other
flags combine among themselves (GTK's and Compose's hover with a press), each pair is a group of its own
(`[["disabled", "hover"], ["disabled", "pressed"], ["disabled", "focus_visible"]]`), so a flag may be in several
groups: the groups apply in their declared order, each over the flags the earlier left, its highest held flag staying
and its others dropped, as the query's drop does. `not_drawn` stays for combinations a connector does not produce or
the platform has no look for (`checked` outside `toggle`, a variant outside its host). Rejected: `not_drawn` for
these pairs (the gate's result, but a look the platform never draws for a connector that reports both); one group of
all of them (`[disabled, pressed, hover]` drops the hover of a pressed button GTK draws hovered).

`recency` names the widget's recency sets (R3, S7.2, ADD-A124), each the flags among which the platform shows the one
set last, as Compose's state layer shows the latest of hover, focus and drag rather than a fixed precedence. A set's
members are a fact cited from the platform's code (the list of interactions it keeps); its stated order is the
tie-break for flags whose order the connector does not report, its first the latest, chosen as the order a connector
that reports none should give and stated in the state models with its reason, as an exclusive group's precedence is
(S17). A flag may be in several sets (Compose's hover is in the state layer's and in the elevation's) and in an
exclusive group too, the drop applying first. A widget's sets apply to the elements they name, to every element of
the widget, its *(element)* parts included, where they name none, as its exclusive groups do (*Groups and sets per
element*, above; ADD-A146), and a flavour's section replaces them as any key. The name is a key
(S1), one set per name in a widget, declared where it is used, so a `latest` term naming a set the widget does not
declare, or one that does not apply to the element its rule's part is queried with, is refused (S12).

`exclusive_variants` lists groups of variants of which an element holds at most one, as the platform's style is one
of them (iOS's `UIButton.Configuration` styles, B-1): an element given two of one
group is answered `NotAvailable(Variant)` (S8), the validation's combinations hold at most one of each group (S12),
and a variant set a state model lists holds at most one of each group (S17). A variant in no group combines with any
other. The gate checks the variant sets the platform draws, which the state model lists (`variant_sets`, or `variant_products` compactly, S17), never
every combination of the declared variants.

`requires_variants` lists the forms the platform draws the widget only as (ADD-A123): an element holding any one of
them is drawn, and one holding none is answered `NotAvailable(Variant)` (S8); an empty list requires none. Each listed
variant is a form the platform draws on its own (iOS's checkbox only as `selection`, Material's link only as
`inline`), so a widget the platform draws in two forms lists both; a form it draws only as two variants together is one
variant of the catalogue, so "all of them" is never needed. Rejected: "all of them", which could not state two forms.

A `sizes_by_variant` entry may state `default_size`, the default size of an element that holds the variant and
states no size, where it differs from the widget's `default_size` (Material's FAB, `regular`, among Expressive buttons
whose default is `small`; MAT-N1, ADD-A121), one of the entry's `sizes`; the first entry, in its written order, whose
variant the element holds gives both the element's sizes and, where it states one, its default (ADD-A131; rejected:
a separate `default_size_by_variant` list, ADD-A121's form, whose lookup could stop at another variant than the sizes'
and which S12 would have to check over every set of variants an element may hold together).

`default_size` is stated wherever `sizes` is not empty and is one of them, in the declarations in force under each
flavour (ADD-A131): the two keys go together, so a flavour's section that states `sizes` states `default_size` with
it where its `sizes` is not empty, and under a flavour whose `sizes` is empty no `default_size` is in force. An
element that states no size is drawn at the size the toolkit draws a control it is not told the size of, its own
