initial value, or the size its container gives it, which is a platform value the facts state like any other (the
state models, S17), or, where the platform draws the element at one size only, that size, stated as its only size
(`sizes`, its variants' other sizes in their `sizes_by_variant` entries); so no element that takes a size is without
one, and S17's combinations, which take one of the sizes the element takes, test it as the default size's. A
`sizes_by_context` entry's `context` is one S11 context selector, the table a `when`'s `context` entries and a state
model's `axes.contexts` use, its keys `scope`, `widget`, `part`, `variants` and `not_variants` (S12 refuses
`states`, `not_states`, `sizes`, `not_sizes` and `surface` there, as the sizes an element takes do not change with
an ancestor's state, size or surface), its `scope` deciding which ancestor matches, and the first entry in written
order whose selector matches applies, as for `sizes_by_variant` (rejected: a `"<widget>.<part>"` string, a
second spelling of a context; a widget's name, 0.8.0's first reading, which names no part and no container variant).
An element takes the sizes of the first `sizes_by_variant` entry whose variant it holds, else the widget's `sizes` (a
variant's entry may name sizes `sizes` does not, the sizes that variant alone takes), less those the first
`sizes_by_context` entry whose selector matches leaves out, no matching context entry removing any (ADD-A131, ledger
queue #108; rejected: the variant's entry alone, which drops the container's restriction, a variant's button in a
toolbar ignoring the toolbar's sizes; the context's entry alone, which drops the variant's, a baseline
`@extended_fab`, drawn at `regular` alone, offered another size in a context; the intersection of each with
`sizes`, under which a variant's entry could only narrow `sizes`, so neither S10's `@fab` above, nor Material's
segmented button groups, whose widget declares no size, nor baseline's one-size `Button` beside its FAB's three
sizes could be stated). Where the element takes sizes outside the context and none inside it, S12 refuses the
declaration; where it takes none either way, no default is needed and none is in force: an
unsized element resolves with no size, and a stated size is answered `NotAvailable(Size)` (S8). An entry may
state `default_size`, the size the container gives an element that states none, where the platform's container sets
it (`macos-tahoe`'s default toolbar, `toolbarStyle` automatic and size mode regular,
`docs/evidence/os-probe/2026-10-30-run-41006842699/os-probe-macos-26/button-pass/probe.toml:49141-49143`, gives the
two button styles placed in it `extra_large`, the probe's `view_*_controlSize_raw` 4, `:49155-49158`, U94;
`sizes_by_context = [{ context = { scope = "any", widget = "toolbar", part = "bar" }, sizes = [ … ], default_size =
"extra_large" }]`), in force before the variant entry's `default_size` and the widget's, as the container sets the size of
the view it holds (ADD-A131); a container that gives a size per variant, or by another ancestor's variant (the window's toolbar
style, U94's question for the macOS lane), is a class 1 change with the fact that needs it, `context` then taking a
conjunction list as `when.context` does (no platform read: AppKit's toolbar gave both measured bezel styles one size;
rejected: the list now, which no fact needs yet). The default in force (the first matching context entry's `default_size`
where it states one, a later matching entry's never applying, else the first matching variant entry's, else the
widget's) is always a size the element takes there, wherever it takes any: a `sizes_by_variant` entry whose `sizes`
is not empty and leaves out `default_size` (or there is none) states its own, and a `sizes_by_context` entry holds the
default in force there (S12). Rejected:
an element with no size of its own where a widget with sizes states no default (its values no fact gives: no
combination tests it, and the only values to write there are another size's, an invented value); S17 testing a
no-size combination (it asks the facts for an element the platform never draws, its size being the toolkit's
initial one); the query answering `NotAvailable(Size)` for it (a portable application would then fail on the
presets that leave the default out alone); a top-level `default_size_by_context` (it would repeat the context
lookup of `sizes_by_context`); context rules restating the larger size's values (they would draw an explicitly sized
element at the container's size too, which no fact says the container overrides). **A pending default** (ADD-A131): a default no source or evidence gives yet, the widget's, a `sizes_by_variant`
entry's or a `sizes_by_context` entry's, is a pending measurement, `default_size = { pending = "U<n>" }` in S17's
state model and listed in the preset's `[pending]` table, the preset stating none there. The default lookup above
stops at it: where it is the first default the lookup reaches for an element, that element has a pending default, not
the next one in the order. Every theme but a synthetic one refuses the preset (S12's missing default size), and a
synthetic theme accepts it, the checks that read that default waived (S17), and answers `NotAvailable(Size)` for an
element that states no size and whose default is pending (S8), the answer rejected above confined to that
doc-hidden route while the row is pending.

## S11. Preset files (TOML)

```toml
[preset]
id = "adwaita"
generation = "libadwaita-1.10"
[declare] …                                    # S10

[inputs.accent]                                # every value below is a placeholder; values come
light = "<colour>"                             # from the facts in the value phase
dark = "<colour>"

[colors.light.surfaces.window]
background = "<colour>"
foreground = "<colour>"
[colors.light.global]
accent = "= input.accent"

[tokens.motion.durations]
button_ms = <n>

[widgets.button.body]
fill = "= surface.background"
corners_px = <n>
corners.curve = "<curve>"

[[rules]]
when = { conditions = ["scheme:dark"] }
target = "button.body"
set = { shadow = "<layers>" }

[[rules]]
when = { states = ["checked", "hover"], variants = ["flat"] }
target = "button.body"
set = { fill.append = ["= alpha(surface.foreground, <fraction>)"] }
```

**Spelling.**

| Model | TOML |
|---|---|
| `Value::Stated(x)` | the value: `"<colour>"`; a plain number under a key with its unit's suffix (`_px`, `_ms`, `_deg`; a `FontSize` takes `_pt` or `_px` by its variant); `true`; a table for a block |
| the key of a field with a unit | one key per field: the suffixed key for every value of a one-unit field (`min_width_px = <n>`, `min_width_px = "= …"`, `"auto"`, `"absent"`); a `FontSize` field takes `<field>_pt` or `<field>_px` for a stated number and the bare name for an expression, `"auto"` or `"absent"` (`line_height = "= mul(font_size, <n>)"`), which carry their own units; a `Radius` corner takes `<corner>_px` for `Radius::Px` (`top_left_px = <n>` or `"= …"`) and the bare name for the other variants (`top_left = { full = { maximum_px = "absent" } }`, `top_left = { concentric = { minimum_px = <n> } }`, `top_left = "follow_part"`, `top_left = "ellipse"`); `corners_px` sets the four corners' `Radius::Px` at once, beside `corners.curve` (S2.4); two keys for one field in one table are otherwise a duplicate key (S12) |
| a text value (`String`: a font family, an icon name) | a TOML string taken as written (`".AppleSystemUIFont"`), compared as S17's quote check compares text (a measured one's `tolerance` 0); in a `Value` field a string starting `=` is an expression, which may only be a reference to a text field (S12 refuses a call), `"absent"` means `Absent` (S6.3 deciding where it is allowed), `"none"` means `None` only in an `Option` field, and `"auto"` is `Auto` only in a `Value<Px>` or `Value<FontSize>` field (S2.2: a length or a line height), so in a `Value<String>` `"auto"` is the text `auto` and `"none"` the text `none` unless the field is an `Option`; a plain `String` (`ThemeIcon.name`, a family list's entries) is always text (ADD-A120, ADD-A123) |
| `Value::Expr(e)` | `"= <expression>"` |
| `Value::Auto` | `"auto"` |
| `Value::Absent` | `"absent"`; a whole part: `absent = true` in its table or a rule's `set`, and `absent = false` for `PartPresence::Present` (S6.3); one table or `set` states at most one presence (`absent = true`, `absent = false` or `drawn_as`), beside any of the part's fields, the one `PartPatch` holding both: fields beside `absent = false` draw the part again with them, and fields beside `absent = true` or `drawn_as` are kept beneath the absence for a later `absent = false` (S6.1, S6.3; ADD-A131) |
| an `Option` that is `None` | `"none"`; an `Option` field or leaf of a field (`Caret.blink_timeout`, `Behavior.key_repeat`, `TextStyle.max_lines`, `PlacementParams.max_visible_items`) is stated like any other, so left out it is missing (S2.2, S2.11), never a silent `None`; an `Option` inside a list item or an enum variant's payload left out is `None` (`focus_visible_when = { keyboard = {} }`: no timeout); an `Option` of a plain block (`RippleStyle.indication_box`, `Behavior.key_repeat`) is `"none"` or a table holding every field, wherever it is stated, never a `Fields` patch or a reference to the block, its `Value` leaves taking their own forms (a reference, or `"absent"` where S6.3 allows it), a table missing a field refused by the TOML reader as a mistyped value naming the leaf (`LayerError`, S1; S6.1; ADD-A125) |
| a whole `Value` struct block, or a struct bare-block map entry, in a patch | `{ replace = { <the block's table> } }`, the block stated whole (S2.2), accepted only where the type at its position is a struct block's patch: a rule's `set`, a layer's bases above the preset, a `[for_preset.<id>]` part, a keyframe's `patch` wherever the keyframe stands (S2.2); where the type is the block itself (the preset layer's bases outside a keyframe's `patch`, a list's item, inside a `replace`) and on a plain block or a `Value<Paint>` it is an unknown key, which the TOML reader refuses (`LayerError`, S1); `replace` is the table's only key, another beside it refused, and its value a table only, never a reference or `"absent"` (on a `Value` block those are the bare forms; on a struct bare-block entry they are refused, S12); an enum block is spelt whole by its variant with no wrapper; `replace` is reserved, no field or variant named so (ADD-A125) |
| an enum variant | a unit variant is its snake_case name (`"follow_part"`, `"continuous"`); a variant with data is a one-key table, `{ <variant> = <payload> }`: `top_left = { concentric = { minimum_px = <n> } }` (a `Corners` field is a table of its four corners and its curve, S2.4), `shadow = { elevation = "<step>" }`, `timing = { spring = { mass = <n>, … } }` |
| a list | a TOML array; where the platform has none, `[]` with its citation (a list is never `"absent"`, S2.11) |
| a map (`Vec<(K, V)>`) | a TOML table, one key per entry, never a list of pairs: a `Key` (or an enum-keyed map's variant) bare, by S1's key grammar; a key that is text (`per_family`'s font families, `per_language`'s language tags) as written, quoted where TOML does not allow it bare (`"Segoe Fluent Icons" = ["Segoe MDL2 Assets"]`); two keys are one entry exactly where they are equal as TOML keys, that is case-sensitively, so a family is written as its source writes it, and the toolkit's own family matching (fontconfig's ignores case and blanks, `fontconfig@2.18.3 src/fcmatch.c:69-82`) is the connector's (ADD-A123); an entry whose value has a unit (`Value<Ms>`, `Value<Px>`) takes the unit's suffix on its key as a field does (`[tokens.motion.durations] button_ms = <n>`), its path naming it without (`token.motion.durations.button`), while a `Scalar` entry (a keyed param, a material or transition param) and a component's value (`[components.<key>.values]`: `delay = <n>`, `button_gap = <n>`) take none, the number in the unit the declaration names (S10: a `"length"` in px, a `"duration"` in ms; ADD-A146, the catalogue's rule stated here; rejected: `delay_ms`, as a `Value<Ms>` entry spells it: a component value's type is `Value<WidgetValue>`, which names no unit, its declaration does); an empty map `{}` with its citation (in a patch on the map itself, outside a `{ replace = { … } }` and not creating an entry, `{}` is no change, S6.1); in a `Value` (`Font.axes`, `Font.features`) also `"= <reference>"` (ADD-A125) |
| a tuple, a tuple variant | a positional TOML array: `center = [<x>, <y>]` (`Radial.center`, `Conic.center`), `origin = [<x>, <y>]` (`Transform.origin`); a tuple variant is a one-key table holding that array, `timing = { cubic_bezier = [<x1>, <y1>, <x2>, <y2>] }` |
| `input.kde_scheme.groups`, `.inactive_groups`, `.unset_keys` | `[inputs.kde_scheme.groups]`, `[inputs.kde_scheme.inactive_groups]` and `[inputs.kde_scheme.unset_keys]`, each with `light` and `dark`: arrays of surface sets (`["header"]`, or `[]`), and for `unset_keys` of scheme input names (`["kde_scheme.view.foreground_visited"]`, or `[]`) |
| a `PartRef` stated as a value (a keyframe's `part`, S2.7; `Measured::Part`; a fade's `under`; an `IndicationBox.part`, S2.12) | `"<part>"`, a bare name of the parts of the widget whose table it is in, or `"<widget>.<part>"`, which names its widget (a keyframe of a component's loop naming a part of a widget it holds); a bare name where no widget's table is read is mistyped (ADD-A123) |
| a part drawn by another widget | `drawn_as = { widget = "<w>", part = "<p>", variants = [ … ] }` (`part` left out: the whole widget; `part` a bare name of `<w>`'s parts, so the two keys spell one `WidgetOrPart`, S1) |
| a condition | wherever a `Condition` is stated (a `when`'s `conditions` and `not_conditions`, a `BreezeTest`'s and a `ThemeChange::Suspend`'s `conditions`; ADD-A131), `"<name>"` in snake_case (`"window_inactive"`); with a parameter `"<name>:<value>"`: `"scheme:dark"`, `"tiled:left,top"`, `"input:touch"`, `"idiom:pad"`, `"flavor:kirigami"`, `"preset:adwaita"`, `"system_setting:<key>"`, `"container_size:sidebar:<key>"` |
| a rule's target | `"colors"`, `"tokens"`, `"<widget>.<part>"`, `"<widget>.values"`, `"component.<key>.<part>"`, `"component.<key>.values"` |
| a rule's patch | the table `set`; the keys `when`, `target` and `set` are the rule's own |
| an input's bases | `[inputs.<name>]` with `light`, `dark` or both (the per-scheme value; a preset states both but a listed scheme, S17), and the per-contrast bases `[inputs.<name>.contrast.increased]`, `[inputs.<name>.contrast.high]`, each with `light`, `dark` or both, a scheme a contrast table leaves out taking the per-scheme value there (S9; ADD-A132) |
| a path pending in a preset (S17) | `[pending]`, one entry per path, its TOML path quoted and its register id: `"tokens.behavior.touch.delay_ms" = "U151"`, or, where the path's pending facts (or a state model's pending `default_size`) that leave it listed carry two or more ids, the list of them, each id once, in any order (one id is always the string, a list of one being mistyped): a field S6.1 sets whole whose leaves are pending under different ids (`"tokens.behavior.key_repeat" = ["<id>", "<id>"]`), or a field whose pending facts differ by combination (`"widgets.button.body.corners.curve" = ["<id>", "<id>"]`, two facts split by `variants` and `not_variants`; ADD-A131), a pending `default_size` by its declaration's path (`"declare.widget.button.sizes_by_variant.@gray.default_size" = "U<n>"`: a `sizes_by_variant` entry's by its variant's name as the segment, `@` included, a `sizes_by_context` entry's by its position, a flavour's under `declare.flavor.<f>.`; S17), a pending presence by its part's path (`"widgets.button.label" = "U122"`, S17), a pending input by its scheme, `"inputs.<name>.<scheme>"` (`"inputs.accent.dark" = "U<n>"`, the last segment the scheme; only a per-scheme value is listed, a pending contrast base standing over its scheme's per-scheme value, S9, S17; ADD-A132), the path as S11 writes its key, unit suffix included, which the reader maps to the model's path (`token.behavior.touch.delay`), the spelling of the problems and of the synthetic values; a preset's only, written by `generate_preset.py`, empty at the release (ADD-A128) |
| one preset's part of a layer | `[for_preset.<id>.…]` (bases naming that preset's keyed names, in an application layer or a palette) |
| widget values, component parts | `[widgets.<widget>.values]`, `[components.<key>.<part>]`, `[components.<key>.values]` |
| a `Breakpoint` (S7.3), an item of a widget's `breakpoints` value | `breakpoints = [{ measured = "window", width = { at_most = <n> }, height = { at_most = <n> }, combine = "any", variant = "bottom_sheet" }]`, among the widget's values or in a `Values` rule's `set`: `measured` by the enum rule (`"allocation"`, `"window"`, `{ part = "<part>" }`, a bare name of the widget's parts); `width` and `height` each a one-key table of the `Comparison`'s snake_case name and the threshold, a number in px or `"= …"` (the key is the comparison, so it takes no unit suffix), one left out where the breakpoint does not test that size; `combine` `"all"` or `"any"`, left out only where fewer than two sizes are tested; `variant` the variant's name, `@` before a keyed one (ADD-A146: the form S10's example showed under `[declare.widget.<w>]`, moved with the value, S7.3) |

`when` keys: `conditions`, `not_conditions`, `context` and `not_context` (arrays of `{ scope = "any" | { nearest =
[...] }` (left out: `"any"`, any ancestor; ADD-A123), widget, part, surface, sizes, not_sizes, variants, not_variants, states, not_states }`; `widget` may be left out to match by
variant alone, and `part`, a bare name of `widget`'s parts, is stated only with it, the two keys spelling one
`WidgetOrPart`, S1), `position` (`{ among, first, last, only, parity, previous, next }`, `among` = `"same"`, `"any"` or a
list of widgets; `previous` and `next` as `{ widget, part, variants, not_variants, states, not_states }`),
`variants`, `not_variants`, `sizes`, `not_sizes`, `densities`, `not_densities`, `size_class` (`{ horizontal,
not_horizontal, vertical, not_vertical }`, each a list), `direction`, `states`, `not_states`, `latest` (a table, one
key per recency set and its flag as the value, `latest = { elevation = "hover" }`: `Selector.latest`, S7.2). A
transition's `from` is a list of flags, `from = ["hover", "focus_visible", "pressed"]`; left out of an entry of a
`transitions` list it is `None`, any state (an `Option` in a list item), and in a single `Value<Transition>` (a
part's `focus.transition`, a component's `"transition"` value) it is stated, `"none"` for any state (S2.11); a
zero-duration transition's `timing = "absent"` (S2.7; ADD-A125). A transition's `engine` is spelt as an enum
block's variant (S6.1): `engine = "gtk_css"`, `"qt_quick"`, `"compose_animatable"`, `"compose_transition"`,
`"compose_shape_morph"` (ADD-A146), `"win_ui"`, `"gtk_switch"`, `"compose_held"`, `{ win_ui_animated_icon = { visual = "accept" } }`,
`{ adw_animation = { replays = false } }`, `{ breeze = { any = ["hover"], none =
["focused", "disabled"], conditions = [] } }`, `{ breeze_tab_bar = { … } }`, every list of a test stated (each empty
on a stated zero), on every transition stated, a stated zero's included; a `focus.transition` states `properties =
[]` (S2.10); `token.icons.animated_visuals` as a map of tables, `animated_visuals.accept = { duration_ms = "= …",
markers = { NormalOnToNormalOff_Start = 0.0, … } }`, each marker named as its source names it (S2.7); the
theme-change token
`{ suspend = { duration_ms = "= …", conditions = ["reduced_motion"] } }` (S4.3; ADD-A126). The
interaction block (S2.12) is spelt as any block: `interaction.state_layer.alpha = "= …"`, `interaction.ripple.color =
"= …"`. Every value carries its fact's citation in a comment, as today
(`scripts/check_preset_citations.py`), except a value the specification itself defines, which carries the defining
section instead (S9.4's `token.text.font_dpi = 72` on `macos-*` and `ios-*`, `# S9.4`; S4.5's
`token.icons.animated_visuals = {}` on every preset but `windows-11`, `# S4.5`, ADD-A131): the citation checkers accept
that comment for that key on those presets alone, `check_preset_citations.py` in the preset and
`check_fact_citations.py`, which then asks no fact for the key (ADD-A125). A value of a labelled mapping (S3) carries
its label first, `# mapping: <the fact's mapping text>`, then its fact's citations, if any, so the preset says which
of its values are native-theme's pairings; `check_preset_citations.py` accepts the label for a key whose fact has
`mapping` and refuses it elsewhere (S17; ADD-A147). Palettes use the same format with `[preset] kind = "palette"` and only
`colors`, `inputs`, `tokens.kde` and colour rules, and a mapping palette's `[palette.sources]` and `[palette.picks]`
(S14), which the loader reads past: each keyed by a stated colour's TOML path (`colors.dark.<…>`,
`for_preset.kde-breeze.<…>`, `inputs.<…>`), every colour literal the file states being in exactly one of them. A
mapping palette states its colour literals in its bases (and `for_preset`), its colour rules only references and
derivations; with them a palette states `[declare] schemes`.

## S12. Validation (R2.8)

Adding a layer (S8) fails with `LayerError` (listing every problem) when:

- a field is missing (S2.2), a preset's listed path included (S17, ADD-A128: a path a layer states is stated, on every
  theme; a listed part is missing unless an application layer's bases state its presence, but on a synthetic theme,
  which draws it, and a listed `default_size` is waived there, ADD-A131), judged
  under each combination in which its part resolves drawn, a `Present` over a part with nothing beneath included
  (S6.3), or `Absent` where not `may_be_absent` (S6.3): among the conditional marks, an `Edge.dash`
  absent on an edge whose `width` and `paint` can be drawn, an `IconStyle.fill` absent, outside an icon-size context
  (S4.5), where `rendering_mode` can be other than `Original`, or a `Glyph.fill` absent where its `stroke` can be
  absent too and its `source` can be other than `SystemControl`, or a `Glyph.size` absent where its `source` can be
  other than `SystemControl`, or a `RippleStyle.color`, `alpha` or `padding` absent where, under some
  combination of the rules, its `effect` is stated (S12's combinations, the merged value checked, not a patch alone);
  the other marks conservatively, following references and rules (S2.4, S2.9, S2.12); on a synthetic theme (S17) a listed path's synthetic value is validated as stated,
  as any layer's value (S17; ADD-A131); a mark of one place does not travel with a reference: a part's `text` whose `fill`, `elision`, `wrap` or `max_lines` can resolve `Absent` from the style or slot it references (a slot referencing a style takes its absence with the mark), a caret part whose width can resolve an absent `token.caret.width`, and a part's icon whose `rendering_mode` can resolve `Absent` from the icon-size context it references are refused (S2.8, S4.2, S4.5; ADD-A130); a declared input (S10's `inputs`) is missing likewise at a slot (S9) at which no layer whose inputs apply there gives it a value, its contrast base for that contrast or its per-scheme value at that scheme (the inputs S8 leaves out, a reader's, a stand-in's or a port's, a palette suspended at that scheme or skipped under that contrast, and another preset's `for_preset` part not counting): its `Problem` the missing field's, one per scheme at which it is missing with no contrast, at `inputs.<name>.<scheme>` (a listed input's too, S17), and, at a scheme where it has a value with no contrast, one per contrast under which it is missing, at `inputs.<name>.contrast.<contrast>.<scheme>` (S11's spelling; a contrast base gives no value with no contrast), so no reference evaluates an input to nothing at any scheme or contrast (ADD-A131, ADD-A132); a table at an `Option` of a plain block that lacks a field is no missing field but the TOML reader's mistyped value naming the leaf (S11), the block being stated whole in one layer, which no other layer completes (ADD-A131);
- a keyframe of a loop stated as a widget's or a component's value leaves its `part` out (`None`): such a loop is on
  no part, so each keyframe names the part it sets (S2.7);
- a name is undeclared (S10), except a palette's typed role or surface set the current preset does not declare,
  which is skipped (S14); or a `Colors` or `Tokens` rule has non-condition selector parts;
- a variant a `later` list holds, or a size, a density or a flavour of a unit not enabled (S10), in a positive or a negative list of a
  selector, a reference or a patch, is refused with a problem of its own: the theme declares the name, and a later
  unit states it (`ProblemKind::Later`, S16's diagnostic enums; S10's *Later names*, ADD-A147);
- a `DrawnAs` names a widget the preset does not make available, a part that widget does not have, or a variant it
  does not declare (S6.1); `DrawnAs` patches form a cycle under some combination (a part drawn as another widget's
  part that is drawn, followed through `DrawnAs`, as the first);
- in TOML, a `context`, `not_context`, `previous`, `next` or `drawn_as` table states `part` without `widget` (S11;
  a `part` its `widget` lacks is an unknown name);
- an axis or feature duplicates a field's route (S2.8): `wght` or `wdth` in `Font.axes`, `wght` in `IconStyle.axes`,
  `smcp` in `Font.features`;
- `Radius::FollowPart` is stated outside a `FocusIndicator.corners`, or in one whose `kind` can be `Underline` (the line follows no outline, S2.10; ADD-A146); a `Stroke.outset` is `Absent` under a combination of the rules in which the stroke's `position` is `Outside`, or stated under one in which it is `Inside` or `Center` (S2.4; ADD-A146); `round_pt` is called outside an expression stated on a `Font.size`, or with an operand that is not a reference to a font size (S2.2; ADD-A131); `kde_accent` is called with group `disabled`, or
  with a set that is not one of KDE's seven colour sets (S2.2); `text_scale` is read where `token.text.scaling` can be
  `DynamicType` (S2.2, S9.4);
- `token.text.font_dpi`, or a reader's or stand-in's `ReaderState.font_dpi` or `text_scaling_factor`, is not finite
  and above zero (S9.4); a `ReaderState.container_sizes` names one container twice (one value at a time, below);
- under a mapping palette the preset shows a colour of its own beside the palette's (S14). On every preset
  (ADD-A146): a `Colors` rule of the current preset that can apply while the palette applies (under any combination
  of conditions but a contrast the palette is skipped under, S8) sets a role the palette's bases state at that scheme
  to a value that, followed through references, reads no role and no input the palette states (a literal; a keyed
  role or an input the palette leaves to the preset), and no colour rule of the palette states that role under every
  combination in which the preset's rule applies. Every layer's bases apply before every layer's rules (S8), so such
  a rule wins over the palette's base: `adwaita`'s sidebar in an inactive window, a literal under `window_inactive`,
  and `macos-*`'s inactive selection, `= role.@selected_control_secondary`, would show the platform's colour in the
  palette's window; a rule that follows the palette passes (`adwaita`'s header, `= role.window.background`;
  `kde-breeze`'s inactive rule where the mapping states the inactive input roles it reads), and a palette's rule
  that keeps its own base is `= active(role.<set>.<role>)` (S2.2, S11). Over a preset whose widgets read keyed colour
  roles: a mapping palette's `[for_preset.<id>]` section for the current preset leaves unstated a keyed colour role a
  value of the preset reads that follows neither the accent nor a role the mapping states (S14's *Keyed roles*;
  ADD-A147). And on `kde-breeze`: a mapping palette
  leaves unstated an accent-dependent role (S9.1's list, its tinting entries wherever the
  preset's `token.kde.tint_factor` can be `Some`) or an inactive input role, which the accent-derivation layer would
  derive over Breeze's scheme inputs, a mapping having none, so an
  inactive window or a title bar would show Breeze's colours under the palette's (S9.2, S14); an
  `input.kde_scheme.groups` or `inactive_groups` list names a set twice or a set the preset does not declare, or an
  `unset_keys` list names an input twice or one that is not a declared `kde_scheme.<set>.<key>` or
  `.<set>.inactive.<key>` input;
- an application layer that is neither a palette nor a reader stand-in states an accent input (S9.1's
  `accent_inputs`, in its bases or a `for_preset` part): the accent is `Theme::set_accent`'s (S9.2), the one route
  that checks the derived inputs and, on `kde-breeze`, has Plasma's derivation replace the user's results (S8, S9.2; a palette and a stand-in state them as one group,
  S9.2's `AccentInputsMissing`);
- a map or table has a duplicate key (two TOML keys for one field included, S11); `Auto` is stated on a field
  marked `auto` neither by the catalogue for that part nor by the core (S6.3); a call is stated on a `Value<bool>`, `Value<Key>`, `Value<String>` or enum field (a

  keyframe's `at` outside `0..=1` or not above the one before it, a keyframe naming a `part`, or a keyframe patch

  a keyframe's patch, a loop's or a `Keyframes` transition's, states `icon.animation`, field by field or in a whole

- a stated number lies outside its type's range: a stated `kirigami_lerp` balance outside `0..=1` (S2.2), a negative
  length where the field cannot be negative (S1), a
  `Fraction` outside `0..=1`, a negative `Material.saturation` (a typo's sign; only a computed result is clamped,
  S2.2);
- an expression mistypes, refers to an unknown name, forms a cycle (through bindings too), or can meet an absent
  operand under any binding and rule it can apply under (a keyframe's field whose value resolves `Absent`, a block, a paint

  under a combination where what it patches resolves `Absent`, as the patch sets or appends nothing there, S2.2,

  exempt the part's `line_height` operand and `widget.<part>.line_height`, each the line spacing under `auto`, and a

  reference can bring `Auto` to a field that does not allow it; a `TextStyle`
  token's expression reads `line_height` while that style's line height can be `Auto` (S2.2);
- an input's expression (S9: a per-scheme value or a contrast base; a scheme input's `= input.…`, an inactive input

  a role's rule reads that reads that role's active value is no cycle (`kde-breeze`'s inactive rule over a port's

  (`ProblemKind::ExpressionCycle`);
- a `widget.<part>` reference names a part of another element than the one its part is queried with (S2.2: an

- an expression names element data its part does not declare in the preset's `[declare]` (S10; an application

  `FollowPart` on a corner whose two sides can have different offsets in either direction (S2.4), or a part states

- a part's `shape` can be stated while its corners' curve can be `Continuous`, or a corner `Ellipse` (S2.4);
- a `Corners` value states `Ellipse` on some of its corners but not all four, or with a `Continuous` curve, or a

- a widget's `recency` set (S10) has fewer than two flags, or names a flag twice or a keyed flag the widget does not
  declare (as a rule's `states` may not, above), or two of a widget's sets that apply to one element order two flags

  under no reported order is one order of the flags, which the gate checks, S17); a `latest` term names a set the queried element's widget does not
  declare or one that does not apply to that element, or a flag that is not a member of it (S7.2; ADD-A124); an

- a `Values` rule patches `breakpoints` and selects, in `variants` or `not_variants`, on a variant a `Breakpoint` of

  the connector evaluates the list before it sets those variants, so the term could never decide which list it
  evaluates; ADD-A146);
- a `Transition.from` is an empty list (it would apply from no state), names a flag twice, or names a keyed flag the
  widget of the element it is queried with does not declare (S2.7; ADD-A124);
- a `StateLayer` transition is stated on a part whose fields lack `interaction` (S2.7, S2.12; ADD-A124);
- an `IndicationBox.part` names a part of another widget than the ripple's (`"<widget>.<part>"`, S11), or a part that

- under some combination of the rules (S12's combinations, the merged value checked, not a patch alone), a
  `Transition.timing` or `PresentationStep.timing` is `Absent` where its `duration` is not a stated zero, but under

  `Transition.duration` is `Absent` but on a spring or under `WinUiAnimatedIcon`;
- a transition's stated timing, followed through references, is not one its engine's code computes (S2.7): under

- a `FocusMove` transition is stated: no member runs one yet, as an engine runs per element part and the move crosses
  two (it is added with X-MO-1's measurement, the catalogue's Open items; ADD-A126);

  `TransitionKind::Keyed` transition names a value engine, or a `WinUiAnimatedIcon` one another kind or a `visual`

  earlier in its own list, in the base or in an earlier rule of its part, can apply under the flags its rule selects

  a `ThemeChange::Suspend.conditions` names a condition whose change is a theme change (`Scheme`,

- an expression nests deeper than 32, or a chain of references is longer than 32;
- `base` or `Append` appears in a layer's bases outside a keyframe's patch (a `Fields` patch is never refused for what

  base's patch for a key that no base before it states (the bases of the layers below and the earlier bases of its
  own layer, a layer's `for_preset` part counting after its common bases for that preset only, checked while that

  where it applies, checked conservatively (below): refused where some combination of the bases and the rules before it

  an entry creates it whole, S17, ADD-A133); a paint map's entry created by an `Append`
  alone has its paint so unset (S6.1; ADD-A131);
- a field that lays the element out (a part's padding, margin, size limits and `touch_target`, widget gaps) or sizes
  its content (`text.font.size`, `text.line_height`, `text.letter_spacing`, `text.word_spacing`, `icon.size`,
  `glyph.size`) can read `element.width` or `element.height`, directly or through `part.`, `widget.`, `values.` or a
  `Full` corner (transitively), unless the element's own part (the widget's root part, or the *(element)* part the
  field's part is queried with, S8) states `min_width` and `max_width` equal (for `element.width`; `min_height` and
  `max_height` for `element.height`) under every combination it can resolve under, a fixed box (S8), or the field is
  a `glyph.size` or `icon.size`, drawn to its box, and the element's own part states that axis's minimum as a length,

- a patch sets a field its part does not have (S2.11);
- a spring has a mass or stiffness not above zero, a negative `damping_ratio` or a `rest_epsilon` not above zero; a cubic
  Bézier has an x outside `0..=1`; a `Steps` timing has no step, or has `jump-none` and fewer than two steps (CSS's
  own constraint: its evaluation divides by the steps less one); a `ThemeChange::Crossfade` or `Suspend` states a

- a spring under a Compose member states a `mass` other than 1 or `clamp` true, which Compose's arithmetic has
  neither of and ignores (S2.7's *How a spring runs*; ADD-A146);
- a token or colour-role expression names an operand only an element has (`element.`, `widget.`, `values.`,
  `part.`, `body_font_height`, and `font_size`, `line_height` outside `TextStyle` tokens) or a colour-role definition names
  `surface.` (S3.3);
- a keyed selector name (a variant, flag, condition, container size or recency set) is declared but no rule selects on it, or a
  declared keyed name no base states (a synthetic layer's base states it, S17, ADD-A133), or a declared event that no `presentations` list uses (a typo's sign); exempt:
  the default flavour, a flavour of a unit not enabled (S6.1), with its `[declare.flavor.<f>]` sections (it cannot be
  asked for, S16, and the clause above refuses any rule naming it; ADD-A147), each container-size set's default, variants named in `requires_variants` and
  `sizes_by_variant`, what a connector sets (a content variant on the widget or *(element)* part its catalogue pair
  names, S8, and breakpoint variants), a `SystemSetting` declared for
  applications to read (`for_applications = true` in `[declare] conditions`, S10; `Theme::system`), and a variant a
  platform preset declares, which the facts gate checks both ways against the platform's state model (S17): a
  misspelt variant in the preset's declarations differs from the state model, which the gate fails, and one in the
  state model is no variant of the catalogue's entry, which `check_facts.py`'s state-model rule refuses, so the
  refusal would catch nothing there and would refuse a variant the platform draws by the rules that apply
  (libadwaita's `@tab_button`, as `icon_only`); every bundled preset is a platform's and no layer above a preset
  declares (S10: an application layer holds no `[declare]`, a palette `schemes` alone), so no declared variant is
  refused as unused, and the refusal stays for the other keyed selector names (ADD-A128; ADD-A146: the clause had
  kept it for an application layer's and a palette's declared variants, which no layer can state);
- a stated number is not finite;
- an `exclusive_variants` group names a variant twice (a variant may be in several groups); a
  `sizes_by_variant` entry names a variant the widget does not declare, states a `default_size` that is not one of its
  `sizes`, or two entries name one variant (S10, ADD-A121, ADD-A131); a widget's or component's declarations in force (the preset's, each flavour's
  section replacing the keys it states, and `default_size` with `sizes`, so a flavour's `sizes = []` leaves none in
  force, S10) have a non-empty `sizes` and no `default_size`, a
  `default_size` that is not one of `sizes`, or a `default_size` where `sizes` is empty; a flavour's section states
  `sizes` without `default_size` where its `sizes` is not empty; a `sizes_by_variant` entry whose `sizes` is not
  empty states no `default_size` and leaves out the widget's (or there is none); for each `sizes_by_variant` entry
  and for no entry, in each `sizes_by_context` entry's context, the element takes sizes outside that context and none
  inside it, or takes some there and the default in force there (S10) is not among them, as S12 does not know which
  variants a platform places in which container; a `sizes_by_context` entry's
  selector states `states`, `not_states`, `sizes`, `not_sizes` or `surface`; a pending default, the widget's or an
  entry's, is the missing default size, but on a synthetic theme, where the checks that read it are waived (S10's *A
  pending default*, S17) (S10, ADD-A131);
- a component's rule or base names a part or field that the catalogue's generated table does not give it, or a
  variant, flag, size or value its declaration does not (S5.1).

**Combinations, conservatively.** Where a check considers "every combination" of conditions and states (absent and
`Auto` operands, a rule's map entry created with a field unset that may not be
`Absent`, the conditional `Absent` marks, a listed field missing where a part resolves drawn, R2.8), it is decided per
combination of rule applicability, not field by field. The check evaluates the query under each assignment of the
selectors' atoms (each condition, state flag, variant, control size, density, direction, size class, position and
context match the rules name) that honours the exclusions below, every rule's and binding's applicability fixed by
that assignment: a rule that applies under it applies and one that does not is skipped, references and rules being
followed as the query follows them. A violation is reported exactly when some such assignment makes the path so
evaluated violate, rules that apply and rules that do not alike.
The exclusions are all the check knows of the atoms: the values of each one-of parametrised condition (`Scheme`,
`Input`, `Idiom`, `DeviceModel`, `Posture`, `Flavor`, `Preset`, and `ContainerSize` per container; one value holds at
a time), the two contrast conditions (`ReaderState.contrast` is one value, S9), the flags of each declared exclusive
group that applies to the element (S10), after the S10 reduction, the latest flag of each recency set that applies to it (at most one, a kept flag, and one exactly
where any flag of the set is kept after the drop, S7.2), the variants of each exclusive variant group (at most one at a time, S10), the one-of selector parts (an element has one control size, one density, one
direction, one size class on each axis and one parity at a time, and each ancestor one control size, which a
`ContextMatch.sizes` tests per ancestor), and the model's own definitions among the atoms: among one `among` set of
siblings, `only` holds exactly when `first` and `last` do, and `first` implies odd parity; `Tiled(e)` implies
`Tiled(e')` for every `e'` whose edges `e` includes; and `Maximized` implies `Tiled` on all four edges (S7.1). Every
other combination is assumed possible, so a preset stating a length `Auto` under `scheme:dark` and a call reading
that length under `scheme:light` passes, as does the `Auto` under `sizes = ["mini"]` with the call under
`sizes = ["regular"]`, and one stating them under two independent conditions fails. Deciding per combination
lets correlated settings pass that a field-by-field approximation would refuse (one rule stating `rendering_mode =
original` with `fill = "absent"`: `fill` can be absent and the mode can be other than `Original`, never together),
so the approximation is not allowed: each check is a small satisfiability problem over one part's rules and the
tokens and roles they read, solved exactly.

**What a change re-checks** (ADD-A147). The checks over combinations of a layer read the stack up to it only as its
flattened values: each layer's bases (its part for the current preset among them) and rules with their selectors,
what it is to the stack and what S8 leaves out of it, the declarations, the preset and whether the reader's accent is
left out. They read no input but through the input cycle check and a palette's KDE mapping check (S14); a reference
to an input is read only as a reference, the input's value unread; a stated string, flag or integer is read only as
stated, its value unread (the flattening's `Unknown`). So after a change they run for
each layer whose stack up to it differs, each layer compared with its inputs set aside (a palette's kept) and the
layers stating nothing else left out, from each form S19.1's build test validates and from the stack, as it was
before the change, up to each of its layers. At every change, each layer above the preset has its own checks (each
value, patch, rule and reference against the current preset's declarations) and the input cycle check over the
stack up to it run, and so do the reader's state, the listed paths and the missing inputs; the preset's own checks
run when it is loaded, except for a bundled preset whose `[pending]` table is empty on S8's trusted route (S19.1). S19.1's build test and the facts gate run every check
of every layer, nothing skipped (R2.8). Rejected: every layer's checks over combinations run at every change, as
before, which runs them over the whole stack where they would read what they read on a stack that passed (the 0.8.0
plan's *The load budget*, line 4).

`Theme::add_layer` validates the layer against the theme and refuses it with the error (R2.5). A rule whose
`Preset` condition excludes the current preset is neither validated nor applied, so one application layer can carry
rules for several presets' keyed names (R2.3).

## S13. Placement (R16)

```rust
pub struct Placement { pub strategy: PlacementStrategy, pub params: PlacementParams }   // a widget value (S1)
pub enum PlacementStrategy { GtkPopover, GtkTooltip, QtMenu, QtTooltip, QtQuickTooltip, KToolTipWidget,
                             QtQuickMenu, QtComboBox, QtDialog, QtCompletionBox, QtWhatsThis,
                             KTextEditorCompletion, KirigamiTextActions,
                             WinUiFlyout, WinUiFlyoutFull, WinUiToolTip, WinUiComboBox, WinUiAutoSuggest,
                             WinUiTeachingTip,
                             AppKitMenu, AppKitPopover, AppKitToolTip, AppKitExpansionTip, AppKitComboList,
                             AppKitSheet, AppKitWindowCenter,
                             MaterialMenu, MaterialTooltip, MaterialScaffoldSlot(ScaffoldSlot),
                             MaterialLevitatedPane, AndroidTextToolbar,
                             UiKitPopover, UiKitMenu, UiKitAlert, UiKitEditMenu,
                             KCommandBar, AppKitContextHelp, WinUiKeyTip, UiKitContextMenu,
                             KirigamiAddonsSearchPopup, KirigamiAddonsOnboardingTip,
                             CenteredInHost, OverlayBottomCenter, BottomSheet,
                             KeyboardAvoid(KeyboardAvoidance) }   // OverlayBottomCenter: AdwToastOverlay's and
                                                                  // Kirigami's toasts (GN-2.12, Q2.50)
pub enum ScaffoldSlot { Fab, Snackbar }
pub enum KeyboardAvoidance { WinUiContentDialog, UiKitAlert, UiKitSheet, WinUiScrollIntoView, AndroidPan,
                             AndroidResize, AndroidInsetsAnimation }
pub struct PlacementParams { pub gap: Value<Px>, pub edge_margin: Sides<Value<Px>>, pub side: PlacementSide,
                             pub align: PlacementAlign,            // side, align and the Sides are returned
                                                                  // physical, mirrored for rtl (S2.4)
                             pub flip: Axes<bool>, pub slide: Axes<bool>, pub width: AnchorWidth,
                             pub over_selected_item: bool, pub max_visible_items: Option<u32>,   // None: no limit
                             pub use_full_screen_height: bool, pub anchor_grow: Sides<Value<Px>>,
                             pub host: HostArea, pub window_edge_margin: Value<Px>,
                             pub handedness: bool }               // the menu drop alignment, set by the preset's
                                                                  // rule under `system_setting:menu_drop_alignment`
                                                                  // (S4.2; Win32 menus; WinUI flyouts to verify, W3-55†)
pub enum PlacementSide { Below, Above, Start, End, AtPointer }
pub enum PlacementAlign { Start, Center, End }
pub enum AnchorWidth { Content, AtLeastAnchor, Anchor }
pub enum HostArea { Window, ClientArea, Overlay }
pub struct PlacementInput { pub anchor: Rect, pub size: Size, pub window: Rect,
                             pub host: Rect,                    // the area `params.host` names (below)
                             pub work_area: Option<Rect>,       // None: the toolkit does not give it
                             pub pointer: Option<Point>,
                             pub selected_item: Option<Rect>,   // relative to the element's origin (below)
                             pub keyboard: Option<Rect>, pub direction: Direction }
pub struct Placed { pub frame: Rect,                            // the element's rect, in the input's space
                    pub side: PlacementSide,                    // the side it ended on, after `flip`
                    pub tip: Option<Point> }                    // where its tail points, in that space; None:
                                                                // the strategy draws none
pub fn place(strategy: &PlacementStrategy, params: &ResolvedPlacementParams, input: &PlacementInput) -> Placed;
// ResolvedPlacementParams: PlacementParams with every Value evaluated, as `values()` returns it (S8)
```

`native_theme::placement`, pure functions, each to its platform's source (cited in its doc comment); the closed
list is the traceability's placement rows, each implemented (R16). `params` are physical as the query returns them
(S2.4), so `place()` does not mirror them again; `direction` is the element's, for what a strategy's source reads of
the direction beyond those parameters.

**The input** (ADD-A146). Every rect and point of a `PlacementInput` is in one coordinate space of the connector's
choosing, its window's or its screen's, in logical pixels with y growing downward, and `place()` answers in that
space: the strategies read differences of the rects only, so either space gives the same placement. `anchor` is the
rect the element is placed against, `size` the element's own, `window` the window's, and `host` the rect of the area
the element is placed in, the one `params.host` names: the window's (then `window` again), its client area (the
window less its title or header bar)
or the overlay the element is presented in (AdwToastOverlay's, GN-2.12), which the connector alone knows; it reads
`params.host`, which it passes, and fills the one rect (rejected: a rect per area, of which a call reads one, the
overlay's an `Option` beside). `work_area` is the screen's work area in the same space, `None` where the toolkit
does not give the window's place on its screen. `selected_item` is the rect, relative to the element's origin, as
the element is not placed yet, of the item a strategy with `over_selected_item` puts over the anchor: the selected
item's, or the first item's where none is selected, which the connector passes as it lays the items out (`place()`
holds no item). `max_visible_items` is the connector's to apply as it sizes the element, `size` being the size with
at most that many items shown: `place()` is given no item's extent. An optional input a strategy needs and lacks is
taken as: no pointer, the anchor's start corner; no selected item (an element with no item), a rect of zero height
along the element's top edge; no keyboard, none shown; no work area, the window's rect.

**The answer** (ADD-A146). `Placed.frame` is the element's rect; `side` the side it ended on, the stated one or its
opposite where `flip` turned it, physical as the parameters are; `tip` the point its tail points from, on the
frame's edge, where the strategy's source computes one with the placement (GtkPopover keeps the final position
after a flip and derives the tail's coordinates from it and the pointing rect, `gtk@4.24.1 gtk/gtkpopover.c:430-444`,
`:1305-1394`), else `None`. So a connector draws a popover's `arrow` part from the answer. Rejected: a bare `Rect`
(each connector would find the side by comparing rects and write the tail's rule again, where R16 has each
strategy written once).

**The keyboard strategies** (ADD-A146). A `KeyboardAvoid` member places what it moves for the on-screen keyboard,
the thing whose `keyboard_avoidance` value states it: `anchor` is that thing's rect before the keyboard shows and
`size` its size, `host` the area it moves in, `selected_item` the focused field's rect in it where the member's
source reads one, `keyboard` the keyboard's rect. `frame` is its rect while the keyboard shows, `anchor`'s where
`keyboard` is `None`; `side` is the stated one and `tip` `None`. By member, each to its source as any strategy:
`WinUiContentDialog` and `UiKitAlert`, the dialog; `UiKitSheet`, the sheet; `AndroidPan`, `AndroidResize` and
`AndroidInsetsAnimation`, the window's content, panned, resized, or moved by the insets animation (its end state:
the motion between is the platform's, the catalogue's *placement strategies*); `WinUiScrollIntoView`, the content
of the focused field's nearest scroll container, its `host` that container's viewport, the area it scrolls in,
which no `HostArea` names. What each computes from them is its source's, cited in its doc comment and checked by its
vectors (below).

**Checked against their references** (ADD-A113): each strategy, in the `placement` module, has a vector table as
S2.2's platform functions do, generated by the reference where one runs (the GTK and Qt containers, Compose's code, a
WinUI host for microsoft-ui-xaml's strategies), and measured where the reference is closed (AppKit, UIKit: anchor,
size and window in, frame out, each with its evidence); `scripts/check_function_vectors.py` covers them.

## S14. Palettes (R19)

A palette is a file in S11's format with `[preset] kind = "palette"`: colour-role bases, input bases, colour rules
and `token.kde`, the one token group it may state (S11), for the schemes its project defines (R19). A bundled
palette is one variant its project publishes (S19.1). Two sources, each stated in the file's header:

- **native-theme's mapping** (the default): each role it covers maps to a colour the project publishes, or to a
  derivation of those (S2.2); the file's `[palette.sources]` table names, for each colour it states, by the colour's
  TOML path, the project's colour by its palette-fact key (`"colors.dark.<…>" = "catppuccin.mocha.base"`, S17, S11),
  and its `[palette.picks]` table names each value picked from a range the project's guide gives, with the guide's
  words. It is the same file on every platform.
- **the project's port** for one platform, where one exists (Catppuccin's and Dracula's KDE colour schemes, R19):
  `Palette::from_port(file, scheme) -> Result<Palette, PortError>` converts a KDE `.colors` file mechanically, and
  that palette is used on `kde-breeze` in place of the mapping. A `.colors` file does not say whether it is light or
  dark, so the caller names its one scheme: each bundled palette states it (Catppuccin Latte light, its other flavours
  and Dracula dark, R19), and an application loading a port names it (no luminance guess). Where the project
  publishes a scheme file per accent (Catppuccin's, one for each flavour and accent, R19), a bundled palette's port
  is the file of its own variant, the flavour with the one accent the palette has (S19.1; ADD-A146).

A palette's bases name typed roles, the `accent` input and the declared inputs of the presets it has sections for; a
typed role or surface set the current preset does not declare is skipped, not refused (S12). **Keyed roles**
(ADD-A147; the 0.8.0 plan's D6, outcome 7; R19): over a preset whose widgets read keyed colour roles, a mapping
reaches them by a stated method, or the palette is not offered over that preset: in its `[for_preset.<id>]`
section it states each keyed colour role the preset's values read that follows nothing the mapping states, each
keyed role mapped once to a colour of the project's vocabulary (or a derivation of those, S2.2), the same for every
variant of the project, its colours named in `[palette.sources]` as the others' are, and the method's table, per
project and preset, reviewed before a palette is bundled over that preset; a palette without that section for such
a preset has no source there and is refused on it (`Err(PaletteNotForPreset)`, below). A keyed role that follows the
accent or another role the mapping states (`material-3`'s, through S9.2's derivation) needs no entry; S12 refuses a
mapping palette whose section for the current preset leaves unstated a keyed colour role a value of the preset reads
that follows neither (S12's palette checks). The method
itself is designed with the palettes (the 0.8.0 plan's M2, task 4). A palette is not offered over a preset whose
widget colours the mapping method cannot reach, measured literals that follow no role (`macos-*`, `ios-*`): a
recorded limit (R19; the 0.8.0 plan's M2 task 4; veto list item 49). Rejected: typed roles alone, the mixed look
recorded (`windows-11`'s button reads 24 keyed colour roles and no typed one, so it would keep WinUI's greys under
the project's colours, the mix of two schemes R19 rejects); the keyed colours picked one by one for the maintainer's
veto (21 picks per palette and scheme for that button alone). A role a mapping states
is the mapping's under every condition it applies in (ADD-A146): where a `Colors` rule of the preset would set that
role there to a value that follows nothing the mapping states (`adwaita`'s inactive window's sidebar, a literal), the
mapping states the role under that condition by a colour rule of its own, conditioned `preset:<id>`, a reference or
a derivation as its rules are (S11: `= active(role.<set>.<role>)` keeps its base), and `apply_palette` and
`set_preset` refuse a mapping that leaves such a rule standing (S12's check, on every preset; the palette run, which
resolves the base conditions, does not see it, S17). On `windows-11` and
`macos-*`, whose accent derivations are not published (R2.6), the mapping states the preset's accent
inputs (S9.1) in a per-preset section (`[for_preset.windows-11.inputs]`), each labelled as native-theme's pick (R19;
on `ios-*` the accent is the one accent input, S9.1, ADD-A146), and
`apply_palette` refuses a mapping that lacks one of the current preset's at one of the palette's schemes (its
per-scheme value there), or that states them otherwise than as one group (S9.2), with `Err(AccentInputsMissing)`, as
`set_accent` does (S9.2; ADD-A132). On `kde-breeze` (S9.1), a mapping states the accent-dependent roles and the inactive input roles itself, in `[for_preset.kde-breeze]`
(no `kde_accent`: a mapping has no scheme inputs, and the preset's would be Breeze's): each accent-dependent role as
the project's colour or by reference to `input.accent` where it follows the accent; each inactive input role as the
project's colour where it publishes an inactive one, else as its own set's active role, `= active(role.<set>.<role>)`,
which is how KColorScheme reads a scheme with no `[Inactive]` group (`kcolorscheme.cpp`), and a mapping is one; and
each `[WM]` keyed role as the project's colour, or as `applyScheme()`'s default takes it from the `Header` set (S9.1):
the active ones by reference to its `Header` background and foreground (`= active(role.header.background)`, `=
active(role.header.foreground)`), the inactive ones as the inactive colour rule computes the `Header` set's
background and foreground, `kde_effects(…, inactive, …)` over its own `input.inactive.header.*` (the catalogue's KDE
inactive rule). One
that leaves such a role to the preset is refused (S12): an inactive window or a title bar would otherwise show
Breeze's colours under the palette's. A KDE port is a scheme file, converted by `applyScheme()`'s rules as Plasma's
default path writes it ("Accent color from color scheme", no accent), the rule the preset follows (S9.1), not as the
raw file reads, so the port shows what Plasma shows for that scheme and an accent set later changes only what
Plasma's derivation changes. It converts to the scheme inputs (`kde_scheme.<set>.<key>` and `.inactive.<key>`, the
file's values, a group or key it lacks as S9.1 states, as KColorScheme reads it unset; `kde_scheme.groups`,
`inactive_groups` and `unset_keys` from the file, a set `inactive_groups` does not name stated as S9.1 says; and
`kde_scheme.wm.*` from its `[WM]` group, or for a key the file lacks the `Header` default S9.1 states); to `token.kde`
(S4.8); to the colour roles as that path writes them, the file's own values with no accent
(`colorsapplicator.cpp:225-226`), and for a group or key it lacks what KColorScheme then reads, as the scheme inputs
hold it (S9.1: Dracula's port, which has no `Header` or `Complementary` group, gets `Window`'s values for `Header`,
`kcolorscheme.cpp:330-333`, and KColorScheme's defaults for `Complementary`); each inactive input role as that path writes it (`:247-284`): for a set the
list names, in a scheme that does not tint, `Header`'s the file's active `Window` value (Plasma 6.8's substitute) and
another set's its `[Inactive]` group's value, and in one that tints, the group as that path writes it: the colours
`kde_accent` gives with the accent `#00000000` over the port's own scheme inputs (S2.2; S9.2's no-accent branch),
computed at conversion and stated as colours, so no second derivation exists beside that function (ADD-A142; rejected:
`= kde_accent(<set>, <key>, inactive)` stated in the port, evaluated over the accent in force: it gives the same colours
wherever the port's roles show, since S8 leaves them out at every slot where the accent-derivation layer states its
roles, and only adds an accent-reading expression to a palette); for a set the list does not name, `= active(role.<set>.<role>)`; and each `[WM]`
keyed role as `applyScheme()`'s no-accent result, the 8-bit rounding of `input.kde_scheme.wm.<key>` (S9.1), the
colour `kde_accent_wm` gives with `#00000000`, computed at conversion and stated as a colour like the tinting
inactive roles (ADD-A142; rejected: `= input.kde_scheme.wm.<key>`, which is half a level off where the file lacks
`[WM]`'s inactive keys and the inactive effects are on). No group or key is required but
one colour group: the file is read as the KDE reader reads a scheme file, its bytes decoded as the reader decodes them
and its lines by KConfig's rules (S9.3's *The KDE reader's readings*: the lines KConfig skips skipped, each colour
entry read as KConfig reads a colour), so a group or key it lacks and a line KConfig skips are converted as Plasma
applies the file, and `from_port` refuses only a file with no `[Colors:<Set>]` group of a declared set (any such
group counts, a subgroup such as `[Colors:Header][Inactive]` included),
`Err(PortError::NoColorGroup)` (S1; ADD-A142). The refusal reads the file's groups themselves, a subgroup counting
for its set, and is no test of `kde_scheme.groups`, which lists the `[Colors:<Set>]` groups (S9.1): a file whose one
colour group is a subgroup is converted (ADD-A144, task T6a's question). Whether KConfig counts a set's own group
as present where only its subgroup holds keys, which decides that list and `Header`'s reading of `Window`'s values
(`kcolorscheme.cpp:330-333`), is the clean room's question (D10), and no fact depends on it: the conversion leaves
the set out of `kde_scheme.groups` there, a recorded reading until the clean room's description states KConfig's;
a different answer takes a spec row. A file the refusal meets (empty, or no colour scheme at all) would convert
to KColorScheme's defaults, Breeze Light's colours under whichever scheme the caller names,
presented as the file's, while no real scheme lacks every colour group; a file with some colour groups, which
KColorScheme completes from its defaults as Plasma applies it, is converted (Dracula's port). Rejected:
`PortError::Parse { line }` for a line KConfig skips (it refuses a file Plasma applies, and needs a second reading of
the format beside the reader's); no error at all (an empty `groups` list is a signal callers would miss); refusing a
file that lacks some colour groups (Plasma applies it). S19.1's build test
validates every bundled port, Dracula's among them. The conversion is one module in every build, on every target,
with no feature, and the KDE reader reads its scheme file and kdeglobals through the same KConfig reading and the
same KColorScheme defaults (S9.1, S9.3), so a port and a reading never read a file differently (ADD-A142): a port applies to `kde-breeze` on whatever platform
the application runs, a palette being no reading of the system (R19), S19.1's build test validates the
bundled ports on every target, and the facts gate, which runs `from_port` in its accent run (S17), runs without
features. Its cost is the INI parser the reader reads KConfig files with on Linux (`configparser`, safe Rust with no
required dependency, MIT or LGPL-3.0) in every build on every target. Rejected: the conversion behind the `kde` feature, or a feature of its own (a bundled
palette would then resolve with its port in one build and its mapping in another, a feature changing a value, and the
facts gate would need the feature on every platform); an own KConfig reader instead of the crate (KConfig's rules
are LGPL code, so a new reader of them goes through the clean room, D10, to save a dependency of some 1,600 lines); the bundled
ports converted ahead of time by a script (two conversions, the script's and `from_port`'s, which an application's own
port still needs). A port states no accent input, and the reader's or stand-in's accent stays in force under it
(S8): R2.6 has a reader's or stand-in's accent, like the application's, derive each accent-dependent role "over the
scheme inputs in force, the reader's or those of a palette from a KDE port", and Plasma applies a scheme with the
user's stored accent (`colorsapplicator.cpp:127-136`, as the 0.8.0 plan's KDE measurement cites it); R19 says so:
under a mapping the user's accent is not applied, and under a KDE port, which states no accent, the reader's accent
stays in force and Plasma's derivation applies over the port's scheme (ADD-A146). So at a slot the port serves, the accent-derivation layer states its roles
over the port's scheme inputs wherever the `Accent`, the reader or the stand-in gives the accent, S8 leaving the
port's roles out there, and where the preset's `#00000000` is in force the port's no-accent roles show (S9.2); an
application wanting the port's own look under a user's accent sets `#00000000` through `set_accent` (S9.2's
`#00000000` bullet). Rejected: the reader's or stand-in's accent left out under a port as under a mapping (R19's
mapping clause read for every palette: the user's accent would vanish whenever an application applies a port,
unlike Plasma, though R2.6 names the port's scheme inputs beneath it). So Plasma's derivation applies over the
port's own scheme when an accent is set (S9.2), and a non-tinting port's inactive title bar is, without the
accent-coloured title bar option, the same with an accent as without, as in Plasma (`kde_accent`'s non-tinting branch
gives `Header` the same `Window` values; under the option, where the file has a `Header` group, the accent tints it,
S2.2).

A `Palette` holds the mapping and the ports it has, per preset (a port carries its preset: a `.colors` file's is
`kde-breeze`); `Palette::with_port(self, port)` adds the ports another palette holds, one replacing another for the
same preset, and is refused where the port's scheme is not one of the palette's (`Err(SchemeNotInPalette)`), so an
application builds a mapping (`from_toml`) with its project's port (`from_port`) as the bundled palettes are built;
`Theme::apply_palette(Some(palette))` adds, as an
application layer that replaces the reader's or stand-in's colours (S8), the port for the current preset where there is one (a KDE port
converts to the `kde_scheme.*` inputs, the colour roles and `token.kde`), else the mapping. The source is chosen per
preset and scheme: where a preset has a port with fewer schemes than the mapping (a one-scheme `.colors` file beside
a two-scheme mapping), the port serves its scheme and the mapping the palette's others, so each scheme has one
source and the palette applies under every scheme it declares; the port's `token.kde` then applies under its scheme
only (a `Tokens` rule under that scheme), the mapping keeping the preset's under the others. A palette that lacks
the scheme in force is refused where the application picked that scheme and suspended where the scheme is followed
(ADD-A146): `apply_palette` is `Err(SchemeNotInPalette)` only while `pick(Some(s))` holds a scheme the palette
lacks, two choices of the application's that contradict; while the scheme is followed (`pick(None)`: the reader's or
the stand-in's, else the one `from_preset` was given, S16) it accepts the palette and suspends it, the theme being
the preset with the reader's values, as when the system scheme changes to one the palette lacks, and the palette
applies when the scheme in force is one it has (R19: it stays chosen, so the application need not watch the scheme
to apply it again); `ResolvedTheme::palette_status()` reports `Applied`, `Suspended` or `SkippedForContrast` (`None`:
no palette). Rejected: refusing it under a followed scheme too (the outcome then depends on the order at start-up:
an application that follows the system and starts in light with a dark-only palette gets an error and no palette,
and must watch the scheme to apply it later, which R19 says it need not); never refusing, a picked scheme
suspending it too (two choices of the application's own, which no system change resolves, where the error says so
at once). A palette carries no icon set. A palette states its schemes in its `[declare] schemes` (S10);
`Theme::pick(Some(s))` of a scheme the applied palette lacks is refused (`Err(SchemeNotInPalette)`), while `pick(None)`, which
follows the system's scheme, suspends the palette while that scheme is one it lacks, as a system change does; a
`set_preset` to a preset whose accent inputs the applied mapping's per-preset section lacks at one of the palette's
schemes is refused (`Err(AccentInputsMissing)`), as `apply_palette` refuses it; a palette that has neither a
mapping nor a port for the current preset (a KDE port alone, on `adwaita`) is refused (`Err(PaletteNotForPreset)`).
The palette's source, port or mapping, is chosen again on every change of the stack, as the accent layer is derived
again (S8), so `set_preset` switches it to the new preset's; a `set_preset` to a preset the applied palette can
serve with neither is refused whole (`Err(PaletteNotForPreset)`, S8), as `apply_palette` refuses it, and the
application removes the palette first (`apply_palette(None)`) to switch. A mapping palette need not state
`token.kde`: the preset's applies. The facts gate checks each mapped colour against the project's
published colours (pinned like any source, S17) and skips the picks: the colours are palette facts (S17), and the
gate's palette run resolves every bundled palette over each preset it has a source for and compares each colour its
`[palette.sources]` names (a role, input or token colour, by its TOML path) with that fact, under the schemes, on
the presets and for the paths S17's *The palette run* states; a colour stated as a
derivation names none, its operands being checked where they are mapped (ADD-A115).

## S15. System control rendering (R11)

```rust
pub enum SystemControl { AppKitCheckbox, AppKitRadio, AppKitDisclosure, AppKitPushDisclosure, AppKitPopUp }
pub struct ControlImage { pub width: u32, pub height: u32, pub pixels: Vec<[f32; 4]>,  // extended sRGB, straight
                          pub alignment: Rect }       // alpha (S2.1); the control's alignment rect inside the
                                                      // image, in logical px from its top-left corner (below)
pub struct SystemAppearance { pub scheme: Scheme, pub increased_contrast: bool }   // AppKit's four appearances
pub fn render_system_control(control: SystemControl, states: StateFlags, size: ControlSize,
                             appearance: SystemAppearance, key_window: bool, direction: Direction,
                             scale: f32,
                             width: Option<Px>) -> Option<ControlImage>;   // width: a content-sized control's
```

It returns `None` for a `ControlSize` AppKit has no size for on the running macOS (which sizes it has per version is
the facts', S17), as the preset declares no such size there (S7.3).

What each image covers: `AppKitCheckbox`, `AppKitRadio`, the box and mark; `AppKitDisclosure`, the triangle;
`AppKitPushDisclosure`, the bezel and chevron; `AppKitPopUp`, the whole button at `width`. The image is the control
as AppKit draws it, and `ControlImage.alignment` the control's alignment rect inside it: AppKit holds a control's
frame and its alignment rect apart (`alignmentRectForFrame:`, `alignmentRectInsets`, `NSLayoutConstraint.h:297-302`
at xcode@26.6), and the facts measure a control's box from the alignment rect (S17's evidence rule, AppKit's
padding), so the connector lays the image with that rect over the box of the parts it replaces (ADD-A146). The
pop-up's arrow area is no field of the image: the connector places it from the resolved values, its width
`arrow_area.min_width` and its inset from the image's end `body.padding`'s end (the catalogue's `combo_box` layout,
MAC-CB01's measurements), the SDK declaring no rect for it (`NSPopUpButtonCell.h:95` declares `arrowPosition` alone,
`NSCell.h:154-156` the image, title and drawing rects) (ADD-A146; rejected: `ControlImage.arrow` from the cell's
`indicatorRect`, a name no header of the SDK declares, at xcode@26.6 or xcode@16.4; the cell's frame less
`titleRectForBounds:`, a second source for a place the facts already give, to be measured equal before it could
stand). The rendering uses the system's accent; an accent the
application or a palette sets cannot reach it, which the connector's contract records as its limit (R11, R23).

**The parameters** (ADD-A146). `states` sets the cell's own state and nothing more: `Checked` its `state` on and
`Indeterminate` mixed, else off (`NSControlStateValueOn`, `Mixed`, `Off`, `NSCell.h:71-74`, `:111`), which on the two
disclosure controls `Open` sets on; `Pressed` its `highlighted` (`:127`); `Disabled` its `enabled` off (`:117`). The
cell declares no state for another flag: the focus ring is a drawing of its own beside the cell's
(`drawFocusRingMaskWithFrame:inView:`, `:225`, against `drawWithFrame:inView:`, `:164`), the part's `focus` (S2.10),
and whether AppKit draws any of the five differently under the pointer is unmeasured, pending on register row
U708, a flag it finds joining this list. `states` are the control's, gathered where the catalogue's *Flags* rule
puts each, whichever element the glyph's part belongs to: `Open` from the element that opens, `Pressed` from the
element that takes the press (the disclosure's own, MAC-L10, MAC-EX03; the combo box's for the pop-up), `Disabled`
and `Checked` from the widget's own element. `direction` sets the cell's
`userInterfaceLayoutDirection` (`NSCell.h:197-199`), which otherwise follows the application's (`NSView.h:354`) and
not the element's (S8); whether AppKit mirrors the pop-up's arrow side and the disclosure triangle by it is the
same row's reading, the parameter deciding the image either way.

On macOS's main thread it renders; anywhere else, and off macOS, it returns `None`, so connectors need no `cfg` of
their own. Cached per (control, states, size, appearance, key, direction, scale, width), and emptied whenever the
reader reads again (`reload_reader`, S16, which the application calls on the watcher's notification): AppKit's
drawing follows settings the key does not hold, the system's accent among them, so a cached checkbox would keep the
old accent while every role follows the new one (ADD-A146; rejected: the accent in the key, one of the settings the
drawing follows, not all of them). **Approved by the maintainer (2026-10-29):** rendering through AppKit uses `unsafe` objc2 calls under the same
exception as the SF Symbols loader (`native-theme/src/sficons.rs`): module-scoped, each block with its safety
argument. A glyph naming a system control
(`GlyphSource::SystemControl { control, replaces }`) states the parts the rendering replaces (the checkbox's box and
mark together, R11), on a part drawn in every state, the one whose glyph it is (`checkbox.box`, `radio.ring`, MAC-C06,
MAC-C07), never on one hidden by state, which would hide the rendering of an unchecked control. Where the rendering
is not drawn, the parts it replaces draw their modelled style: the box, and on the radio its measured dot, while the
checkbox's mark has no model (R11), so without the rendering no mark is drawn and a checked and a mixed checkbox
differ only where their measured box fills do (the mixed fill a measurement, MAC-C01), the limit the
connector records (R23; ADD-A126). Whether AppKit draws these controls differently in an emphasized selected table row
(`NSTableCellView`'s background style) is MAC-L17†'s measurement; if it does, the cache key needs the background style
(the catalogue's Open items, ADD-A125). The list of `SystemControl`s is the traceability's rows that need it.

## S16. The API surface

`SystemTheme` is renamed `Theme`, the one owner of the stack, the inputs and the application's conditions.
`AccessibilityPreferences` goes: the reader reports conditions, the text-scaling factor and the font DPI in its
`ReaderState`. Today's `ColorMode` is `Scheme`, and today's `Rgba` is `Color` (S2.1).
After every mutation the whole stack passes S12, or the mutation is refused whole, the theme staying as it was (S8,
S12; ADD-A147):

```rust
impl Theme {
    pub fn from_system(generation: Option<PresetId>) -> Result<Theme, ThemeError>;
                                                          // reads the system; the preset is `generation`, the
                                                          // application's opt-out to another generation of this
                                                          // platform (R1.5; `Err(PresetNotForPlatform)` otherwise),
                                                          // else the one the OS version and the app's declared
                                                          // opt-out choose (as `pipeline::preset_for_version` does);
                                                          // a failed first read is `Err(Reader { preset, failure })`
    pub async fn from_system_async(generation: Option<PresetId>) -> Result<Theme, ThemeError>;
                                                          // the same; the portal reads are D-Bus calls, which an
                                                          // application inside an async executor awaits rather
                                                          // than blocking it (`from_system` blocks on them)
    pub fn from_preset(id: PresetId, scheme: Scheme) -> Result<Theme, ThemeError>;   // no reader: the no-reader
                                                          // state below, with this scheme
    #[doc(hidden)]
    pub fn from_preset_synthetic(id: PresetId, scheme: Scheme, layers: Vec<Layer>) -> Result<Theme, ThemeError>;
                                                          // the facts gate's and the build test's route while a
                                                          // preset's `[pending]` table is not empty (S17, S19.1,
                                                          // ADD-A128): the preset validated with these layers over
                                                          // it, all added at once, so a listed path they leave
                                                          // unstated is the missing-field problem; a listed
                                                          // `default_size`, which no layer can state, exempt from
                                                          // S12's default-size checks; a listed part drawn, no
                                                          // value stated for it; a listed input's per-scheme
                                                          // value these layers state folded into the preset's
                                                          // own input base, marked synthetic (ADD-A132); kept by the
                                                          // theme's later mutations while this preset is current,
                                                          // a successful `set_preset` ending it and removing these
                                                          // layers (S17; ADD-A131)
    pub fn set_preset(&mut self, id: PresetId) -> Result<(), LayerError>;          // a theme change: the reader
```
