```rust
                                                          // applies its portable part (accent, scheme, fonts, text
                                                          // scaling, conditions) to any preset and its
                                                          // `[for_preset.<id>]` part and preset-conditioned rules
                                                          // to its own; the accent layer (and on `kde-breeze` and
                                                          // `material-3` the accent-derivation layer) is derived
                                                          // again and the
                                                          // palette's source chosen again for the new preset (S9.5,
                                                          // S14); the flavour is kept where the new preset declares
                                                          // it, else it becomes the new preset's default (its first
                                                          // declared, S10; none where it declares none), which
                                                          // `flavor()` reports
    pub fn set_reader_stand_in(&mut self, state: ReaderState, layer: Layer) -> Result<(), LayerError>;
                                                          // sets it, or replaces the one set (the facts gate replaces
                                                          // it per combination, S17); refused while a reader exists,
                                                          // and (`Err(AccentInputsMissing)`) where it states the
                                                          // preset's accent inputs otherwise than as one group (S9.2)
    pub fn remove_reader_stand_in(&mut self) -> Result<(), LayerError>;   // back to the no-reader state (below);
                                                          // a no-op without a stand-in
    pub fn pick(&mut self, scheme: Option<Scheme>) -> Result<(), LayerError>;     // None: follow the reader's or
                                                          // stand-in's scheme, else the one `from_preset` was given;
                                                          // under a palette as S14 says (Some: refused for a scheme
                                                          // it lacks; None: suspends it while the system's is one)
    pub fn set_flavor(&mut self, flavor: Key) -> Result<(), LayerError>;          // undeclared: refused; a declared
                                                          // flavour but the default while the flavours unit is not
                                                          // enabled (S6.1): refused with `ProblemKind::Later`
                                                          // (S12; ADD-A147)
    pub fn preset(&self) -> PresetId;                     // the current preset
    pub fn flavor(&self) -> Option<Key>;                  // the flavour in force: set, or the preset's default;
                                                          // None on a preset that declares no flavours (R1.6)
    pub fn flavors(&self) -> Vec<Key>;                    // the current preset's declared flavours (the default
                                                          // alone while the flavours unit is not enabled, S6.1;
                                                          // ADD-A147), its default first (S10), the keys
                                                          // `set_flavor` accepts; empty where it declares none
                                                          // (ADD-A146)
    pub fn scheme(&self) -> Scheme;                       // the scheme in force: `pick`ed, else the reader's or
                                                          // stand-in's, else the one `from_preset` was given
    pub fn version_match(&self) -> Option<VersionMatch>; // how the running OS version relates to the current
                                                          // preset's generation (R1.5: macOS 27 under
                                                          // `macos-tahoe` is `PresetOlder`); None where the platform
                                                          // has no generation table (Linux), the version cannot be
                                                          // read (the reader's feature off), or the current preset
                                                          // is not a generation of the running platform
    pub fn add_layer(&mut self, layer: Layer) -> Result<LayerId, LayerError>;
    pub fn replace_layer(&mut self, id: LayerId, layer: Layer) -> Result<(), LayerError>;
    pub fn remove_layer(&mut self, id: LayerId) -> Result<(), LayerError>;   // both: `Err(UnknownLayer(id))` for an id
                                                          // this theme does not hold, as a stale id is the caller's
                                                          // error (S1)
    pub fn set_accent(&mut self, accent: Option<Accent>) -> Result<(), LayerError>;   // None: the system's again
    pub fn apply_palette(&mut self, palette: Option<Palette>) -> Result<(), LayerError>;  // None: removes it;
                                                          // refused as S14 says (a picked scheme it lacks, no
                                                          // source for the preset, missing accent inputs, a preset
                                                          // colour rule left standing over a role it states);
                                                          // under a followed scheme it lacks, accepted and
                                                          // suspended (ADD-A146)
    pub fn reader_status(&self) -> ReaderStatus;         // `Fallback` where a read succeeded with a source standing
                                                          // in (S9.1; the KDE palette's colours file, S9.3) or an
                                                          // accent group left out after a failed read (S9.3; not
                                                          // a slot the platform gives none at):
                                                          // `from_system` returns the theme then
    pub fn reload_reader(&mut self) -> ReaderStatus;     // re-read the system into the reader layer in place
                                                          // (a failure keeps the old layer); the application calls it
                                                          // from its event loop on the watcher's `on_theme_change`;
                                                          // it empties S15's rendering cache
    pub async fn reload_reader_async(&mut self) -> ReaderStatus;   // the same, awaited (as `from_system_async`)
    pub fn system(&self) -> Option<&ReaderState>;         // the conditions the reader or stand-in reports, for what
                                                          // an application acts on itself (Windows' ShowSounds,
                                                          // W-P3-11†); None without either
    pub fn set_contrast(&mut self, contrast: ContrastChoice) -> Result<(), LayerError>;   // below
    pub fn resolve(&self, window: &mut WindowState, conditions: &WindowConditions) -> Resolution;   // S8
}
pub enum ContrastChoice { System,       // the reader's or stand-in's contrast (none without either), the default
                          Standard,     // no contrast condition, whatever the reader reports
                          Increased, High }   // that `Contrast`, whatever the reader reports (ADD-A146)
impl ResolvedTheme {
    pub fn icon(&self, scope: &Scope, id: IconId<'_>, style: &ResolvedIconStyle) -> Option<IconData>;
                                                          // from `token.icons`' set, theme and theme fallback (S4.5),
                                                          // in `style` (size, weight, scale, rendering mode, symbol
                                                          // variants, axes; its fill where the set recolours), for the
                                                          // direction and language in `scope` (the scope the part's
                                                          // query returned, which carries the element's own) and the
                                                          // role's `token.icons.mirroring` (S2.9, R25.8); None where
                                                          // the set has no such icon or lacks its feature
}
impl PresetId {
    pub fn all() -> &'static [PresetId];                  // every bundled preset, in a stable order
    pub fn for_platform() -> Vec<PresetId>;               // the presets to offer on the running platform and
                                                          // desktop, in `all()`'s order (*Which presets*, below)
    pub fn for_system() -> Option<PresetId>;              // the preset the platform, the detected desktop and the OS
                                                          // version choose, as `from_system(None)` does, without
                                                          // reading the theme or asking the portal (on Linux the
                                                          // desktop the last read refined, as `platform_preset_name`
                                                          // does today); where the version cannot be read (the
                                                          // reader's feature off), the oldest generation's; None
                                                          // on a platform `from_system` reads nothing on (below)
    pub fn key(self) -> &'static str;                     // `"kde-breeze"`: S11's `id`, `preset:<key>`, `for_preset`
    pub fn from_key(key: &str) -> Option<PresetId>;
    pub fn display_name(self) -> &'static str;            // `"KDE Breeze"`
}
impl PaletteId {
    pub fn all() -> &'static [PaletteId];                 // every bundled palette
    pub fn key(self) -> &'static str;
    pub fn from_key(key: &str) -> Option<PaletteId>;
    pub fn display_name(self) -> &'static str;
}
impl Palette {
    pub fn bundled(id: PaletteId) -> Result<Palette, LayerError>;   // native-theme's mapping, with the ports it
                                                          // has; a build test parses and validates every bundled
                                                          // palette, so the error is never met in a release
    pub fn from_toml(text: &str) -> Result<Palette, LayerError>;
    pub fn from_port(file: &[u8], scheme: Scheme) -> Result<Palette, PortError>;   // S14: every build, no feature;
                                                          // the file's bytes, decoded as the KDE reader decodes
                                                          // them (ADD-A142)
    pub fn with_port(self, port: Palette) -> Result<Palette, LayerError>;          // S14
}
```

**Without a reader.** A theme with neither a reader nor a stand-in (`from_preset`) resolves under the **no-reader
state**: the scheme `from_preset` was given (or `pick`ed), no contrast, every flag false, no idiom, device model,
container size, system setting or content-size category, a text-scaling factor of 1 and `font_dpi: None` (the
preset's token converts its points, S9.4). Nothing in it is a reading, so `system()` returns `None` and
`reader_status()` `NoReader`; the facts gate's base conditions are this state under each scheme (S17). A failed first
read in `from_system` is an error carrying the preset it chose, not a silent fallback: the application that wants the
preset alone calls `from_preset(preset, scheme)` with the scheme it chooses, so no scheme is assumed for it. A later
failed re-read keeps the previous reader layer and `ReaderState` (S8).

**The contrast an application picks** (ADD-A146). `set_contrast` takes a `ContrastChoice`: `System` follows the
reader's or stand-in's `ReaderState.contrast`, and `Standard`, `Increased` and `High` hold whatever it reports,
`Standard` being no contrast condition at all. So an application resolves the standard look on a system with
Increase Contrast on (a showcase's contrast picker, a screenshot run), as `pick(Some(scheme))` gives it either scheme
over the system's: the application's conditions win over the reader's (S8). `ReaderState.contrast` stays an
`Option<Contrast>`, a reader reporting one contrast or none. Rejected: `Option<Contrast>` with `None` the reader's,
as it was (no value says "no contrast" over a reader that reports one); `Option<Option<Contrast>>` (two `None`s to
tell apart at every call); a `Contrast::Standard` member (`ReaderState.contrast` would then spell no contrast two
ways).

**Which reader** (ADD-A135; ledger queue #173). `from_system` chooses the reader and its preset from the platform and,
on Linux, the desktop `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP` names, refined where it names none by asking the session bus which portal
backend runs (within the readers' D-Bus deadline), then by the user's `kdeglobals` (with the `kde` feature), as
`PresetId::for_system` chooses. On Linux:
- GNOME and Budgie are read by the GNOME reader under `adwaita` (S9.3), KDE by the KDE reader under `kde-breeze`;
  `Err(FeatureDisabled)` where the build lacks the reader's feature;
- every other desktop (Xfce, Cinnamon, MATE, LXQt, the Wayland compositors, COSMIC, one the refinement leaves
  unnamed) has no reader of its own and is read under the preset `PresetId::for_system` gives (`adwaita`), in its
  common bases and conditions only, nothing under `for_preset`: the portal's `org.freedesktop.appearance` settings
  first (`color-scheme`, `accent-color`, `contrast`, `reduced-motion`), as the GNOME reader reads them, then, for
  the scheme and motion the portal does not give, 0.7.0's own chain on these desktops (`detect.rs` at the switch's parent 2796b26e, the file as tagged `v0.7.0`,
  caeddd6b): the scheme dark where `GTK_THEME`, lowercased, ends in `:dark` or holds `-dark` (`:768-774`), else gsettings'
  `org.gnome.desktop.interface color-scheme` (`:727-742`, "reliable on GNOME and GTK-based desktops", `:744-748`), else
  dark where `gtk-3.0/settings.ini` sets `gtk-application-prefer-dark-theme` (`:797-810`), else light; reduced motion
  gsettings' `org.gnome.desktop.a11y.interface reduced-motion`, a read 0.7.0 did not make there, and `animations_off`
  its `enable-animations` false, the key 0.7.0 read there and reported as reduced motion, its one motion flag
  (`:952-967`, `:976-988`): the model holds the two apart (S7.1), so an application checking reduced motion there
  sees `enable-animations` as `animations_off` now.
  `kdeglobals`, which 0.7.0 also asked there, stays the KDE reader's. The read cannot fail, a setting none of these
  gives keeping the no-reader state's value (no flag); it needs the `portal` feature as the GNOME reader does
  (`Err(FeatureDisabled)` without it). So these desktops keep what 0.7.0 gave them, the preset in the scheme and
  motion the desktop set, with the portal's reading first (the 0.8.0 plan's D13: nothing 0.7.0 has is lost);
- Linux has no generation table, so the one preset of the desktop is its only generation: `from_system(Some(id))`
  takes that preset and is `Err(PresetNotForPlatform(id))` for any other.
A platform this build reads nothing on is `Err(PlatformUnsupported)`, never a preset in an assumed scheme. The
watcher (below) chooses its backend by the same refined desktop, so `on_theme_change` on a desktop
`XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP` does not name waits for the portal backend's answer up to that deadline. Rejected:
`PlatformUnsupported` on the desktops without a reader of their own (an application there loses the scheme 0.7.0
gave it); the portal alone there (where no portal answers it reports light where 0.7.0 found dark); the GNOME reader
whole there (its text-scaling, overlay-scrolling and icon-theme reads go beyond what 0.7.0 read on these desktops,
which D13 does not ask for: a readers unit's decision). The watcher of those desktops fires on the portal's
`SettingChanged` of the settings their read takes from the portal and gsettings, the gsettings keys where the
desktop's portal backend forwards them, as GNOME's does (`xdg-desktop-portal-gnome@51.0 src/settings.c:389-438`);
`GTK_THEME` (fixed for a process)
and `gtk-3.0/settings.ini` (a file no signal reports, which 0.7.0 did not watch either) are not watched, so a change
there shows at the next read (ADD-A138; ledger queue #179).

**Which presets** (ADD-A146). `PresetId::for_system()` is `Some` on the platforms `from_system` has a reader for,
macOS, Windows and Linux, whatever the build's features, the preset `from_system(None)` chooses there (*Which
reader*); on any other platform (iOS and Android until their readers, R18; any target the crate reads nothing on) it
is `None`, as `from_system` is `Err(PlatformUnsupported)` there: the library reports that it knows no preset of the
system, and the application chooses one, from `for_platform()` or `all()`. `PresetId::for_platform()` lists the
presets to offer on the running platform and desktop, by 0.7.0's platform tags (`native-theme/src/presets.rs:58-64`,
`:164-174` at `v0.7.0`; the 0.8.0 plan's D13), `ios-26` tagged as `ios-13` is: on macOS `macos-monterey`,
`macos-tahoe`, `ios-13` and `ios-26`; on iOS `ios-13` and `ios-26`; on Windows `windows-11`; on Linux `adwaita`,
and on a KDE desktop (the desktop `for_system` reads) `kde-breeze` as well; and on every platform `material-3`,
which has no tag, alone on a platform no tag names. Rejected: `for_system() -> PresetId` (it is called exactly
where the read failed, `PlatformUnsupported` among the failures, and would name a preset for a system the library
knows nothing of: 0.7.0 answered `adwaita` there, `native-theme/src/pipeline.rs:693-696` at `v0.7.0`, a choice the
library has no ground for); `adwaita` listed on a platform no tag names (0.7.0's listing, its platform detection
answering `linux` for every other target, `presets.rs:149-157` at `v0.7.0`: the list follows 0.7.0's tags, not that
detection's fallback, the same choice `for_system` declines by answering `None` there); "those whose platform
is the running one", the rule as it stood (it said neither that a KDE desktop lists `adwaita` too nor that macOS
lists the iOS presets).

**The main thread on macOS** (ADD-A138; ledger queue #178). AppKit gives the Keyboard navigation setting and the
scroller style to the main thread only, so `from_system`, `from_system_async`, `reload_reader` and
`reload_reader_async` read `full_keyboard_access` and `overlay_scrollbars` only when called on the main thread, and
elsewhere report both `false`, with no `Fallback` (S9.3's *The macOS reader's readings*); their documentation says
so. An AppKit application's event loop, from which it calls `reload_reader` (above), runs on the main thread; one
that awaits `from_system_async` on another thread and needs the two settings calls `reload_reader` from its event
loop.

**Today's API, feature by feature** (S19.3 migrates the branch's callers):

- *Preset listing* (`Theme::list_presets`, `list_presets_for_platform`, `PresetInfo`): kept, as `PresetId::all`,
  `PresetId::for_platform` and `PresetId`'s `key` and `display_name` (`PresetInfo`'s fields; the platform tags stay
  internal, read by `for_platform`, whose list *Which presets*, above, states); the community presets, now palettes,
  are listed by `PaletteId::all`, and a preset's flavours by `Theme::flavors` (ADD-A146). The showcases'
  pickers and an application's own still need them.
- *`from_system_with_preset` and the two `_async` constructors:* `from_system_with_preset` is replaced by
  `from_system(Some(generation))`, one constructor with the generation an optional input (R1.5's opt-out; it differs
  from `from_system(None)` and `set_preset`, as the reader's preset-specific part follows the generation it is built
  with, S9.5); `from_system_async` and `from_system_with_preset_async` become `from_system_async(generation)`, and
  `reload_reader_async` is added, because the portal reader is asynchronous.
- *Icon loading* (`SystemTheme::icon`, `icon_theme_for`): `icon` is kept as `ResolvedTheme::icon` above, which takes the
  part's resolved icon style and the scope's direction and language (R25.8); `icon_theme_for(mode)` is replaced by the
  resolved `token.icons` (`ResolvedTheme::tokens(scope).icons`: set, theme, theme fallback), which rules state per
  scheme (`breeze`, `breeze-dark`) and which a re-resolution after a scheme change gives anew (S8). The `icons`
  module's free loaders (a set and theme the caller names, custom icons through `IconProvider`) stay for icons outside
  the theme, with `Color` for `Rgba`; `icon_indicator` and `load_icon_indicator` go (S2.7).
- *`Theme::to_toml`, `Theme::lint_toml`:* removed. There is no whole theme to write: a look is an application layer an
  author writes in TOML (S11); and `Layer::from_toml` and `Palette::from_toml` refuse every unknown key, each a
  `Problem` with its TOML key path (the TOML reader's own, `LayerError`, S1), which is what linting reported.
- *The `detect` functions:* `system_is_dark`, `detect_is_dark`, `prefers_reduced_motion`, `detect_reduced_motion` and
  `accessibility_preferences` are replaced by `Theme::system()` (the reader's `ReaderState`); `system_icon_set`,
  `system_icon_theme` and its other forms (`detect_icon_theme`, `DetectionContext::icon_theme`) by the resolved
  `token.icons`, which the reader states where the platform has a setting. The
  desktop detection (`LinuxDesktop`, `detect_linux_desktop`, `parse_linux_desktop`, `detect::system()`) and
  `invalidate_caches` stay: they are not theme values, `native-theme-build`'s generated icon code reads the desktop,
  and `reload_reader` clears the caches it reads through.
- *`ResolutionContext`* (`font_dpi`, `button_order`, `icon_theme`): removed, each field having its place in the
  model: the font DPI is `ReaderState.font_dpi` over `token.text.font_dpi` (S9.4), the dialog's button order its
  widget value (`dialog.values.action_layout.row_order`), the icon theme `token.icons.theme`.
- *`SystemTheme`'s fields:* `preset` is `Theme::preset()` (the gpui showcase reads it for its picker's default);
  `mode` is `Theme::scheme()`; `version_match` is `Theme::version_match()`, kept with `VersionMatch` (R1.5's case,
  an OS newer or older than the chosen generation; a status enum, the type keeps `#[non_exhaustive]`, S21.2,
  ADD-A146); `light` and `dark`
  are `Theme::resolve` under each scheme (S8): `resolve` takes the scheme in force, so a caller wanting both
  `pick(Some(..))`s each in turn and resolves each with a `WindowState` of its own, not a window's (a window's would
  record a theme change, and `suspends`, at that window's next resolution, S4.3), a palette refusing a scheme it
  lacks (S14), then `pick`s again what it had picked, which it keeps itself: `scheme()` reports the scheme in force,
  not whether it was picked (ADD-A146); `icon_set` and `icon_theme` the resolved `token.icons`; `layout` the
  `layout` widget's values (the catalogue); `accessibility` `Theme::system()`. `name` (the KDE colour scheme's name,
  or the preset's) is removed: a scheme file's name is not a theme value, and its one caller, the gpui connector,
  needs only a name for its toolkit's theme, which it takes from `Theme::preset().display_name()`.
- *`pipeline::platform_preset_name()` and `PlatformPreset`:* replaced by `PresetId::for_system()`, the same choice
  without reading the theme, `None` where 0.7.0 answered `adwaita` for a platform it did not know (*Which presets*,
  above; ADD-A146); the three showcases call it for their pickers' default where the system read fails, choosing
  their own where it is `None`, and the egui connector's font tests for the platform's preset.
- *`pipeline::diagnose_platform_support()` and `DiagnosticEntry`:* kept: they report what the readers' detection
  depends on (the desktop, environment variables, tools, configuration files, features, the OS generation), which the
  model does not change, for an application to show when a read fails; `DiagnosticEntry::OsGeneration.preset`
  becomes a `PresetId`, and the enum, a diagnostic one, keeps `#[non_exhaustive]` (S21.2; ADD-A146).
- *`SystemTheme::with_overlay`:* replaced by `Theme::add_layer` (R2.4): an application's look is a layer in the
  stack, validated when added (S8, S12).
- *Helpers outside the model:* `color::composite_over` is kept, over `Color` (a translucent colour or appended
  layer composited over what lies beneath, which connectors do, R5.3), drawing as S2.1's hand-over does (each colour
  premultiplied, each premultiplied channel clamped to `0..=1`, then blended, the composite returned as a straight
  colour; ADD-A128); the `fonts` module (`select_face`,
  `system_face`, `substitute_family`, `substitute_family_cached`) is kept: it finds a resolved font's face on the
  system, which is not a theme value; today's `Theme::preset(name)`, which loads a whole theme by name as
  today's `Theme::from_toml` does, goes with it (below, R21), replaced by `Theme::from_preset(id, scheme)` and `Palette::bundled(id)`; the KDE reader's tests
  are its unit tests (`src/kde/tests.rs`, over `tests/fixtures/kde/`): `kde` is `pub(crate)` and no hidden test
  entry is kept (ADD-A146: the text follows the code, which holds none).
- *`crate::Error` and `crate::Result`:* kept for the APIs that are not theme values, with the variants they return:
  `PlatformUnsupported`, `WatchUnavailable` and `ReaderFailed` (`watch::on_theme_change` and its backends,
  `rasterize::rasterize_svg`; the `icons` loaders return `Option`). The variants the theme's APIs returned go with
  them: `FeatureDisabled` (now `ThemeError::FeatureDisabled`), `NoVariant`, `Toml`, `Io` (`Theme::from_toml`,
  `from_file`, `pick_variant`), `UnknownPreset` (a `PresetId` is never unknown; `PresetId::from_key` returns `None`),
  `ResolutionIncomplete` and `ResolutionInvalid` with `RangeViolation` (validation is `LayerError`'s, S12).
  `ErrorKind` and `Error::kind()` go: the
  three variants left are matched directly, beside a wildcard arm, the enum having `#[non_exhaustive]` as every
  error enum has (S21.2; ADD-A146). The theme's own errors are S1's.

A look of the application's own is an application layer over a bundled preset (`Layer::from_toml`, S1), never a whole
preset of its own: today's `Theme::from_toml` and `Theme::from_file`, which load a whole theme, go (R21), so every
look starts from a preset the facts gate checks.

The watcher (`native-theme/src/watch`) tells the application that the system changed; `on_theme_change` stays the
notification, and the application calls `reload_reader` and resolves its windows again (S8).

## S17. Facts as data and the gate (R4, R22)

**Format** (`docs/facts/<platform>/<area>.toml`; ADD-A116):

```toml
[[fact]]                                          # docs/facts/gnome/buttons.toml
key = "button.body.fill"                          # the field path (below)
when = { states = ["hover"], variants = ["flat"] }   # as S11's `when`
value = "= alpha(surface.foreground, <a>)"        # a value or the platform's derivation
rows = ["GN-1.29"]                                # the gap-map rows the fact carries (R24)

[[fact.cite]]                                     # one or more: together they serve every generation (below)
kind = "published"
source = "libadwaita@1.10.0 src/stylesheet/<file>.scss:<l1>-<l2>"
quote = "<the source's text at those lines>"

[[fact]]                                          # docs/facts/macos/…: one fact for macOS 15 and 26
key = "<field path>"
value = "<n>px"
rows = ["<row>"]

[[fact.cite]]                                     # serves macos-monterey
kind = "measured"
evidence = "docs/evidence/os-probe/<date>-run-<id>/os-probe-macos-15/probe.toml#<dotted.key>"
tolerance = <t>

[[fact.cite]]                                     # serves macos-tahoe
kind = "measured"
evidence = "docs/evidence/os-probe/<date>-run-<id>/os-probe-macos-26/probe.toml#<dotted.key>"
tolerance = <t>
```

- **A file's size** (ADD-A147; the 0.8.0 plan's D6, outcome 8). A facts file past 40 MiB (41,943,040 bytes) is split
  by key prefix, each part a file of the same platform holding the facts of its prefixes,
  `docs/facts/<platform>/<stem>-<prefix>.toml` (`<stem>` the split file's), which `check_facts.py` enforces by failing
  a file past that size; the split changes no fact. Rejected: no limit (`docs/facts/ios/button.toml` is 34,075,260
  bytes with most of its facts pending, and a measured fact carries the citations a pending one lacks).
- **Keys and values.** A key is a field path in the Rust names (S1), without TOML's unit suffix:
  `<widget>.<part>.<field>` and `<widget>.values.<name>` for a typed widget (S5, S6.1), `component.<key>.<part>.<field>`
  and `component.<key>.values.<name>` for a keyed one (S5.1), and S2.2's reference forms for colour roles, tokens and
  inputs (`role.…`, `token.…`, `input.…`); a whole part's absence or substitution is keyed by the part,
  `<widget>.<part>` (`component.<key>.<part>`), with `value = "absent"` (S6.3's `absent = true`,
  `PartPresence::Absent`), `value = "present"` (S6.3's `absent = false`, `PartPresence::Present`, a part drawn over
  an `Absent` or `DrawnAs` below, stated after the fact that makes it absent or drawn as another; ADD-A126, ledger queue #126) or the
  part's `drawn_as` table as S11 spells it (`PartPresence::DrawnAs`), and the gate compares it with the query's
  `Styled::NotDrawn`, `Styled::DrawnAs` or, for `present`, any `Styled::Style` (ADD-A121); a map entry whose key is text is keyed by that key as a TOML
  dotted key writes it, quoted where needed, and equal to the preset's entry as S11's TOML keys are
  (`token.text.fallbacks.per_family."Segoe Fluent Icons"`; ADD-A123); a `Value` struct block field is stated per leaf, or whole: by a
table (the whole block, as the preset layer's bases spell it, S2.2), a reference (`….focus = "= token.focus"`; never a part's `text`, which
references a style or slot leaf by leaf, S2.8: `….text.font.size = "= token.text.keyed.body.font.size"` and each
other leaf that follows the style so, its four drawn-text leaves stated, `….text.elision =
"= token.text.keyed.body.elision"` where the style sets it and a value otherwise) or `value = "absent"` where S6.3
allows it (S2.2), a plain one (`TextStyle.font`, a part's `padding` or a focus indicator's `offset`, `Sides`, S2.2) per leaf
(`….text.font.size`) or whole, by a table holding every leaf as S11 spells it, as S2.2 allows (`button.body.padding = {
top_px = 5, right_px = 17, bottom_px = 5, left_px = 17 }`, each leaf a value or, in a `Value` leaf, a reference), never by a
reference, the gate comparing it leaf by leaf as it compares leaves stated one by one, a `Value` field of an enum block (S6.1 lists them: `Value<Timing>`, `Value<Shadow>`) whole, by S11's spelling of
its variant (`{ cubic_bezier = […] }`), a reference, or `"absent"` where S6.3 allows it (`button.body.shadow =
"absent"`), a plain or bare enum block (a `Corners` corner, a `token.motion.timings` entry) by its variant only;
a map field (`Vec<(K, V)>`, or a `Value` of one: `Font.axes`, `Font.features`) stated whole, by a table (`{}` the
empty map) or, in a `Value`, a reference, is compared whole, entry by entry by key and in no order, as the preset
layer's bases state it, never merged over the theme's value as a patch's map is (S6.1): a fact is the value, not a
patch, so `{}` says the map has no entries and an entry the theme holds beyond the fact's fails it (ADD-A132);
which fields are struct blocks the valid keys decide (below).
  **Per-leaf facts of a field set whole** (ADD-A128): facts stated per leaf of a block that S6.1 sets whole (an
  `Option<B>`: `token.behavior.key_repeat.delay` and `.interval`, each a setting of its own in the sources) are
  composed into one value per combination, from the applying fact of each leaf (*Which fact applies*, below); a leaf
  with no applying fact fails as a missing fact, and a leaf whose applying fact is pending makes the whole field
  pending for that combination: the generator writes nothing for it there (where nothing lies beneath, the preset lists the
  field as pending, *A pending fact with nothing beneath it*, below), and the gate reports the other leaf's fact with
  the pending one, unchecked. The gate compares the composed value with the resolved field leaf by leaf, each leaf at its own
  key's gate tolerance (below), a resolved `None` failing it; the perturbed run compares it leaf by leaf too, a
  derived leaf (KDE's interval) evaluated, a literal one skipped. The preset generator writes the composed value
  whole, as S11 spells it, a sub-table holding one leaf per line, each line with its fact's citation comment
  (`[tokens.behavior.key_repeat]` with `delay_ms = 500  # <citation>` and `interval_ms = 30  # <citation>`; in a
  rule, its target `"tokens"` and the sub-table `[rules.set.behavior.key_repeat]`, as an inline table holds no
  comments), so each leaf's citation stays on its line; a leaf fact's `preset:` condition selects the preset's file,
  not a rule. Where the leaves' facts hold
  under different `when`s, the value differs between the classes of combinations in which the same fact applies to
  each leaf, so the generator writes the bases for the class with no condition and a rule for each other class, the
  overlaps of the leaves' `when`s included, each stating both leaves, in an order where a rule for an overlap comes
  after the rules it overlaps. A fact keyed by the field itself states it whole (`token.behavior.key_repeat`:
  `"none"` or a table holding every leaf, as S11 spells it; never a reference, the field being no `Value`), its
  `None` only so, and a generation's facts state the field whole or per leaf, never both, which `check_facts.py`
  refuses. Rejected: an `Option<B>` taking `Fields` (refused over `None`, as over `Absent`), a class 2 change to the
  model that no source needs, as no platform rule changes one leaf while keeping the other from beneath. Setting the
  field whole costs the layers above the preset a restatement instead: a reader states both leaves wherever it
  states one, the KDE reader stating the interval, for a `kcminputrc` that sets `RepeatDelay` alone, as KWin reads
  `RepeatRate` unset (`kwin@6.8.2 src/keyboard_input.cpp:202-204`), cited, as S9.1 states a value a file lacks; and an
  application that changes only the delay restates the interval, which `Fields` would have spared it at the cost of
  a patch over `None` that the merge must refuse. The
  valid keys are the catalogue's (through `scripts/spec_catalogue.py`) and the core's (S3, S4, S9; its Rust
  sketches as `scripts/check_spec_names.py` reads them) until `docs/property-registry.toml` is generated (S18), and
  the registry's from then on; palette facts have keys of their own (below). A value is spelled as S11's **Spelling** table spells it in a preset, as a TOML value
  (a number a TOML number, a bool a TOML bool, a variant with data a one-key table, a list of layers a list of
  tables), with the key's own length, duration or angle in S2.2's units (`"4px"`, `"150ms"`) since the key carries no
  suffix, while tables nested in a value keep S11's suffixed keys (`x_px = <n>`); the quote check compares its
  numeric, colour and text leaves. Every expression a fact states (`"= …"`, the value or any leaf or item of it) is
  read by S2.2's grammar, which `check_facts.py` applies production by production (ADD-A144): each operand as its
  own production spells it, the reserved operands bare (`body_font_height`, `text_scale`, `font_size`,
  `line_height`, `base`, `scheme`) and taking no path, `element.` followed by one of the names its own production
  lists (`ElementData`'s fields, the window's and screen's sizes and the font metrics) and no other word, a call's name one of S2.2's
  functions with its arity, `active(…)` around a role reference, so `element.body_font_height`, which the parser
  refuses, fails the checker too (the three KDE facts 0ed889fb corrected, found by `kirigami_label_icon_size`'s
  wiring test while the gate skipped them, their units not enabled). Rejected: the gate parsing every fact's
  expression whatever its unit (it parses each when the unit is enabled, before anything ships, so it would add only
  an earlier report the checker gives); the core's parser called from the checker (a build in a check that runs
  without one). A keyed list (S6.1's: the transitions, bindings and presentations) is stated as
  the query resolves it under the fact's `when`, the merged list in S6.1's order (the base's items no rule replaces,
  then each applying rule's), as every fact states the resolved value the gate compares (rejected: the applying rule's
  own patch, the other reading the ledger's question asked about, which is no resolved value and leaves the base's
  items to the reader; ADD-A125): Breeze's disabled button states the base's four transitions and its rule's two. A transition's
  `engine` is cited like any value, to the code that runs it (ADD-A126): the stylesheet's `transition` for `GtkCss`,
  the widget's `adw_animation_play` call, the `Behavior`, the `updateState` call whose test a Breeze engine quotes,
  Compose's `animateTo` or `updateTransition`, ButtonGroup's press (`EnlargeOnPressNode`,
  `material3/…/ButtonGroup.kt:994-1040`), WinUI's `BrushTransition` or storyboard, the template's `AnimatedIcon` with
  its `Source` and `State` setters (`CommonStyles/CheckBox_themeresources.xaml:604-608`), GtkSwitch's slide. Where no
  cached source states the engine (`macos-*`'s and `ios-*`'s transitions, Mica's change in an inactive window on
  `windows-11`, W3-10), the transition is a pending fact (below) and the preset states none, as `engine` is required
  only where a transition is stated: the part's list, or a single transition (a `FocusIndicator.transition`,
  MAC-X11), has nothing beneath its pending facts and is listed in the preset's `[pending]` table with its register
  id (U181, U184; *A pending fact with nothing beneath it*, below, ADD-A128), never stated `[]` or `"absent"`, which
  would say the platform animates nothing where it animates something not yet measured, and the gate lists them with
  their register ids until S2.7's measurement adds the member and the transitions. A value the
  specification itself defines (S9.4's `token.text.font_dpi` of 72 on the Apple presets, S4.5's empty
  `token.icons.animated_visuals` on every preset but `windows-11`, ADD-A131) has no fact: the gate
  compares the resolved value with the definition (ADD-A125).
- **Fields.** `key`, `value`, `rows` and at least one `cite` are required, except on a pending fact, which has `pending` in
  place of `value` and no `cite` (below), and on a labelled mapping whose value holds no literal, which has none (*A
  labelled mapping*, below; ADD-A147); `when` is optional (no condition); `mapping` is a labelled mapping's alone;
  `scheme_file` (`<entry> <path>`, a `sources.toml` entry and the scheme file's path in it) and `accent` (a colour
  literal) are the accent run's, both or neither, in the `kde` directory only, a fact with them holding one `scheme:`
  condition in its `when` (*The accent run*, ADD-A142), and `accent` alone is `material-3`'s
  accent run's, in the `material` directory only (ADD-A134; refused until that run is built, ADD-A145). `rows` lists gap-map row IDs as the
  gap maps write them (`†` included), and is `[]` only for a state-model entry or combination no row names; palette facts leave
  it out (below). Per citation, by `kind`:

  | `kind` | required | optional | not allowed |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `published` | `source`, `quote` | `conversion`, `absent` | `evidence`, `tolerance`, `inputs` |
  | `read` | `source`, `quote` | `conversion` | `evidence`, `tolerance`, `absent`, `inputs` |
  | `measured` | `evidence`, `tolerance` | `conversion`, `inputs` (a measured derivation, below) | `source`, `quote`, `absent` |

  A `measured` citation names no `source`: its evidence run's README names the harness and its commit. `tolerance` is
  a number in the value's canonical unit (a colour's per 8-bit channel, alpha included; channels compare on the 0–255
scale unclamped, so one outside the gamut lies outside `0..=255`, while a colour measured from drawn pixels is compared
with the resolved colour as the platform draws it, S2.1's hand-over; ADD-A128). A tolerance is at most the precision
  the analysis's method gives the value, its error bound, which the analysis's docstring states (ADD-A141; the iOS
  tie-break round 4): a straight colour solved from composites over black and over white, each read to one 8-bit
  level, holds to `floor(1/α)` levels per straight channel, `α` the solved alpha, as one level of a composite is
  `1/α` levels of the channel beneath it (`read_buttons.py`'s one-level rule). Readings
  of merged runs that spread wider than that bound disagree: the fact states the reading the bound holds, or is
  pending, never a tolerance widened to hold them all. The gate has no connector, so no case
  of the hand-over's connector types is its: it draws the resolved colour as the measured platform's renderer does
  into the capture's frame, then reads it as the measured colour was read from the pixels (ADD-A131). An in-gamut
  colour draws the same in every case, so this matters only where the resolved colour leaves the gamut, and each
  renderer's rule is its source's. On `adwaita`, GTK's (S2.1): premultiplied, each premultiplied channel clamped to
  `0..=1`, so a channel `c` at alpha `a > 0` compares as `clamp(c·a, 0, 1) / a`, the alpha unchanged, and at alpha 0
  the alpha alone. On `kde-breeze`, for what QPainter draws (QStyle's parts), the same: Qt's raster engine
  premultiplies an extended-RGB colour's unclamped channels, a brush's and a filled rectangle's alike (`qtbase@6.12.0
  src/gui/painting/qpaintengine_raster.cpp:1758-1768`, `:4484-4487`, `:1782`; its opaque fast path skips such a
  colour, `:1407-1412`), and an 8-bit or 16-bit store reads them through `QColor::rgba()` or `rgba64()`
  (`src/gui/painting/qdrawhelper.cpp:3998`, `:4075`; `qcolor.cpp:1537-1541`, `:1569-1573`), which clamp each colour
  channel of an extended-RGB colour to `0..=1` (`qcolor.cpp:2348-2350`; the alpha, in range by `fromRgbF`'s check,
  `:484-487`, is not). On `material-3`, each straight channel and the alpha clamped to `0..=1` before anything draws, as
  Compose's sRGB `Color` constructor coerces them (`androidx@e4d933c9
  compose/ui/ui-graphics/src/commonMain/kotlin/androidx/compose/ui/graphics/Color.kt:413-419`), so `clamp(c, 0, 1)`,
  S2.1's third case. On `macos-*`, `ios-*`, `windows-11` and for Qt Quick's scene graph (`kde-breeze` under
  `flavor:kirigami`), no source in the cache states how the renderer draws a channel outside `0..=1`, so a measured
  drawn colour whose resolved colour leaves the gamut there fails, naming the key, until a measurement of that
  renderer (a register row) states it, never drawn by another platform's rule by assumption; none of those facts
  states a colour outside the gamut today (no `srgb(…)` or `display_p3(…)` literal in `docs/facts/macos`, `ios` or
  `windows`), so it arises only where a derivation leaves the gamut. For a value with leaves (a
  shadow's layers, a curve), the `evidence` path names a table of the evidence file shaped like the value, and
  `tolerance` is one number for every numeric leaf or a table from each numeric leaf's path in the value as S11
  spells it to its number (`{ "layers.0.y_px" = <t>, "layers.0.color" = <t> }`); leaves that are not numbers or
  colours (a bool, a name, a text value) compare as S11 spells them; a colour leaf is numeric for this rule (its tolerance per channel). Where several `measured` citations serve one generation, each must hold
  and the gate uses the smallest tolerance per leaf; where a generation has `published` or `read` citations too, both checks
  must hold and the gate uses the measured tolerance.
- **A labelled mapping** (ADD-A147; S3; the 0.8.0 plan's D6, outcome 5). A fact that states native-theme's pairing for
  a typed role (S3's three conditions) or a text slot (S3's clause for a slot) of S3's labelled mapping carries `mapping = "<what the platform names none for;
  what it is paired with>"`. Its value is the pairing: a reference to a role or style the platform's facts state (`=
  role.@system_red`, `= role.global.accent_foreground`), or a value the platform is measured drawing in that role or, for a slot, a family it names for
  the nearest uses (S3), whose literals its citations hold as any fact's
  do (the quote check, the evidence check: U651's `#ffffff`, the four measured filled-title facts' evidence; U509's
  family, the pages that name it), so the colour or font is the platform's and only the pairing is native-theme's. A
  value that is a reference alone has no `cite`: no source states a pairing, and the label says so. The status
  pairings are listed in the catalogue's *global roles*; the text slots' pairings are the facts with `mapping`,
  which the generated `platform-facts.md` shows under their label (below), the list the maintainer vetoes once M2
  task 0's second step and the lanes have written them (the catalogue's slot table, a draft of facts, marks none).
  Each pairing is open to the maintainer's veto. The gate compares the resolved value with the fact, which checks the generator and the
  resolution, and reports it apart from the platform's stated and pending facts; the independent verification
  checks the reference's target and the literals' citations, never the pairing. The generated
  `platform-facts.md` shows it under its label, and the preset carries the label (S11). Rejected: a citation kind
  of its own (a citation states where a value comes from, and the pairing comes from no source); a separate table
  beside the facts (a second place the generator and the gate would read for one value).
- **Sources** are pinned in `docs/facts/sources.toml`, whose header defines its entries: `[[source]]` entries of
  kind `git` (a repository at a release's commit, id `<name>@<version>`, or the commit's first eight hex digits where
  the project has no tag for the release), `sdk` (an SDK or a runner image on CI, id `<sdk or image>@<version>`,
  not fetched: `xcode@<version>`, whose header citations `check_fact_citations.py` checks against the copies of its
  SDK headers in the source cache, `<cache>/xcode@<version>/<Framework>/`, a citation's
  `…/<Framework>.framework/Headers/<file>` read there as `<Framework>/<file>` (UIKit's from the iPhone Simulator SDK),
  copied by `os-probe.yml`'s macOS job, Xcode 26.6's by run 42215651196 (the folder's `README.txt` and `xcode.txt`
  record the run and each file's SHA-256), no CI job checking them; a runner image or the Android emulator's system image another harness measures) and `distribution` (a
  dated package snapshot the harnesses install, which no citation names), each listing the generations (preset IDs)
  it serves, and the one `git` entry with `evidence = true`, the evidence repository, which serves none
  (`generations = []`; *The evidence root*, below); `[[site]]` documentation sites with their pinning method (their source repositories at a commit, or
  snapshots); `[[not_pinned]]` cited code that is not a platform source (the toolkits, the project's own files), with
  its reason; and a `[presets]` table naming the release each preset describes (`macos-tahoe = "macOS 26"`). A page
  snapshot is a `[[source]]` of kind `snapshot`, one per page and keyed by its id (not by generation), with its site,
  URL, date, SHA-256 and `describes` (the releases, as `[presets]` writes them, its page describes: Apple's pages the
  newest macOS and iOS releases when taken, which `[presets]` need not name), and its generations are only presets
  describing one of its `describes`: a page snapshotted while 27 is current serves no preset (`generations = []`), an
  archived snapshot from 26's lifetime serves `macos-tahoe` and `ios-26` (D12). A palette project's entry serves no generation
  (`generations = []`, `palette = true`). A citation's `source` is `<id> <path>:<line or range>` (a JSON page:
  `<id> #<JSON pointer>`; an `sdk` header: a path from the Xcode's `Contents/Developer/Platforms/`, which names the SDK),
  and it serves every generation its entry lists. `check_sources.py` checks the form (its docstring holds the id
  pattern and each kind's fields), that a snapshot's generations describe its `describes`, and that every cited
  project is pinned, a site or not pinned; it gains the `snapshot` kind, palette entries and `[presets]` when the
  first of them is written.
- **The quote check.** `quote`, whitespace-normalised, occurs in the cited lines at the pin. For each generation the
  fact covers that has a `published` or `read` citation (a palette fact: over all its citations), every literal of
  `value` (S2.2's numeric, length, duration, angle, font size and colour literals, and a text value, which equals a
  whole string as the source's notation reads it — a quoted string, a list's entry, a font description's family
  part (Pango's `'Adwaita Sans 11'`, read as Pango's font-description parser does), an unquoted INI value
  (`Theme=breeze`), from the checker's closed text notations — whitespace-normalised and
  case-sensitive; references and names are left to the verifier, a `Timing::Platform` curve's name among them, S2.7;
  no literal is exempt as a form's constant, S2.2's arithmetic stating a fallback with `if_le`, ADD-A147) equals a literal of the union of those citations' quotes, as written or after a citation's
  `conversion`, which the checker applies to its quote's literals; a generation with only `measured` citations is
  held by the evidence check alone. A quote's literals are read by its source file's notation, from closed lists
  that `scripts/check_fact_citations.py` holds, documents in its docstring and tests in its self-test: the number
  form (bounded by non-identifier characters, so `Qt6` holds no number), the colour notations (CSS, SCSS, XAML's
  `#argb` and `#aarrggbb`, Qt's and C++'s byte forms, an INI key's `r,g,b[,a]`), XAML's `TimeSpan` `[d.]h:m:s[.f]`, and
  each unit's dimension (`px`, `dp`, `sp` and logical points as px, `sp` being Android's text size before its
  scaling, S9.4; `pt`; `ms` and `s`; `deg`; `rem` and `em` have none, so a value written in them is cited where the
  platform states it in px, or measured, or, for a factor of the default font size, read through `rem_to_factor`, below); a member is added to a list, or to the conversions below, as a class 1
  change; a span the number, colour or `TimeSpan` notations read (a `TimeSpan`, a byte list) is not read again by the number
  form, while the text notations only add candidate strings and take no span. A gradient's angle, which no source
  writes as a number of degrees, is read as the angle the gradient's own notation computes, S2.3's convention: XAML's
  `LinearGradientBrush` from its start and end points (ledger queue #38, #57), and QML's `Gradient` from its
  `orientation`, `Gradient.Vertical`, the default a quote leaves out (`qtdeclarative@6.12.0
  src/quick/items/qquickrectangle_p.h:123`), 180°, and `Gradient.Horizontal` 90° (ADD-A141; U421, Kirigami's round
  button's gloss), its `GradientStop`s' positions and colours read by the number and colour notations, a QML colour
  form the facts need added to them as a class 1 change. A literal
  without a unit takes the value literal's dimension in its
  canonical unit; a literal with a unit must be of the value's dimension, px and pt being distinct, and is normalised
  within it (`0.2s` is `200ms`). Numbers are equal to a relative 1e-4, colours as 8-bit sRGB channels with alpha to
  1e-3, unclamped and unrounded (a channel may lie outside `0..=255`; ADD-A128). `conversion` is a list from a closed set, applied in order: `percent_to_fraction` (÷ 100), `byte_to_fraction`
  (÷ 255), `complement` (1 − x), `seconds_to_ms` (× 1000, for a unitless number of seconds), `ticks_to_ms` (÷ 10 000, for a
unitless number of a WinRT `TimeSpan`'s ticks, which count 100 ns (Learn *Timeline.Duration*,
`microsoft.ui.xaml.media.animation/timeline_duration.md:41` in `sources.toml`'s Windows App SDK API reference), 10 000 a
millisecond as WinUI counts them,
`microsoft-ui-xaml@2.5.1 src/dxaml/phone/lib/NavigateTransitionHelper.cpp:111`: an AnimatedVisual source's `duration`,
S2.7's `WinUiAnimatedIcon`, `AnimatedChevronDownSmallVisualSource.cpp:462`'s `TimeSpan{ 4833333L }` being 483.3333 ms,
the C++ literal's `L` suffix its type, not a unit, as in Kotlin), `negate` (−x, the quoted
  number's sign flipped: WinUI's `FocusVisualMargin`, whose negative margin is an outward distance, S2.10; ADD-A122),
  and `rem_to_factor`, each the model's own conversion, the same for every generation. `rem_to_factor` (GTK's `rem`, ledger queue #152) reads each `<n>rem`
  literal of the citation's quote as the unitless factor n, which GTK multiplies by the default font size

  GtkSettings' `gtk-font-name`, not the root widget's computed size): the fact keeps GTK's derivation,
  `= mul(token.text.roles.body.font.size, 0.75)` for libadwaita's `0.75rem`, the `body` slot, which the GNOME
  reader's `font-name` patch reaches as GTK's default font size follows the setting, not the keyed `.body` style
  (ADD-A141; the GN-C1 tie-break, which moved the facts so); without the conversion a `rem` value keeps no literal,
  so a `0.75rem` quote never holds a plain `0.75`. AppKit's width trait has no conversion: no pinned
  source maps `NSFontWidthTrait` to a percent, so a `macos-*` width is measured on the font's `wdth` axis

  point size (S9.4 converts it by the preset's font DPI). A JSON-pointer citation's quote occurs in the string value
  at the pointer. A `GtkCss` transitions fact whose transitions name several curves is checked further: its
  transitions follow its quoted CSS `transition` list item by item, in the list's order, each item's duration, delay
  and curve (S2.7; ADD-A131).

  rests on it.
