  rule needs no exemption, the preset being the bottom layer (S9.2). Rejected: the synthetic value in a layer above
  the stand-in, as for the other listed paths (it beats the perturbed value at the listed scheme, so the derivations
  reading the input there go uncompared, its per-scheme value masks the preset's contrast base there, and it meets
  the accent-input refusal and the group rule); a slot of its own beneath the reader or stand-in for every listed path
  (no fold and no mark, but its per-scheme value masks the preset's contrast base at the listed scheme just as well,
  so the normal run holds the synthetic value where the preset states a measured one, and it needs exemptions from
  both accent rules); the fold for inputs with that slot for the other listed paths (a second placement, whose one
  gain, a listed colour-role operand the perturbed run varies, no preset has). The theme `from_preset_synthetic` returns is a **synthetic theme**
  while its preset is current: every later mutation of it (`set_reader_stand_in`, `remove_reader_stand_in`, `pick`,
  `set_flavor`, `set_accent`, `set_contrast`, `apply_palette`, `add_layer`, `replace_layer`, `remove_layer`)
  validates the stack as the route does, the listed `default_size` waived, a listed presence drawn and a listed
  input's folded value kept, and a `set_preset` that succeeds ends it and removes the layers `from_preset_synthetic`
  added and the values it folded, chosen
  for that preset's listed paths (one to the same preset included, refused where a listed path no remaining layer states is left; a refused one changes
  nothing, S16), the new preset validated as on every other theme, so the gate replaces
  its stand-in per combination and changes scheme, flavour and accent through the ordinary mutations (ADD-A131;
  rejected: the waivers on the constructor alone, which the gate's first stand-in change would undo; a fresh theme
  per combination through extra constructor parameters, a doc-hidden parameter per mutation that would bypass the
  mutations the gate exercises). Those
  bases also override a stand-in's value at a listed path but an input's (S8's layer order), so a fact reading that
  reader value reaches the synthetic one. The listed paths below one entry of a map of bare blocks (S6.1: a keyed
  text style, a keyed icon context) that no base of the preset states share one synthetic layer, which creates the
  entry with every listed field stated, as a base creating it would (S12's created entry): one layer per path would
  create the entry with the other fields unset and be refused whatever its value, the case below of no single value,
  whose real shape is a keyed icon context no fact of `macos-tahoe` measures yet (ADD-A133; rejected: stating the
  unmeasured fields to create the entry, values no fact gives; judging the per-path layers together for the entry's
  creation alone, a second rule where one layer is the same and simpler). The route validates its layers with the
  preset in one pass, which gives each layer what a check over the layers beneath it alone would give only while no
  layer's value reads another's or is masked by it: so, past the fold of the listed inputs (above), it refuses a
  layer value stated as an expression (`ProblemKind::SyntheticExpression`: a synthetic value is a constant of its
  path's type, chosen in the gate's source, above) and a place a layer states where an earlier of its layers states one at, above
  or below it, a list's items taken as the list (`ProblemKind::SyntheticOverlap`: the listed paths are disjoint, none
  below another, one layer per path or per map entry), naming each place, with S12's problems in
  `ThemeError::Preset(LayerError::Invalid)` (ADD-A134). The gate's own layers meet neither; a hand-written `[pending]`
  table listing a block and one of its fields, or a caller passing its own layers, can. They are the route's two
  refusals, no S12 item, so `ProblemKind` has a variant for each beside S12's and the TOML reader's (S1). Rejected:
  validating the stack once per layer prefix (a pass per listed path, for a shape the gate never makes); no check (a
  stack of that shape would load, judged wrongly by the one pass). S12 validates the synthetic values as stated, as it validates any
  layer's (ADD-A131): each is a value S12 accepts at its place, beside the values the preset states and the other
  synthetic ones (never `Absent` where a conditional mark refuses it there, no `FollowPart` corner beside unequal
  offsets), chosen so in the gate's source, one value per listed path accepted at every combination it reaches, which the
  build test checks by validating the synthetic layers over the preset; where no such single value exists (none is
  known), the build test fails with S12's problems and names the listed paths whose synthetic values the refused
  stack holds, and the case takes a spec row when it first appears, with its real shape; a refusal that disappears
  with the preset's facts measured is the gate's choice of values to fix, any other the preset's. A check that passes on a synthetic
  value and would fail on the real one is found when the fact is measured: the preset is regenerated with the measured value stated and
  validated with it (through S19.1's build test once its table is empty; ADD-A147), and every table is empty at each release, so nothing it misses ships. Rejected: ADD-A128's
  reading of a listed path as able to take any value of its type (it includes values S12 itself refuses, so a preset
  listing a whole focus indicator, an edge or a conditionally marked field could never load, and the repairs it
  needs, a joint reading of every listed value against the checks across fields, are machinery that serves only the
  build, which a refusal found later, at the cost of a regeneration, does not warrant).
  The gate checks that the table holds exactly the preset's listed paths, each with exactly the ids of the pending
  facts, or of the state model's pending `default_size`, that leave it listed (compared as sets, ADD-A131), compares every other fact as before,
  skips every fact whose evaluation reaches a synthetic value (the synthetic value itself, any value referencing it,
  a reader-backed fact at a listed path; a listed input's folded value where it is the value in force, at its scheme
  under no contrast or a contrast the preset states no base for, and no layer above gives one; ADD-A132), reporting each, which costs coverage and nothing else, while the facts
  where the preset's rules state the path are compared, and reports each listed path with its id; each release is made
  with every `[pending]` table empty (the tables listing the enabled units' paths alone, as the preset holds only
  those), as R21 and
  ADD-A122 require of pending facts. Rejected: the preset left out of the bundle (the gate then resolves none of its
  facts, M1a design decision 7, against the plan's queue of every preset per unit); a `Pending` answer of the query, and
  `PresetPending` variants of `ThemeError` and `LayerError` (each a permanent API and variant, which the refusal
  test must trigger, for a state that ends before the release); S6.1's deferral of the field
  from its unit (it removes the field from every preset and context, and a pending leaf may be a leaf of a type
  every context shares, as `IconStyle`'s fields are); a placeholder value or `Absent` (both
  invented: `Absent` says the platform draws nothing where it draws something not yet measured); an earlier
  generation's value, a fact of another release that the release described need not share.
- **A measured derivation** (a value that follows an input, as a default button's fill follows the accent) has a
  `measured` citation with `inputs`, the references of its expression the harness varied as written there
  (`inputs = ["input.accent"]`). Its `evidence` path names a list of tables in a TOML evidence file, each a pass:
  the varied references as quoted keys (`"input.accent" = "#ff0000"`), `result` (the value measured) and
  `conditions` (the pass's conditions, including its `scheme:` condition, required unless the fact's `when` fixes
  the scheme), every value spelled as a
  fact's `value` is (units written: `"4px"`, `"17pt"`; `conversion` does not apply to them); every other operand resolves from the preset under the fact's
  `when` plus the pass's `conditions` (a list of condition strings, as `when.conditions` writes them), so `inputs`
  lists every operand that changes with the varied input. The checker checks the form: for each input and each
  scheme the fact covers, two passes that differ in that input alone, by more than its own type's quote-check precision, and whose results
  differ by more than `tolerance` (a per-leaf table: in some leaf, by more than that leaf's); `inputs` only
  on an expression value, an expression value's `measured` citation always with `inputs`, and no `conversion` beside
  `inputs`. The gate evaluates the
  expression over each pass within `tolerance`. It is the one case where the evidence value is not compared with the
  fact's value directly (ADD-A120).
- **`read`** facts state the reference the key takes from a reader input (`value = "= input.accent"`); the quote is the
  API's declaration at the pinned source or SDK; the gate checks them as derivations (the perturbed run changes the
  input).
- **`evidence`** (`measured`): a file under `docs/evidence/<harness>/<date>-run-<id>/<image>/`, committed in the
  evidence repository (*The evidence root*, below), and the path of the value inside it, in the file type's form (a dotted key in TOML, written as TOML writes one, a key that is no
  bare key, one holding a dot among them, quoted as a basic string, `macos.symbols."chevron.forward".size`, and a
  bare decimal key indexing an array where the value there is one and naming a table's key otherwise, the fact's `evidence` then a literal string, `'…#macos.symbols."chevron.forward".size'`,
  so the quotes need no escape: the form the fact keys and S11 already use for a map entry, ADD-A136; a JSON pointer in JSON, `<group>/<key>` in an
  INI file such as kdeglobals, a nested group written as its bracketed names joined by `][`,
  `Colors:Header][Inactive/BackgroundNormal`; `<first column>/<header>` in CSV); for a value read from an image, the committed output of
  a committed analysis script naming its input image and the pixels it reads; for a value computed from values a
  harness read (AppKit's padding, the distance from the alignment rect to the union of the title and image rects,
  three API reads, `docs/evidence/os-probe/2026-10-30-run-41006842699/README.md`), the committed output of a committed
  analysis script naming the files it reads and stating in its docstring the arithmetic it applies, so the method is
  reviewed where it runs and the fact cites its result as it cites an image's (ADD-A125). Every analysis output names
  its input files in its top-level `input_image`, images or not (the key the checker reads, its name kept from the
  image analyses: renaming it to `inputs` would rewrite every committed analysis output and the checker for no change
  of meaning, so the name stays and its meaning is stated here). Rejected: a `subtract` conversion (a conversion maps
  one quoted literal, and the value is a difference of read rects); the arithmetic as the fact's expression (an
  expression is the platform's derivation, which the query evaluates, not the probe's method). The value there, after `conversion`
  (applied to it, read as the quote's literals are), equals the fact's within `tolerance` (a measured derivation's
  passes are checked as its bullet says). The run folder's
  `run.toml` maps each image folder to the preset it serves, the `sources.toml` entry of what it measured (the Xcode,
  the distribution snapshot, the WinUI host's Windows App SDK, the emulator image; a runner image measured with no
  such entry gets one of kind `sdk` naming the image) and its exact builds (`[images.os-probe-macos-26]
  preset = "macos-tahoe"`, `source = "xcode@26.6"`, `os = "<build>"`, `toolkit = "<build>"`, the last where a toolkit
  drew or answered); the checker requires the others and that the preset is among the entry's generations. The builds are recorded, not matched: a runner image
  moves within a release (D1). Where two builds of the release a preset describes read one fact differently beyond
  its tolerance (`macos-tahoe`'s facts mix macOS 26.6.2 and 26.7.2 readings, the macOS measured verifier's report),
  the newest build's reading is the fact's, as R1.5 has a preset describe the newest release a supported runner
  measures (D12), and the older build's citation leaves that fact; its file stays evidence while another fact,
  model entry or vector table cites it, and one that loses its last citation leaves the evidence repository's tree in
  the commit the pin moves to, its history keeping it, as ADD-A136 leaves data no citation reads on the harness's
  branch, so every evidence file stays cited (below); where they agree, both cite it (ADD-A141; the macOS tie-break round 7). The SDK entry a run names follows the
  same rule: `xcode@26.6` serves `macos-tahoe` while the newest runner build's Xcode is 26.6, and a newer Xcode on the
  newest build is pinned as its own entry with its header copies. Rejected: the older build (the first measured, no
  reason the platform gives); a tolerance wide enough for both (a value no one build draws); a condition per build
  (the model has none, and R1.5 rejects a per-release overlay). Every evidence file is cited by a fact, a state-model entry or a
  vector table (S2.2, S13), or is the input of a cited analysis output (its `input_image`, above): a recording
  and the crop the harness cut its frames with (`transition-caret.mov` and `.crop`, run 42272240639) are data: the
  analysis that reads the frames names them in its `input_image`, as the files the frames were cut from. Not evidence: a run's README and `run.toml`, and its records, the
  files a harness writes about its own conduct, from which no fact's value is read (`run.toml` takes its builds from
  `environment.txt`), held by name in a closed list of
  `check_fact_citations.py` (a member added as a class 1 change): `settings.txt` (the settings a pass wrote and read
  back) and `environment.txt` (the image's OS, Xcode and SDK builds) (ADD-A136; rejected: every record required
  to be an analysis's input, which most are to none (one an analysis reads, as it may read a pass's settings, it
  names all the same); records left out of the repository, which show the conditions a pass
  ran under, as a review checks them; an exemption by file type, which would pass an uncited table or image written
  as text). A run's data no fact,
  state-model entry, vector table or analysis reads yet stays on the harness's branch until one does: a run brought
  into the facts branch brings its read files and its records;
  the runs the 0.8.0 plan lists as legacy count as cited until its M4.
- **The evidence root** (ADD-A137). Evidence is committed to the evidence repository (the 0.8.0 plan's *The evidence
  repository*), whose tree holds `docs/evidence/` at the paths this section writes, never to this repository, which
  from the plan's switch holds no file under `docs/evidence/`. `sources.toml` pins it by one `[[source]]` of kind
  `git` with `evidence = true`: id `native-theme-evidence` (the one id without `@<version>`, so a moved pin keeps its
  checkout), `repository`, `commit`, `tag = "commit"`, `generations = []` and a `note`, and no `project`, `release`,
  `researched` or `proof`; `check_sources.py` requires exactly one such entry and waives for it alone the rules it
  breaks (`release`, `researched` and `proof` required, `generations` not empty, the `<name>@<version>` id). A path
  `docs/evidence/<rest>` (a citation's `evidence`, an analysis output's `input_image`, a vector table's cell, a legacy
  run) names `<root>/docs/evidence/<rest>`, the root being, in this order: a test fixture's root holding its own
  `docs/evidence/`, which needs no git checkout and no pin; else the directory `NATIVE_THEME_EVIDENCE` names; else the
  entry's checkout in the source cache (`<cache>/native-theme-evidence/`). Outside a fixture every reader (the
  checkers, the generators that read evidence, the gate) requires the root to be a clean git checkout
  (`git status --porcelain --ignored --untracked-files=all` prints nothing, ignored files counting) whose HEAD is the pinned
  commit, and fails otherwise, as it fails without a root; an evidence file is committed when it is in that commit's
  tree. The rules on which files a run holds, ADD-A136's records exempt by name (`settings.txt`, `environment.txt`)
  among them, apply inside the evidence repository unchanged.
- **Generations.** Facts are one directory per platform (and `palettes/`, S14, whose facts have no generation),
  covering its presets: `gnome` (`adwaita`), `kde`
  (`kde-breeze`), `macos` (`macos-monterey`, `macos-tahoe`), `ios` (`ios-13`, `ios-26`), `windows` (`windows-11`),
  `material` (`material-3`); `docs/facts/imported/`, the 0.8.0 plan's lane input, is not facts. A fact for one
  generation carries `preset:<id>` (S7.1) in
  its `when`, and every citation of it serves that generation; a fact without one has citations that together serve
  each generation its directory covers among the presets that exist, a citation's generations being its source
  entry's or its evidence file's. Where two generations' sources order the facts differently, the facts are split by
  `preset:`.
- **The gate's tolerance** for a key is the measured tolerance of the generation the resolved preset serves (above,
  the smallest where several citations serve it); a generation with only `published` or `read` citations compares at
  the quote check's precision.

`docs/platform-facts.md` is generated from these files (a script), and the two existing scripts read the data. It is
not committed (ADD-A147; the 0.8.0 plan's D6, outcome 8): CI and each release generate it, the gates run the
generator and its self-test, and a tool that cites its lines reads the facts or a generated copy, so a citation of
its lines names the commit it was generated at. Rejected: committing it (50,121,732 bytes at the slice, near GitHub's
50 MiB warning, and growing with every measured fact; GitHub renders no file of that size, so the committed copy had no
reader).

**State models** (`docs/facts/<platform>/state-models.toml`, cited): per widget, the combinations the platform
draws (states × conditions × contexts × variants × sizes, R4), the exclusive groups' order of precedence, the
recency sets with their stated order, and the source of each (the catalogue's "state-model source" line points here). They also state each preset's declarations
(S10's platform declarations of a widget: `available`, `variants`, `sizes`, `default_size`,
`densities`, `flags`, `exclusive`, `exclusive_variants`, `recency`, `requires_variants`,
`sizes_by_variant`, `sizes_by_context`), and the gate checks each preset's
declarations against them (ADD-A116), each entry citing as a fact does:

```toml
[[model]]
widget = "pull_to_refresh"                        # a typed widget, or "component.<key>"
when = { conditions = ["preset:macos-tahoe"] }    # optional: one generation's (or flavour's, `flavor:`) entry
available = false                                 # S10's declarations; with `false`, no other declaration
rows = []

[[model.cite]]
kind = "published"
source = "<entry> <header path>:<l1>-<l2>"
quote = "<the @interface line>"
absent = ["<the platform's name for it>"]
```

An available widget's entry also states `variants`, `sizes`, `densities` (S10; `exclusive_variants`, `variant_sets`
and `variant_products` are optional, absent meaning none), `axes = { states, conditions,
contexts }` (what the platform's drawing distinguishes: states by S1's `StateFlag` names, conditions by S7.1's,
contexts as S11's context selectors), `exclusive` (the exclusive groups, each in its order of precedence, S10),
`recency` (the recency sets, each in its stated order, cited for its members and for the order's reason, S10;
absent meaning none; ADD-A124), a group or a set of some elements only spelt as the declaration spells it, `{ parts =
[ … ], flags = [ … ] }` (S10's *Groups and sets per element*; `check_facts.py` checks `parts` as S12 does; ADD-A146),
`exclusive_variants` (S10), `variant_sets` (the sets of two or more variants the platform draws together on one
element, each a list, `variant_sets = [["glass", "primary"], ["clear", "primary"]]`; none where it draws its variants
one at a time; ADD-A121) and `variant_products` (the same sets as products of groups, below; ADD-A122) and `not_drawn` (combinations the platform does not draw, as `when`s); `available` is always stated, and a declaration
it leaves out is stated as none (no flags, no `requires_variants`, no `default_size` where `sizes` is empty, …) and
checked so; `default_size` is stated wherever `sizes` is not empty (S10), as `default_size = { pending = "U<n>" }`
while no source or evidence gives it yet, and a `sizes_by_variant` or `sizes_by_context` entry's `default_size` so too (S10's *A pending default*, ADD-A131), a pending measurement (*A pending measurement*, above: its id a register
row's, which `check_ledger.py` checks as a pending fact's and `--final` refuses as one). The preset then states no
`default_size` there and lists the declaration in its `[pending]` table (`"declare.widget.button.sizes_by_variant.@gray.default_size" = "U<n>"`, as U129 stood before run 42269041636 settled it,
*A pending fact with nothing beneath it*, above): `from_preset` refuses it as S12's missing default size, while
`from_preset_synthetic` waives S12's default-size checks for the listed declaration, the checks that read it (its
presence, its being one of `sizes`, and the `sizes_by_variant` and `sizes_by_context` entries holding it; the others
stand), and states no value for it, the query
answering an element that states no size and whose default is pending `NotAvailable(Size)` there (S10, S8);
the gate loses nothing by it, as no combination tests an element that states no size (below), no fact reads the
declaration, and it reports the listed declaration with its id as any listed path (ADD-A131). Rejected: the preset
refused on every route until the row is decided (the gate would resolve none of its facts, the reason S17 rejects
leaving a preset out of the bundle); a synthetic default the route picks from `sizes` (a value with a selection rule
of its own and no mark a layer carries, since no layer states a declaration, where waiving the check needs neither);
a value written in the state model meanwhile (invented). `check_facts.py` refuses an entry where, for a variant set
and a context it draws (none included), the default size in force there (the `default_size` of the first `sizes_by_context` entry whose selector the
ancestors the gate builds for that context match, S17's chain, where it states one, else the first matching `sizes_by_variant` entry's `default_size`,
else `default_size`, S10) is
one the entry draws in no combination with that set in that context (its `not_drawn` excluding every one), as an element stating no
size would then resolve at a size the platform never draws it at, which no fact tests, and a `sizes_by_context`
entry whose selector no `axes.contexts` entry's ancestors match, a declaration no fact checks; where the first default this order
reaches is pending, no default is in force for that set and context until it is stated (S10's *A pending default*),
and nothing is checked for it (ADD-A131). Flavours are not an axis: a preset with flavours is checked
once per flavour (below). A combination is a subset of `axes.states` (each
state a flag) reduced by `exclusive`, for each element the gate queries by the groups that apply to it (S10;
ADD-A146), and, where it holds two or more flags of a recency set that applies to that element, ordered (one combination
per order of its flags that belong to a recency set, the orders giving every set the same latest flag counted once;
an element whose connector reports no order resolves as under one of them, so it is checked with them; a widget whose
sets hold n flags together gives at most n! orders per combination, Material's widest, the card's and the chip's,
four flags and so 24; ADD-A124),
with, from `axes.conditions`, one value or none per condition kind (a
container size being a condition, one size per container), at most one of `axes.contexts` (an entry a context
selector, or a list of them for nested contexts, an ordered chain, outermost first, the element inside each: a toolbar
inside WinUI's tabbed command bar, `[{ widget = "component.tabbed_command_bar" }, { widget = "toolbar", part = "bar"
}]`, which the gate builds as that chain of ancestors, while a fact's `when.context`, a conjunction, lists its
matches in any order; rejected: several independent contexts in one combination, which builds every subset of the
ancestors and grows combinatorially, and a `when.context` that keeps the chain's order, where a conjunction's order
means nothing and the chain alone needs one; ADD-A125), from `variants` none,
a single variant, or one of the sets `variant_sets` lists or `variant_products` gives (so a platform's dozens of variants are never combined into sets it does
not draw, and no fact is asked for one),
one of `densities` or none, and one of the sizes the element takes (S10: its variant's entry, else `sizes`, less
those its context's entry leaves out; none where it takes none; an element stating no size is the default size's,
no combination of its own; ADD-A131), less those `not_drawn` names and those `requires_variants` excludes
(ADD-A121). A listed set names only
declared variants, holds at most one variant of each `exclusive_variants` group (S10) and is listed once, which
`check_facts.py` checks.

**What the axes and sets hold** (ADD-A141; the KD-C1, GN-C1 and WN-C1 verifiers' questions). `variant_sets` and
`variant_products` together give every set of variants the platform draws on one element, never a sample: a set the
platform draws that the entry leaves out is a defect of the model, as a missing state is (the KDE facts' round 6 added
the KD-C1 verifier's 278; on `ios-*` the system type with an image and a menu, with a menu on hold, and with an image
and a toggle, which the gate met only where a fact's own `when` named them, the iOS facts lane's round 5, c8610c67),
so the gate checks each set whether a fact names it or not. Every flag the entry's `flags` declares is in `axes.states`: a declared flag is one some
rule selects on (S12 refuses a keyed flag none does), so it changes what is drawn, and outside the axes no
combination would hold it (`@keyboard_focus_change`, which 22 KDE facts select on while the combinations never held
it, KD-C1); `check_facts.py` refuses a declared flag the axes leave out. `axes.conditions` holds the conditions under
which the platform draws the widget's own values differently; a condition that reaches the widget only through a
value its facts reference (a token's rule: the speed factor under `animations_off`) is checked at that value's facts,
whose combinations hold it, and the verifiers' comparison opens it at the widget (`verify_facts.py`'s resolver,
f9fb16e4); rejected: every such condition in every widget's axes (each doubles a widget's combinations to check what
the referenced value's facts already check). A variant the platform draws only inside a host (a nested button:
AutoSuggestBox's query button, `@query`; the pager's `@first`) is declared with its host's context in
`axes.contexts` and not drawn outside it (`{ variants = ["@query"], not_context = [{ widget = "autocomplete" }] }`),
even while the host's unit is not enabled: the gate skips the host's combinations until it is (*While the units are
built*, below) and checks the variant nowhere else, so no combination the platform never draws is asked for, and
enabling the host's unit changes no state model. Rejected: such variants left out until their hosts' units (a
model short of what the platform draws); the variant declared with no host context (the gate would check it at the
top level, drawn as the base, where the platform never draws it).

**Variant products** (ADD-A122). Where the sets a platform draws are the combinations of independent choices
(libadwaita's button: a content form, a shape, a colour style, a toggle, each class set or not), an entry states them
as `variant_products` beside or in place of `variant_sets`: a list of products, each a list of groups, a group
`{ any = [...] }` (at most one of its variants, or none) or `{ one = [...] }` (exactly one). A product's sets are
every choice of one variant or none from each `any` group and one from each `one` group, keeping those of two or more
variants and dropping those that hold two variants of an `exclusive_variants` group or that `requires_variants`
excludes; they join `variant_sets`' sets, and `not_drawn` then removes combinations as for any set. So

```toml
variant_products = [
  [{ any = ["icon_only", "with_icon", "@custom_child"] },                     # the content form
   { any = ["pill", "circular"] },                                            # the shape
   { any = ["primary", "destructive", "flat", "@raised", "@opaque", "@osd"] },  # the colour style
   { any = ["toggle"] }],
  [{ one = ["with_icon"] }, { one = ["@image_text_box"] },                    # with `with_icon` only
   { any = ["pill", "circular"] },
   { any = ["primary", "destructive", "flat", "@raised", "@opaque", "@osd"] },
   { any = ["toggle"] }],
  [{ one = ["menu"] },                                                        # a menu button
   { any = ["icon_only", "with_icon", "@custom_child"] },
   { any = ["@with_arrow"] },
   { any = ["flat", "@raised", "@osd"] }],
]
```

states three products in fourteen lines where the list would hold hundreds of sets (the group members here show the
form, the adwaita facts' own lists cite theirs). `check_facts.py` expands the products, checks each set as a listed
one (declared variants, once over the list and the products together: a set a product already gives is not listed
again; the exclusive groups on the listed sets only, as the products' trimming drops every set they would refuse),
refuses a product naming one variant in two of its groups, and prints the number of sets per widget, so the expansion is reviewed by its count and
its groups, each group's members cited as the plain list's are. Two products may give the same set (groups of
independent choices can overlap); the products' sets form a set, so such a set is counted once in that number and
checked once by the gate. The gate checks every set the entry gives, never a
sample, so a set the platform draws cannot pass unchecked; M1a task 14 bounds the cost by resolving each set's
combinations once per scheme and flavour and reusing what the set's rules share, not by checking fewer. Rejected:
the plain list alone, unreviewable at that size; and products left untrimmed, which would assert sets the platform
does not draw, so the exclusive groups, `requires_variants` and `not_drawn` trim them as they trim listed sets.

**Sets not yet measured** (ADD-A141; the MC-C1 tie-break, U695). Where the sets are drawn but no pass measured them,
a key's look on a set is unknown exactly where two of its variants each state their own facts of the key: one
pending fact per such pair, `when` naming the two variants and placed after both, covers every set holding the pair,
and a set whose variants state the key once at most takes that fact, as S17's *Which fact applies* gives it, each
variant's facts being its own look over the base's. A measured pair replaces its pending fact by the measured value,
or by a decision that the pair's looks compose (one variant's facts holding on the other's sets), recorded per key.
Rejected: one pending fact per set and key (`macos-tahoe`'s 1,209 sets each listed where the pairs cover them, the
gate's memory a known limit); no pending fact (the later variant's fact on the set, a composition no evidence shows);
a pending fact on every set holding a variant with facts of its own (the sets where the look follows from one
variant's facts would wait on a measurement they do not need).

The gate also resolves each fact's own
`when`, so a fact naming a size class, a position or a direction is checked too. A fact's own combination is its
`when`'s positive lists completed with what the widget requires and nothing else: where the widget requires a form
(`requires_variants`, any one of which draws it, S10) and the `when` names none of them, it is completed once with
each required form the `when` does not exclude and no variant it names shares an `exclusive_variants` group with
(ADD-A146; rejected: the first such form alone, an order the declaration happens to have, as for a size's styles,
below); where that
completion is one the state model does not draw, for a size or a variant its named variants lack (`ios-13`'s 94
facts naming `mini`, `small` or `large` and no style, which only the configuration styles take, `sizes_by_variant`;
52 "not available (Size)" failures in the iOS facts lane's round 5) or by `not_drawn`, it is completed once with each
variant, or set, the state model draws that makes it drawn (for a size, each `sizes_by_variant` entry whose `sizes`
hold it), each completion the declarations and `not_drawn` leave drawn checked, an undrawn one no failure; a `when` no completion makes drawn holds in no combination the platform draws, a finding of the
fact, not a skip (ADD-A141). The gate completes a size by its styles so (`complete`, `native-theme/tests/facts_gate/run.rs`,
with the fixture `own_size_styles`); the completion with each required form, where it takes the first today, and
with each variant or set where the lack is not a size's are the gate's work at M4 (ADD-A146). Rejected: the first such style alone (the lane's proposal: an
order the entries happen to have picks the one style that checks a fact claiming them all, and a fact naming a
condition outside the axes would be checked on that style only); the style required in the `when` (a size's look
held by every style would be split into a fact per style, the same value each); the combination skipped (a fact
naming a condition outside the axes would go unchecked). A preset with flavours is checked
once per flavour, each with its flavour's entries. An entry with
`preset:` (or `flavor:`) replaces the shared entry of its widget for that preset (or flavour). `check_facts.py` checks
the names against the catalogue's entry, `check_fact_citations.py` the citations, `check_facts_trace.py` counts their
`rows`. **While the units are built** (ADD-A128, ADD-A135), the 0.8.0 plan enables the catalogue's units one by one,
a unit entering the model in the commit whose presets state it (S6.1), 0.8.0 releasing the units of its scope and
each follow-up release its own (the plan's D13, S21.1). A fact is of the enabled units when its key lies in an
enabled unit, every widget its `when`'s positive lists name (`context`, its `scope.nearest`, a `widget`) and the
widget a `drawn_as` value names are enabled, and its `when` holds in at least one combination of the enabled units'
names (each entry's Depth line, the units of depth enabled) that its state model draws, its part drawn there; the
gate skips every other fact, its later unit being the first in the units file's order whose names make it hold
(ADD-A146, ADD-A147). A key that belongs to no widget (a colour role, an input, a token) is judged under the condition
sets the catalogue's *today's fields* table names for it (the scheme and `contrast_high`, `window_inactive` for the
`selection` set, `animations_off` and `reduced_motion` for the speed factor and the motion values' tokens) and the
preset's default flavour. A part whose presence fact is pending counts as drawn. A bundled preset mentions no name
outside the enabled units': a negative entry naming one (`not_context`, `not_variants`, `not_states`,
`not_conditions`, `not_sizes`) is left out of its rule, and its exclusive groups and recency sets list the enabled
units' flags. Its negative lists (`not_context`, `not_variants`) never add a unit: `not_context X` applies
everywhere but inside X, and where X's unit is not enabled no X exists, so the negation holds and the fact applies
everywhere, in its key's unit alone, as the gate already reads a negation naming a widget the model does not hold
(the macOS and iOS button facts stated with a `not_context` and no positive context, 1868 and 1574 of them). A skipped fact (a
fact whose key the model does not hold yet, *The gate*, below, being one case) is drawn in none of its combinations
by the gate (as `generate_preset.py` leaves them out); at run time an element under a given name outside the enabled
units' resolves as without it (S10), the bundled preset mentioning no such name (ADD-A147); a combination that holds
a name outside the enabled units' (a variant or a set holding one, a size, a density, a state, a host context or one
naming a widget whose unit is not enabled, a position, a direction, a condition) is not drawn. The declarations check
compares each preset's declarations with the state model's names that the model's types can spell (a typed variant
no enabled unit holds is skipped, as a fact whose key the model does not hold), its exclusive groups, recency sets
and keyed `flags` with the state model's restricted to the enabled units' flags (a keyed flag only where a fact of
the enabled units names it), and its `later.variants` with the state model's keyed variants of units not enabled,
each declared typed variant the model holds that the entry's Depth line does not list, and its typed variants of
enabled units that it draws in no combination of their names (S10). A variant of the
enabled units that no fact names draws as the rules that apply give it, with none as the base, which the lane states
by leaving it so (libadwaita's unchecked `toggle`) (ADD-A147). Every unit of a release is enabled by that release, so
no fact of the enabled units is skipped then, a fact of a later release's unit skipped as before; from the last
follow-up release no fact is skipped.

**Palette facts** (`docs/facts/palettes/<project>.toml`, S14): the colours a project publishes, one fact per colour
and flavour, keyed `<project>.<flavour>.<the project's name>` (`catppuccin.mocha.surface0`; `<project>` the file's
stem, `<flavour>` the project's own name for the variant, its scheme's where it has one), with a colour literal and
the facts' citations; they have no `when`, no `rows` (no gap-map row carries them) and no generations, their source
entry being the project's at its pin with `generations = []`. `check_facts.py` checks that every value of a bundled
palette's `[palette.sources]` is a palette-fact key, and that every colour literal the palette states is in exactly one
of `[palette.sources]` and `[palette.picks]` (S11, S14).

**The palette run** (ADD-A146). The gate resolves every bundled palette over each preset it has a source for, under
each scheme the palette declares, in the no-reader state (S16) with the palette applied and no other layer. On each
preset and scheme where the mapping is the palette's source, it compares each colour `[palette.sources]` names, by
its TOML path, with its palette fact, where the preset declares the path: a typed role or surface set the preset
does not declare is skipped there (S12, S14), and a `for_preset.<id>.…` path is compared on the preset `<id>`
alone. A path compared on no preset fails the run, a mapped colour nothing checks. A preset and scheme a port
serves is not compared: the mapping's paths resolve to the port's colours there, the port is the project's own
file, converted mechanically, and the conversion is the accent run's to check (below), each bundled port being
validated by the build test (S19.1). The run resolves the base conditions alone, so a preset rule that would undo
a mapped role under a condition is S12's refusal, not the run's (S12, S14).

**Which fact applies.** Facts in a file are ordered as the platform's source orders them (CSS order for libadwaita,
visual-state order for WinUI, branch order for Breeze), so their order is the platform's, independent of the preset's
rule order. A pending fact has no source position: it stands among the facts of its key and combination, after those
that hold where it does (below), and is exempt from source order. For a key and a combination, the fact that applies is the **last** in file order whose `when` holds, after
the exclusive groups' reduction (S10), a pending fact applying as any fact does. A fact's `when` may state
`latest` (S11's spelling, `latest = { elevation = "hover" }`), the notation for an order: it holds where the
combination's order makes that flag its set's latest, and a fact without it holds under every order (ADD-A124). The gate fails a pending fact that a later fact of its key
shadows on any combination its `when` holds in (it would not apply there, and the combination would pass with the
later fact's value), so a pending fact stands after the facts that hold where it does, its `when` narrowed
(`not_states`, …) where a later fact is more specific. A later fact that is itself pending is exempt (ADD-A135;
ledger queue #164 (3)): the combination stays pending, listed with the later fact's id, and passes nothing silently;
once that fact is replaced by a value, the earlier one is shadowed by a value and fails, so its `when` is narrowed
then, where the narrowing follows the measured fact. `check_facts.py` and the gate apply the exemption alike. Rejected:
narrowing the earlier pending fact under every later pending one (a lane's added state narrowed 1311 earlier pending
facts, each narrowing undone or redone when the later fact is measured); exempting only a later fact with the same
register id (a combination two rows wait on is pending either way). Where the platform states a combination ({checked, hover} in GN-1.29), its
facts state it, and a preset that forgot it fails. A fact with `scheme_file` and `accent` (below) applies only in the
accent run, for that scheme file and accent, and on `material-3` one with `accent` alone only in its accent run, for
that accent; the other runs consider only facts without them.

**The gate** (`native-theme/tests/facts_gate.rs`): it resolves each platform preset with a stand-in `ReaderState` and no
reader, so the machine's own settings never enter: by default the no-reader state's conditions (S16) under each
scheme in turn, factor 1 and no font DPI of its own (`font_dpi: None`, so the preset's token converts its points). For every widget and
every combination of its state model, it replaces the stand-in with one holding the combination's reader conditions (and
passes its window conditions in `WindowConditions`), resolves, and queries the element, its `state_order` the
combination's order (S8), and compares each key with the
fact that applies (within tolerance; S9.4's Apple `font_dpi` and S4.5's empty `animated_visuals`, which have no fact, with their definitions), and, for a measured derivation, also evaluates its expression over each
evidence pass under the pass's conditions; a key and combination with no fact fails (R4), but for a part's own key,
which with no part fact is expected drawn (below). **A part not drawn**
(ADD-A130): where the query answers `NotDrawn` or `DrawnAs` for a part, the gate asks no fact for that part's
fields and compares none of them, and a field's fact that applies there is no failure either. A field's facts state
the part's look wherever it is drawn; whether it is drawn is the part's own key (`<widget>.<part>`), compared under
every combination: where a part fact applies, its `absent` or `drawn_as` against the query's `NotDrawn` or `DrawnAs`;
where none applies, the part must be drawn, its own style (`Styled::Style`), so a `NotDrawn` or `DrawnAs` answer there
fails. So a part the preset leaves out where the facts draw it fails, and one it draws where a fact says `absent`
likewise, and that one fact has one home. libadwaita states its menu arrow's look in `menubutton`'s `arrow` block for every arrow
(`libadwaita@1.10.0 src/stylesheet/widgets/_buttons.scss:451-469`), while GTK's code decides whether the arrow is
shown (`gtk@4.24.1 gtk/gtkmenubutton.c:623`, `:651-666`), so `adwaita`'s
`menu_indicator` fields hold without a `when` and `button.menu_indicator` states where it is absent; a `when` on
every field restating where the part is drawn would state that fact on each of its eleven fields, and as two facts
each, a `when` being a conjunction while `adwaita`'s part facts draw the arrow on `menu` with `@with_arrow` or with
`@arrow_only`. A measured derivation's
pass under which the part is not drawn still fails: its evidence measured the part drawn. Rejected: failing a field's
fact that applies where its part is not drawn (it adds no check the part's key does not make, and forces that
restatement). It compares every token,
colour-role and input fact the same way, under its `when`. While the units are built, the gate skips a fact whose key the
model does not hold yet (the 0.8.0 plan enables its units one by one); each release is made with no fact of its
enabled units skipped, the gate failing from the plan's M4 on such a fact and on a fact whose key lies in no unit. Where the
fact that applies is pending, the gate compares nothing for that key and combination: it counts it and lists it with
its register id in its report, apart from the failures, and passes it while the units are built, as a skipped key; the
perturbed and accent runs skip it too. That list, the register and `check_ledger.py --final` meet at each release:
it is made with no pending fact of its enabled units (ADD-A122, ADD-A135).

**The perturbed run** (R4's derivation check) repeats this with the stand-in's layer stating, under each scheme, a
fixed colour for every declared input but one whose fact that applies is a derivation (and `kde-breeze`'s `accent`, below), an input with no fact yet included
and for each colour role a derivation fact names as an operand whose own fact is not a derivation, the colours pinned
in the gate's source and documented there, so the run is reproducible; each input it states stands under every
contrast too with its per-scheme value, over the preset's contrast bases and a listed input's folded value (S9, S17),
and a derived input or role, unstated, follows its perturbed operands and is compared (on `kde-breeze` the inactive
input roles and the scheme inputs of the sets with no `[Inactive]` group, S9.1); no preset's accent input having a
derivation fact, the layer states each preset's group whole (S9.2), and a derived accent input fact,
none today, takes a spec row when it first appears, as the stand-in would then state its group in part; on
`kde-breeze` it states no `accent`, though its fact is the literal `#00000000`, so no accent-derivation layer is
derived (S9.2), the preset's no-accent derivations are compared over the perturbed scheme inputs, and `kde_accent` is
the accent run's (ADD-A132); on `material-3` likewise no `accent`, though its fact is the literal baseline `primary`,
so no accent-derivation layer is derived there either and `m3_role` is the accent run's (ADD-A134). It compares only the keys whose fact is a
derivation, evaluated over the same perturbed values in the same scope: a literal fact is the preset's own base
colour, which the perturbation replaces, so comparing it would always fail, while a preset stating a literal where
the platform derives fails here. iOS's facts are `docs/facts/ios/…` like any platform's (R22).

**The accent run** (`kde-breeze`): neither run sets an accent, and the preset states Plasma's no-accent path (S9.1), so
`kde_accent` and `kde_accent_wm`, the model's implementation of `applyScheme()`, are checked by a run of their own.
For each KDE scheme the facts hold (the scheme files the preset's inputs come from, the bundled ports, and the further
`.colors` files the facts pin as sources) and each accent the facts were measured with, the gate resolves `kde-breeze`
with that scheme's inputs in force (the preset's own for its own files; for every other file the palette
`Palette::from_port` converts from it, applied; each under the scheme its facts name, below) and the accent set through `set_accent`, which gives the accent-derivation layer its roles (S9.2; a port's roles left
out under it, S8), and compares every key the pair's facts state with them, the facts recorded from Plasma with
that scheme and accent applied (kind `measured`: `applyScheme()`'s output in kdeglobals, read back as the KDE reader
reads kdeglobals), which hold every accent-dependent role, every inactive input role and the four `wm_*` keyed roles
(at the pins 172 keys per pair, each declared set's twelve keys active and inactive and the four `wm_*` roles, so
the roles no accent changes are compared too; ADD-A145, task T7's reading of the roles compared). Each such fact names, beside
its `when`, the scheme file and the accent it was measured with (fact-level `scheme_file = "<entry> <path>"` and
`accent = "<colour>"`, both or neither, in the `kde` directory only). The
schemes include at least one that tints, one with the accent-coloured title bar option and a `Header` group, one with
that option and no `Header` group, and one that lacks a colour group the others have; the value phase chooses the
files and the accents and records them as sources. Beside the measured accents, the run sets the preset's own
no-accent accent, the literal of its `input.accent` fact that applies under the file's scheme (Breeze's own
`#00000000`, `plasma-workspace@6.8.2 kcms/colors/colorssettings.kcfg:12-15`, which that fact states; the run fails
where none applies or it states no colour literal), on each of the preset's own scheme files and compares the keys
the pairs state, all pairs' together, with the facts that apply without `scheme_file` and `accent`, the preset's
no-accent facts, in the same scope, and on the tinting file (SUSE-Cafe's) with the facts measured with no
`AccentColor` (`accent = "#00000000"`, that literal): so `kde_accent`'s
and `kde_accent_wm`'s no-accent branch, which a stated `#00000000` reaches (S9.2, S9.3), is compared, its tinted
`[Inactive]` groups included (ADD-A132).

- **The scheme a file is applied under** (ADD-A142; ledger queue #104). The facts name it in their `when`: every fact
  with `scheme_file` holds one `scheme:<s>` condition, and every fact of one pair (`scheme_file` and `accent`) the
  same one (at the pins BreezeClassic's `scheme:light` and SUSE-Cafe's `scheme:dark`, `docs/facts/kde/accent.toml`).
  The gate resolves the pair under that scheme, and converts a file that is not the preset's own with it,
  `from_port(<file>, <s>)` (S14: the caller names a port's scheme). The lane records the scheme Plasma's own test gives
  the applied file (S9.3's *The KDE reader's readings*), the one the KDE reader then reports, which each pair's measured
  `role.window.background` lets a verifier check. `check_facts.py` and the gate fail on a fact with `scheme_file` and
  no `scheme:` condition or two, and on a pair whose facts differ in it. Rejected: a fact field `scheme` (a second home for
  what the `when` states, and which the gate's scope already reads); a scheme per file in `sources.toml` (an entry is a
  repository holding several files, and the scheme is the measurement's); Plasma's test run by the gate over the file
  (a second source for what the facts state, while S14 takes a port's scheme from its caller, never from the file).
- **The preset's own scheme files** (ADD-A142). At each scheme, the one `.colors` file that the KDE facts' scheme
  inputs (`input.kde_scheme.*`) whose `when` names `scheme:<s>` cite (a scheme-input fact with no `when`, which cites
  both files, names neither), as `<entry> <path>` (a citation's `source`
  less its line part), compared with a fact's `scheme_file` as text: at the pins `breeze@6.8.2
  colors/BreezeLight.colors` at light and `breeze@6.8.2 colors/BreezeDark.colors` at dark (`docs/facts/kde/inputs.toml`).
  The gate takes them so from the facts, and fails where a scheme has no such file or several, and where a pair names
  an own file under the other scheme. The run resolves an own file over the preset's own scheme inputs, no port, and
  its `#00000000` row on each own file (above) compares with the preset's no-accent facts under that file's scheme.
  Rejected: the two paths written in
  the gate (a second home, which a re-pin of `breeze` leaves stale); every file of the `breeze` entry (BreezeClassic's
  is one and is not the preset's); every file through `from_port`, the preset's own too (it checks the conversion
  instead of the preset's statements; that `from_port` of Breeze's files gives the preset's scheme inputs, lists and
  `token.kde` is a code test of its own).
- **A port's own roles** (ADD-A142). Every accent-run resolution through `set_accent`, `#00000000` included, has the
  accent-derivation layer state its roles and S8 leave the port's out, so a port's own conversion would be compared
  nowhere. So each file that is not the preset's own is also resolved with no accent set (the stand-in stating none,
  the preset's `#00000000` in force, the layer stating nothing), its port's own colour roles, inactive input roles and
  `wm_*` keyed roles showing, and compared with that file's facts measured with no `AccentColor` (`accent =
  "#00000000"`): S14's conversion, its tinting inactive roles from `kde_accent`'s `#00000000` colours included. Every
  non-preset file has such a pair, stated or pending: a pair not measured yet is pending facts under its register row
  (*A pending measurement*), which the run lists with their ids and skips, as it skips any pending fact (BreezeClassic's,
  U698, was such a pair until KDE facts round 7 stated it from run 41158393408's `classic-none` kdeglobals); only a non-preset file with neither stated nor
  pending no-accent facts fails, as a key with no fact (R4).
- **The scheme files read** (ADD-A142). A file that is not the preset's own is read in place from the source cache
  (the 0.8.0 plan's D1; `NATIVE_THEME_SOURCES`, else `scripts/citations.py`'s default, the cache *The evidence root*
  reads), at `<cache>/<entry>/<path>`: the entry's checkout must be at the entry's pinned commit with the file tracked
  and unchanged, which the gate checks itself, as it checks the evidence root (the commit from `sources.toml`, the
  checkout's HEAD and the file's status read through git, no script called; `update_sources.sh --verify --only
  <entry>` checks the same for a person), and it fails otherwise, naming the entry, as it fails without an evidence
  root. A test fixture holds its own files at
  `<fixture>/sources/<entry>/<path>`, which need no checkout and no pin, each written for the fixture, never a copy of a
  pinned file. No scheme file is copied into this repository (SUSE-Cafe's is GPL-2.0, its `sources.toml` entry's
  note). CI's facts-gate jobs fetch, beside the evidence, every entry a KDE fact's `scheme_file` names into a source
  cache the job names by `NATIVE_THEME_SOURCES` (each as `update_sources.sh --only <entry>` fetches it, the list read
  from the facts, so a re-pin needs no workflow edit). The accent run is split by no condition vector: the first shard
  (`NT_FACTS_GATE_SHARD` 1, which records the work outside the vectors) runs it whole and is the job that fetches
  those entries, and the merge job (`NT_FACTS_GATE_MERGE`, `facts-gate-listed` in `ci.yml`), which fetches neither the
  evidence nor the sources, runs no accent run.
  Rejected: the run skipped where the cache lacks a file (a run that compares nothing passes a wrong derivation,
  R4); a copy among the tests (SUSE-Cafe's GPL-2.0 is not this repository's licence, and the pin would have two
  homes); the whole source cache in CI (about 4.4 GB, `update_sources.sh`'s header, for a few files).

**The accent run** (`material-3`, ADD-A134): neither run sets an accent, and the preset states Compose's baseline
scheme (S9.1), so the accent-derivation layer's `m3_role` roles are checked by a run of their own. For each accent
the Material facts name (fact-level `accent = "<colour>"`, alone), under each scheme and each contrast condition the
facts cover, the gate resolves `material-3` with that accent set through `set_accent` and compares every
accent-dependent role (S9.1) with the facts that apply for that accent: the dynamic scheme's roles for that seed as material-color-utilities gives them at its pin (generated, or
published by its own tests), so the layer's statements and the variant, version and contrast level `m3_role` reads
are compared, while `m3_role`'s own rows are its vector table's (S2.2). Until this run is built (the plan's M2.4,
ledger queue #185), a fact naming `accent` outside the `kde` directory, a Material one included, fails the gate, as
`check_facts.py` refuses it, since no run compares it (R4: a fact compared nowhere would pass a wrong value); none
exists, the Material lane recording them with the run (ADD-A145, task T7's reading). Rejected: such a fact listed
and skipped as a pending one is (it states a value, which a skip would leave unchecked with no register row naming
why).

## S18. Documents and scripts

- `docs/property-registry.toml`: stays the checked list of the model's fields (R22), now generated from the
  derive's field registry (S6.1); a test fails when the checked-in file differs from the generated one.
- `docs/inheritance-rules.toml`, `scripts/check_wrong_safety_nets.py`: removed (R20).
- `scripts/check_platform_facts_rows.py`, `scripts/check_preset_citations.py`: read the facts data.
- `scripts/check_spec_trace.py`: new; checks that every gap-map row (the IDs of the map's Appendix A, which
  holds no pointer row, R24), excluding withdrawn rows, has at least one line in the traceability (S20), that every line names a live row, and that each
  line's kind and target agree (a target kind has a target, a verdict has `-` or `- (note)`, and `readers (R18)` may
  name its read). It checks working documents, so
  it is run by hand while they change and is not part of `scripts/check_release.sh`; it is deleted when the
  documents are archived.
- The showcases' element lists and parity gates follow the connectors (R21), a widget a connector draws through a
  stand-in entry from that entry (S21.3).
- `scripts/check_spec_names.py`, `scripts/check_spec_entries.py`: run by hand as `check_spec_trace.py` is; the
  catalogue parser they share, `scripts/spec_catalogue.py`, is also imported by `generate_widgets.py` and
  `check_facts.py` until `docs/property-registry.toml` gives the keys (S17); all deleted when the documents are
  archived.
- `scripts/generate_widgets.py` (S6.1), `scripts/check_facts.py` (the facts' form), `scripts/check_fact_citations.py`
  (S17's quote, absence, evidence and citation rules), `scripts/check_facts_trace.py` (every live trace row of an
  enabled unit in a fact's or a state-model entry's `rows`, or carrying a verdict, S20), `scripts/check_function_vectors.py` (S2.2, S13),
  `scripts/check_sources.py` and `scripts/update_sources.sh` (S17's sources), `scripts/generate_platform_facts.py`
  (`platform-facts.md` from the facts, generated by CI and each release, not committed, S17; ADD-A147),
  `scripts/generate_preset.py` (each preset's rules and its `[pending]` table
  from the facts, S11, S17), `scripts/check_ledger.py` (the register and each pending fact against it, `--final` at
  a release, S17, S21.1; ADD-A146), `scripts/verify_facts.py` (the verifiers' units, briefs and mechanical
  comparisons of state models and facts, and the audit sample), and the one-off converters
  `scripts/import_platform_facts.py` (today's rows as lane input) and `scripts/convert_inheritance_rules.py` (S19.2):
  new, in `scripts/check_release.sh` or not as the 0.8.0 plan's table of scripts states (ADD-A117).
- `scripts/check_connector_parity.py`: rewritten to apply its naming and sibling rules over the new resolved types'
  leaves.

## S19. Migration inside the branch

**S19.1** The presets are rewritten to S11 from the facts; the community presets become palettes (S14): one per
variant the project publishes, their invented light variants and their `icon_set` removed. A variant is a set of
the project's base colours under one name with one of the accents the project publishes for it (R19): Catppuccin's
4 flavours × 14 accents are 56 variants. 0.8.0 bundles the ten schemes 0.7.0 ships (the 0.8.0 plan's D13), each as
the variant whose accent 0.7.0's preset states (`accent_color`: `#1e66f5`, `catppuccin-latte.toml:10`; `#8caaee`,
`#8aadf4` and `#89b4fa`, `catppuccin-frappe.toml`, `catppuccin-macchiato.toml` and `catppuccin-mocha.toml` `:253`,
under `native-theme/src/presets/` at `v0.7.0`; the project's name for each is its palette fact's, S17), so
Catppuccin is four bundled palettes, each with that variant's port (S14). Another accent's variant is another
palette, not bundled: an application sets the accent over the bundled one (`set_accent`, S9.2) or builds that
palette (`Palette::from_toml` with its port, S14) (ADD-A146; rejected: bundling every variant, 56 Catppuccin
palettes with as many ports, where D13 asks for what 0.7.0 has, four). A build test parses and
validates every bundled preset and palette (each palette over every preset it has a source for, Dracula's KDE port,
which lacks two colour groups, among them, S14), so `Theme::from_preset` and `Palette::bundled` never meet their error in a
release (S16). A theme does not check them again (R2.8, S8), so the test also validates each form of the layers
`Theme` derives from bundled data alone (S9.2's accent-derivation layer for each set of schemes at which an accent is
given, with and without the tinting roles; each bundled palette's source over each preset it serves, under each
contrast condition, once palettes are bundled), and asserts that the stack `Theme::from_preset` builds without the
checks equals the stack the validating construction builds from the same text (ADD-A147). The test validates each
bundled preset through a validating construction of its own, which runs every check a theme's load skips, where its
`[pending]` table is empty, and through `from_preset_synthetic` with one synthetic layer per listed path (one per map entry no base states, its
listed fields together, ADD-A133), a listed `default_size` exempt from its check rather than stated, a listed part drawn (S17; ADD-A131) and a listed input's value folded into the preset's input base (S17; ADD-A132), where
it is not; every table is
empty at each release, so it is the validating construction then (ADD-A128, ADD-A147).
**S19.2** Today's inheritance rules (`[uniform]`, `[per_platform]`) become expressions in each preset's bases,
converted by a script from `docs/inheritance-rules.toml` before it is removed, then checked by the gate; the
`[wrong_safety_nets]` are not converted, as the facts replace them.
**S19.3** Today's `AnimatedIcon` and its loaders go (S2.7): the connectors and showcases draw a busy indicator from the
`spinner` widget's parts and `loop`. Today's `Theme::from_toml` and `Theme::from_file` go (S16): the branch's own
callers (examples, tests) state their looks as application layers, loaded with `Layer::from_toml`. The branch's
callers of today's other API move as S16's feature list says: preset pickers to `PresetId` and `PaletteId`,
`from_system_with_preset` to `from_system(Some(generation))`, `icon` and `icon_theme_for` to `ResolvedTheme::icon` and
the resolved `token.icons`, the `detect` scheme and accessibility functions to `Theme::system()`, `ResolutionContext`
to its fields' places in the model, `SystemTheme`'s fields to `Theme`'s getters (the gpui connector's theme name to
`Theme::preset().display_name()`), `pipeline::platform_preset_name` to `PresetId::for_system`, `with_overlay` to
`add_layer` (the iced and gpui showcases and the connectors' READMEs), and `crate::Error`'s theme variants to S1's
error types; the tests of `to_toml` and `lint_toml` go with them.

## S20. Traceability format (R24)

Per platform, `todo_v0.7.1_model-completeness-spec-trace-<platform>.md`: at least one line per live gap-map row,
several where a row needs several targets:

| Row | Target | Kind |
|---|---|---|
| GN-1.29 | `button.body.fill` rules for each state combination the row lists, under variant `flat` | rule |
| … | | |

Kinds: `field`, `rule`, `role`, `token`, `component`, `input`, `reader` (a new read), `placement`, `system-control`,
`condition`, `flag`, and the verdicts, whose target is `-` (or `- (note)` naming the part of the row a verdict
covers when the row's other parts are carried; `readers (R18)` may instead name the read the later reader makes): `out (R1.1)` (the system draws it), `out (R1.2)` (a
library failing R1.2's test), `out (R1.4)` (a Mac Catalyst-only row; a SwiftUI-only control is in, R1.4), `preset (R1.3)` (another toolkit's preset),
`newest (R1.5)` (a look of a release the preset does not describe: an older generation's, or one only macOS or iOS 27 draws, D12), `reference (R1.6)` (a look the preset's chosen reference does not
draw: material-web where Compose is Material's reference), `readers (R18)` (the iOS and Android readers' milestone).

A target `<widget>.<part>.text (leaf by leaf: <style or slot>)` is S2.8's form (*Styles and drawn text*): each leaf
that follows the style a reference to that leaf of the style or slot (`font.size = "= token.text.keyed.heading_1.font.size"`,
`font.family`, `case`, `letter_spacing`, `scaling_role`, …), but a leaf the row restates (`its weight restated`);
and the four drawn-text leaves, `fill`, `elision`, `wrap` and `max_lines`, stated: each a reference to the style's
leaf where the style sets it, otherwise the value the source of what draws the part gives at its pin, otherwise the
platform's widget default there, and a register row's id where none of them gives it. The row names a drawn-text
leaf it states itself (`elision End`, `fill at reduced alpha`) and cites the sources of the others, or, where many
rows share them, the trace's header gives them once and every row written so takes them from there (`kde-breeze`'s
*Text rows*; ADD-A130).

## S21. Release and compatibility (R21)

**S21.1** Released in steps (the 0.8.0 plan's D13, D14; ADD-A135, ledger queue #168): 0.8.0, on `v0.8.0-rc1`, holds
the units of its scope, everything 0.7.0's model holds (the plan's *0.8.0's scope*); then follow-up releases, each on
its own `v<version>-rc1` branch, its number by SemVer against the previous release (a breaking one the next minor),
each enabling further units, until the catalogue's last. At every release every platform preset, `ios-26` included,
states every field the model then holds, under every combination of the names its enabled units hold, and declares
every variant, size and flavour its platform has that the model's types can spell, a variant of a unit not enabled
under `later`, and the keyed flags of the enabled units (S10; ADD-A147); the release passes the same gates over its
enabled units: the facts
gate with no fact of those units skipped or pending (S17), `check_ledger.py --final` over them (S17's pending facts,
the register), every `[pending]` table empty (S17, S19.1), each connector's contract test with no `pending` entry
(S21.3). The last follow-up release also passes the facts gate with no fact skipped and `check_facts_trace.py` over
every trace line. Rejected: one release holding every unit (the plan's D13 (A)); releases by capability (D13 (C)).
**S21.2** The model's enums are exhaustive (S1), so a connector maps each in full, a new member breaking its build,
which before 1.0 is the check that it maps it (R21): every enum a layer states, a selector names or the query and
the resolution answer with, and every enum of today's API that stays but those named next (`IconRole`, `IconSet`
and `watch::ThemeChangeEvent` among them), which lose their `#[non_exhaustive]`. The error, status and diagnostic
enums have `#[non_exhaustive]` (ADD-A146):
`LayerError`, `ProblemKind`, `ThemeError`, `ReaderFailure`, `PortError` and `crate::Error`; `ReaderStatus` and
`PaletteStatus`; `VersionMatch` and `DiagnosticEntry`, which keep theirs. No connector maps one of these: an
application reports it or matches the members it handles, beside a wildcard arm, so a new validation problem or
failure breaks no build and its release is no breaking one by the 0.8.0 plan's D14; the crate's own refusal tests
match them in full, the attribute not reaching inside the crate. Rejected: every public enum exhaustive, the error
enums included, the rule as it stood (R21's reason is the connector's mapping, which these enums have none of, and
under D14 each member added to one, a new `ProblemKind` with a later unit's check, would make that follow-up
release a breaking one). Every public
struct has it, except the two groups S1 names: the closed value structs, and the inputs their caller fills in full
(`WindowConditions`, `RootInputs`, `SizeClasses`, `Sibling`, `PlacementInput`, `SystemAppearance`, `ReaderState`,
`fonts::FaceTraits`, and the one the motion runtime takes from a connector, `MotionUpdate`, S2.7; ADD-A146;
not `Drawn`, which only `Motion::sample` makes and no connector builds, so it keeps the attribute), which are exhaustive for the same reason as the enums (R21). `FaceTraits` (ADD-A134) is the
face a caller of `select_face` describes, every field an operand of CSS's matching (`families`, `width`, `style`,
`weight`), built as a struct literal (`connectors/native-theme-egui/src/fonts.rs:231`, `native-theme/src/fonts.rs:213`);
rejected: `#[non_exhaustive]` with `FaceTraits::new(families, width, style, weight)` (S1's form for a struct with no
neutral default takes every such field, so a field added later breaks the constructor's callers just as it breaks a
literal: the same break with an extra function, and no field has a default a caller could leave to it).

**S21.3 The connector contract (R23).** Each connector keeps a contract table (today's contract tables, extended):
every resolved field it receives, with the toolkit lines that draw it, or the reason the toolkit cannot and what it
draws instead; the element tree it builds for the query (S8); the window conditions it supplies and how it reads
them; and its colour hand-over (S2.1, ADD-A128): which of S2.1's three colour types its toolkit takes, read from the
toolkit's pinned source, and in the third case the limit and its size. egui's `Color32` is premultiplied
(the first case, as the egui connector records, `connectors/native-theme-egui/src/convert.rs:158-159`); iced's
`Color` and gpui's `Hsla` are float types, whose case (whether the renderer takes them unclamped and premultiplies
them itself) each connector states when it ports to `Color` (the 0.8.0 plan's M2.1), the toolkits' sources not being
in the facts' source cache. The table also holds what the connector supplies (ADD-A146), each entry supplied, with
the toolkit lines it is read from, or listed with the reason the toolkit cannot give it: every `StateFlag`, and
whether it reports their order (`state_order`, S7.2); every content-variant pair of the catalogue whose variant an
enabled unit holds (S8; ADD-A147); every
`ElementData` and `RootInputs` field, and the font metrics (`Element.metrics`, S8); the `Presence` members it
reports (S2.7); and one row per keyed component a bundled preset declares, drawn, its parts and values
mapped as a typed widget's are, or not drawn, with the reason. A flag or a datum a connector never supplies turns
off every rule that selects on it, with no build error: a connector builds flags and never matches on them, so the
exhaustive enum does not catch it, and a keyed component, role or text style is no Rust field the generator's list
of new fields reaches. A connector test fails when a resolved field, a flag, a content-variant pair, a data or root
field, or a declared keyed component of an enabled unit is neither mapped nor listed (rejected: these left to the
description of the element tree, prose no test reads). The connectors' milestones apply it
(R21). While the units are built, a table may hold `pending` entries, resolved fields the connector does not map yet, which
the test accepts; from the connectors' port to the model (the 0.8.0 plan's M2.1) a commit that adds a resolved field
adds it to every connector's table, mapped or `pending` (the generator lists the new fields), and each release is made
with none (ADD-A118, ADD-A135).

**A stand-in entry** (ADD-A135; ledger queue #169; the 0.8.0 plan's *Widgets 0.7.0 styles through stand-ins*). Until
a widget's unit is enabled, a connector that 0.7.0 styles the widget for (a menu bar, a number input, a code editor,
a group box, a loading placeholder, a chart, a drag image's border, gpui's description list) keeps that mapping, from
the model's enabled roles and widgets, as 0.7.0 maps it from its own fields. Its contract table records it as a
stand-in entry: the widget (the catalogue's entry, or none for a widget no catalogue entry names: gpui's description
list), the resolved fields it reads, and the unit that replaces it (none where the widget has no entry: the entry
stays). The contract test accepts it and fails one whose
widget's unit is enabled; the unit's connector task replaces it with the widget's own mapping, so a release enabling
that unit is made with no stand-in entry for it. The showcases' element lists draw such a widget from its stand-in
entry (S18). Rejected: the widgets dropped until their units (each loses what 0.7.0 shows); `pending` entries for them
(a `pending` entry is a resolved field not mapped yet, and these are mappings of a widget the model does not hold);
their units in 0.8.0 (the plan rejects it, against D13's timing).

**A deferred entry** (ADD-A147). For each enabled entry the contract table lists every state the connector reports,
every keyed flag it sets, every host context it builds and every condition it supplies that a unit of depth not yet
enabled holds for that entry, and every construct of its toolkit (a variant, a size, a content form) that only such a
name describes, with what it draws meanwhile (the look at depth, or its 0.7.0 mapping from the values at depth) and
the unit that states it. The contract test fails a table that lacks one against `scripts/widget_units.toml`, and one
that keeps an entry whose unit is enabled. A part's `transitions` are such an entry until the motion unit.

**A widget a preset declares unavailable** (ADD-A147; the 0.8.0 plan's D6, outcome 6). Where a bundled preset
declares an enabled widget `available = false` (S10) and the connector's toolkit has such a widget, the contract
table lists, for that preset, the entry the connector draws the toolkit's widget from: the widget the catalogue's
*Available* line names as the platform's control (`bottom_tab_bar` for `tab` on `ios-*`, `group_box` for `card` on
`macos-*`, a `list` row for `expander` on `material-3` and `ios-*`), as a stand-in entry while that widget's unit is
not enabled and by its own mapping once it is; or, where the line names none (`status_bar` on `adwaita`,
`windows-11`, `ios-*` and `material-3`, `card` on `ios-*`, where the catalogue names two surfaces and no one
control, and `card` on `kde-breeze` under its default flavour
`widgets`, the only one in force until the flavours unit), the toolkit's own geometry with every colour and font from the theme's
typed roles (S3, S4.4), never a colour or font of the toolkit's own. The contract test fails a table that lacks a
row for a pair of a bundled preset and an enabled widget it declares unavailable whose toolkit widget the connector
draws. A stand-in widget whose unit is enabled is under the same rule. The declarations stay as the platforms are,
and the query keeps answering `NotAvailable` (S8). Rejected: `bottom_tab_bar` and `group_box` brought into 0.8.0
(two units against the plan's D13, and the rule still missing where the catalogue names no control); each connector
deciding alone (two
would decide differently, against following the theme's data).

**A toolkit field whose role is absent** (ADD-A147; D6, decided by logic, awaiting the maintainer's veto: veto list
item 56). Where a connector maps a typed role to a toolkit field that cannot be left empty and a bundled preset
leaves the role absent because the platform has nothing to pair it with (S3's *A labelled mapping*: `material-3`'s
warning, success and info), the contract table lists, for that preset, the field as an exception holding the
toolkit's own colour, as it lists a widget a preset declares unavailable (above). The contract test fails a table
that lacks the exception for a pair of a bundled preset and a toolkit field that cannot be left empty whose role the
preset leaves absent.
